stories.title: Akhilesh to show Congress its ground reality:To hand over report on 387 seats to Rahul Gandhi; Congress candidates saved their deposits in only 12 seats
stories.summary: The Congress and the SP are set to contest the UP Assembly elections together. A demand for 200 seats has been put forward by the Congress. To put the Congress in its place, the SP has prepared a report. This report pertains to the 2022 Assembly elections. Back then, the Congress fielded 399 candidates in the state. It received a total of 21.51 lakh votes, which accounts for just 2.33%. The party managed to save its deposit on only 12 seats. On 387 seats, Congress candidates forfeited their deposits. According to a source connected to the SP, a total of 73 seats have been mentioned in this report. These seats have been categorised into 4 groups. The Congress secured more than 5,000 votes in only these 73 seats. The Congress finished in second place on just 4 seats. Leaders such as the then state president Ajay Kumar Lallu and former UP state president Ajay Rai also finished in third place. Read the report… Out of 73 seats, SP candidates won 14—will they give up their claim? The report prepared by the SP regarding the Congress also explains the dynamics of these 73 seats. Among these, SP candidates won 14 seats in the 2022 Assembly elections. Two of these candidates have currently parted ways with the party and joined the BJP camp. The SP will face the challenge of denying tickets to its sitting MLAs. This means the SP is unlikely to hand these seats over to the Congress. Two of these seats belong to Rae Bareli and Amethi, where its MLAs have switched sides to the BJP. The SP might make some compromises on these specific seats. In the list handed over to the SP by the Congress, claims have been made on all 15 seats across the Rae Bareli, Amethi, and Saharanpur districts. It has been stated that the Congress will not back down from its claim on these seats at any cost. The Congress put up a fight on only 6 seats. In the 2022 Assembly elections, the Congress managed to show a contest on just 6 seats. Among these, Aradhana Mishra 'Mona' won from Rampur Khas, and Virendra Chaudhary won from the Pharenda Assembly seat in Maharajganj district. Currently, Aradhana Mishra 'Mona' is the Congress UP State President. Meanwhile, Virendra Chaudhary is the leader of the Congress Legislature Party. In Rampur Khas, Congress candidate Mona received 50% of the votes, and in Pharenda, the Congress candidate secured 40% of the votes. Both winning candidates polled over 84,000 votes. In both places, BJP candidates finished in second position. Where Congress came second, it could only offer a tough contest in Jagdishpur The data compiled by the SP indicates that the Congress was in second place on only 4 seats in the 2022 Assembly elections. Even among these, it was able to offer a close contest on the Jagdishpur seat alone. On the remaining seats, the margin of victory was very large. On the Mathura seat, the BJP candidate received over 1.58 lakh votes. The Congress finished in second place here, but its candidate managed to get only around 49,000 votes. This meant the Congress candidate lost this seat by a margin of over one lakh votes. Similarly, the BJP candidate won the Kheragarh seat by a margin of 36,000 votes. The Congress, coming second here, received around 60,000 votes. On the Kidwai Nagar seat as well, there was a margin of 38,000 votes between the BJP and the Congress. Here, the Congress candidate received over 76,000 votes. In Jagdishpur, the BJP candidate received only 13,000 more votes compared to the Congress candidate, which meant there was a tough contest there. Lok Sabha elections also saw Congress leading in only 39 seats The SP has also compiled data on the performance of the Congress in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. At that time, the Congress contested 17 seats and won 6. These 17 Lok Sabha constituencies encompass 85 Assembly seats. The Congress managed to take a lead in only 39 of these Assembly seats. Even among these, more than 12 seats are currently held by the SP. The SP claims that the lead on these seats was secured by the Congress due to the SP's vote bank. Based on the performance in the 2022 Assembly elections and the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the SP has asked the Congress for a reasonable demand regarding the number of seats. Experts say—If the alliance breaks, Congress will suffer greater loss Senior journalist Rajendra Kumar says—Congress is demanding more seats in the UP elections, but there appears to be no solid reasoning behind it. The Congress cannot take sole credit for its victory in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Figures indicate that the SP's performance was far superior to that of the Congress. While the Congress won 6 out of the 17 seats it contested, the SP won 37 out of 62 seats. The SP's tally increased from 5 to 37 seats. This clearly shows that the SP's strike rate in the election was significantly better than that of the Congress. According to Rajendra Kumar, the organisation of the Congress in UP is very weak. Even in the 6 seats won by the Congress, the SP's strong cadre and ground presence played a major role. An example of this is the Allahabad (Prayagraj) seat. Ujjwal Raman Singh, who won on a Congress ticket from here, was previously with the SP. His father, Reoti Raman Singh, has also been a prominent SP leader. Rajendra Kumar states that even in the Assembly elections, Akhilesh Yadav is aware of which seats have a Congress vote bank and where the party lacks a strong organisation or leader. In such a scenario, demanding more seats without understanding the ground reality could prove harmful to the alliance. He believes that if disputes over seats escalate and the SP–Congress alliance breaks, the Congress will suffer the maximum loss. Now, let us examine the seat-wise performance of the Congress in the 2022 elections—

stories.title: 'Obsession with cleanliness' claims student's life:Death note mentions constant fear of something bad happening; what is OCD?
stories.summary: You must have often heard people say that someone has a ‘cleaning disorder’ or that someone keeps repeating the same task over and over again. Two days ago, Ritu Sharma from Prayagraj died by suicide because of this very condition. Her suicide note read: I keep repeating the same thing over and over again. If I don't do it, my mind scares me by telling me that something bad will happen. I am tired now, so I am ending my life. Ritu had been selected for MBBS and was allotted a government medical college in Sonbhadra. What exactly is this ‘cleaning disorder’ that drove a promising student to take her own life? Question 1: What does Ritu's suicide note reveal? Answer: Experts say the symptoms mentioned in the suicide note point towards Ritu suffering from ‘high-functioning OCD’ or ‘Pure O’. In such cases, academically gifted students may appear calm and perform exceptionally well in their studies from the outside. Senior Consultant Psychiatrist Dr Krishna Mishra says, OCD is not just a disorder involving repeatedly washing hands, cleaning or keeping things organised. These are only its outward manifestations. Sometimes, instead of repeating an action, a person keeps struggling with thoughts in their mind, as happened with Ritu. Ritu used to remain locked in her room studying day and night. During this time, she was also struggling with frightening and unwanted thoughts that kept entering her mind. When thoughts of failing an examination or something bad happening repeatedly occur, a person may repeat the same action again and again to calm the anxiety caused by them. Ritu wrote in her suicide note: I may have already studied a subject thoroughly. But my mind forces me to study the same thing again. It scares me that if I do not repeat it over and over again, I might make a mistake in the examination or fail. When I repeat things again and again as my mind tells me to, I feel relieved for a while. After some time, the same thoughts and doubts return. Even though I want to, I am unable to break free from this. I feel helpless, weak and lacking in confidence. I feel that I have fallen behind others and may not be able to achieve my goals in life. This makes it clear that Ritu's mind had become trapped in an unending loop of thoughts. She knew very well that the thoughts entering her mind were false. Yet, she could not control herself. This is because the disorder creates such intense anxiety and fear that logic takes a back seat. A person feels that if they do not repeat an action, something bad will happen. According to Dr Krishna Mishra, preparation for a difficult examination like NEET, the pressure of becoming a doctor and studying alone, away from her family, together worsened Ritu's condition. Her OCD symptoms became so severe and intense that she could no longer see a way out. Question 2: What causes this disorder? Can career pressure trigger OCD? Answer: Just as the body produces less of the hormone insulin in diabetes, OCD involves changes in the brain's structure and an imbalance in its chemicals. Dr Krishna Mishra explains that different parts of our brain use certain chemicals to send messages to one another. These are called neurotransmitters. In OCD, the balance of chemicals that regulate mood (serotonin) and those involved in detecting errors (dopamine and glutamate) gets disturbed. In most cases, OCD develops gradually. Initial signs may appear at the age of 10–12 or during adolescence (20–22 years of age). Ritu wrote in her suicide note that her OCD symptoms began when she was in Class 11 or 12. She mistook them for normal overthinking and anxiety. However, a few weeks ago, she found out on the internet that her symptoms resembled OCD. Sometimes, children may also suddenly develop severe OCD symptoms overnight after suffering from a throat infection. This is medically known as PANDAS. In this condition, the body's immune system mistakenly attacks the part of the brain (basal ganglia/striatum) that filters our thoughts and calms fear. As a result, that part stops functioning properly. Dr Krishna Mishra says that mental illnesses, including OCD, are genetic. If a person's first-degree relative (such as a parent or biological sibling) has OCD, the risk of developing the condition increases by up to four to five times. Question 3: What are the ways to overcome this disorder? Answer: OCD can be completely treated with medical guidance, modern therapies and medication. However, OCD cannot be detected through a blood test, X-ray or MRI scan. According to Senior Consultant Psychiatrist Dr Krishna Mishra, a patient's symptoms are assessed in accordance with international medical guidelines. Doctors check whether unwanted thoughts and compulsive actions take up more than one hour a day and whether they affect the person's personal or professional life. Dr Krishna Mishra says that the best treatment for OCD is CBT and ERP therapy. This is a way of retraining the brain without medication. Through therapy, patients are taught that frightening thoughts entering their minds are only ‘thoughts’ and do not represent a real danger. In addition, medicines called SSRIs (Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors) are prescribed. They increase serotonin levels in the brain and help restore its balance. This significantly reduces unwanted thoughts and the intense anxiety associated with them. It also makes it easier for patients to undergo therapy. However, it is important to remember that OCD is not a condition that gets cured immediately. Medication may take six to eight weeks to show an effect. In severe cases, treatment may take six months to two years or even longer. In some cases, OCD can return due to factors such as excessive stress, major life changes or suddenly stopping medication. Question 4: Apart from OCD, are there other mental health conditions that silently affect a person's life? Answer: Yes, there are several such mental health conditions that are often dismissed as personality traits or mood changes, but they continue to affect a person from within… GAD (Generalised Anxiety Disorder): Constantly worrying excessively about every small or big issue without any specific reason. High-functioning depression (Dysthymia): A person continues to carry out everyday activities, such as working or studying, normally on the outside but constantly feels empty, exhausted and sad within. PTSD (Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder): Constantly living with memories of a past trauma, such as an accident or the loss of a loved one. Social Anxiety Disorder: Feeling scared or anxious about meeting people, talking to them or being in a crowd. Anxiety: Excessive worry about real-life concerns such as career, health, examinations and money. Free-floating anxiety: The mind constantly imagines that something bad will happen. For example, if someone has stepped out of the house, the person becomes convinced that they will definitely meet with an accident. This is a prominent symptom of GAD (Generalised Anxiety Disorder) or OCD. Depression: This is a complex form of sadness. Sadness is caused by an unpleasant event and usually gets better within a few days. A person may also experience moments of happiness in between. However, depression can occur without any apparent reason and lasts continuously for more than two weeks. A person is unable to enjoy even the activities they once liked. ADHD (Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder): The brain is unable to focus on a single task for a long time. A person often forgets where they have kept their keys, puts off work until the last minute, makes decisions without thinking and finds it difficult to sit still in one place. This can affect performance at school and in the workplace. Question 5: How can you recognise if someone is going through a mental health problem? Answer: Symptoms of mental illness do not always appear in the form of madness or shouting loudly. Sometimes, a person may appear completely normal, successful and cheerful from the outside, while fighting an internal battle. Some signs that may be visible in such a person include… Dr Krishna Mishra says that if a person has always been quiet by nature, preferring to stay alone may be normal. However, if someone who was once cheerful starts withdrawing from people and stops meeting friends, it could be a major sign of depression or severe anxiety. The pressure of examinations and careers can push mental stress to extreme levels. Our society does not teach people how to deal with failure, rejection or low marks. When someone fails an examination, they may feel that their entire identity and life have come to an end. Being excessively absorbed in studies can also be a sign of mental stress or OCD. A child may force themselves to study because of unwanted, frightening thoughts, anxiety or the fear of failure. This is exactly what happened in Ritu's case. If someone in the family talks about having disturbing thoughts, do not dismiss it as attention-seeking behaviour or something trivial. Listen calmly and try to understand what they are saying. They can also be encouraged to seek help from a professional (psychiatrist or psychologist). If someone refuses to talk about their problem, do not pressure them or try to spy on them. Tell them, ‘Whenever you feel comfortable, you can talk to me.’ If they still do not open up, ask a relative or friend they are close to to speak with them. Question 6: What should a person do if they have suicidal thoughts? What role should family and friends play? Answer: Sometimes, a person may talk about suicide to express their helplessness or despair. However, this should never be ignored. Instead of scolding them or calling them weak, cowardly or timid, their words should be taken seriously. Senior Consultant Psychiatrist Dr Krishna Mishra says that people should be encouraged to talk openly about suicidal thoughts. When a distressed person is asked openly and empathetically, ‘Are you having thoughts of harming yourself?’, it can bring them relief. They feel that someone understands their suffering. If someone is having frequent thoughts of taking their own life, they should not be left alone even for a moment. Just as a patient suffering a heart attack is immediately taken to the emergency ward, a person having suicidal thoughts should also be taken to a psychiatrist or clinical psychologist immediately. Anyone going through a mental health problem can seek help from the Government of India and several organisations. These services are available free of charge, 24 hours a day… Tele-MANAS Helpline: The Government of India's helpline provides free mental health support and counselling 24 hours a day. People can call 14416 or 1800-891-4416. The service is available in several languages. KIRAN Helpline: Mental health support is also available through the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment's helpline at 1800-599-0019. Immediate emergency assistance: If there is an immediate and direct threat to someone's life, call the national emergency number 112 immediately.

stories.title: Terror threat to Ayodhya, Kashi Mathura on Diwali:Bombings planned for 20 days, note reads, 'Protect Your Schoolchildren'
stories.summary: A threat has been issued to carry out bomb blasts in Ayodhya, Varanasi and Mathura in Uttar Pradesh during Diwali. An email from someone named Slater Johnson was received on the official email ID of the Ayodhya court at 12:25 p.m. on Wednesday. It said, "8 November will be a dark Diwali. Ayodhya, Varanasi and Mathura will say 'Khalistan-Khalistan Zindabad'. Blasts will take place from 8 November and continue until 27 November." The email mentioned pro-Khalistan slogans and the names of some organisations. It also threatened to blow up schools in Varanasi and said that people should save their children. The threat also mentioned targeting religious sites in Mathura. Ayodhya CJM seeks security from SSP In view of the seriousness of the threat, Ayodhya Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM) Piyush Tripathi wrote to the SSP. He has sought the immediate strengthening of security at the court complex. Police have increased checking and surveillance at all entry gates of the court complex. Action is also being taken to have the premises inspected by the bomb disposal squad and identify the person who sent the email. The court complex has been targeted by threats and bomb blasts several times in the past. Demand to strengthen security until 27 November CJM Piyush Tripathi has ordered the deployment of adequate police personnel, thorough checks at the entry and exit gates, searches of suspicious persons and objects, and regular inspections by bomb disposal and dog squads. It has also been requested that effective surveillance be maintained through CCTV cameras, the functionality of security equipment be ensured, and the source and sender of the email be identified before legal action is taken. The authorities have also been asked to arrange additional security forces and patrolling with heightened vigilance from 8 to 27 November. Security beefed up at the court After receiving information about the threat, Ayodhya Nagar Kotwali police and Cantonment police reached the court on Wednesday afternoon and checked all the entry gates. The premises were also searched. The metal detectors and other equipment were inspected to determine whether they were functioning properly. The personnel present there were instructed to remain alert at all times. They were told not to allow anyone to enter the court without being checked. City CO Shri Yash Tripathi said, "Security at the court premises will be tightened further on Thursday. Surveillance is being stepped up through several technological means. Efforts are under way to find out who sent the email and from where." Five terrorists were killed near the makeshift Ram temple in 2005 On 5 July 2005, five Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists arrived to attack the makeshift Ram temple. As the terrorists tried to fire a rocket launcher, security forces surrounded and killed all five. Acharya Satyendra Das, who was then the chief priest of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi temple, had said that Lord Ram's child idol was housed in a tent on the day of the incident. Devotees used to come there for darshan at the time. However, on 5 July 2005, some terrorists launched an attack. As soon as the terrorists fired a launcher, there was a loud explosion there. Following this, all the personnel deployed for security became alert. Everyone said that the terrorists had arrived. The CRPF personnel then went on high alert. The terrorists broke through the barricading and reached behind Sita Rasoi. Their aim was to destroy the place where Lord Ram was enshrined. However, the security forces killed the terrorists at the scene. Bombs Found Outside Hanumangarhi and at Railway Station On 28 March 1999, a highly powerful time bomb was found at Ayodhya railway station. It emerged that if it had exploded, the entire station premises would have been destroyed. An accident was averted because a tea vendor remained alert. The bomb was defused after he informed the authorities. On 13 June 2001, a cooker bomb was found in a jeep parked under a tamarind tree outside Hanumangarhi. There was a conspiracy to terrorise the entire area. The Lashkar-e-Taiba emerged as the group behind the incident. Lashkar area commander was killed in Ayodhya Lashkar area commander Mohammad Imran was killed on the Ayodhya bypass in September 2001. Two other associates of Mohammad Imran were also arrested. In addition, incidents such as the Sabarmati bomb blast and the Faizabad court blast took place. However, over time, security in Ayodhya has become several times better and more vigilant than before.

stories.title: Container overturns onto car, killing husband, wife, mother and driver:Bodies recovered by cutting open car in Dehradun; police rescue 6-year-old child alive
stories.summary: A lawyer from Saharanpur died in a road accident in Dehradun. His mother, wife and driver also died in the accident, while his six-year-old son was seriously injured. Lawyer Vishesh Kapoor, 38, left home in a car with his family on Wednesday evening. His car had reached the Mohabbewala area of Dehradun when a speeding container truck rammed into it. The container then overturned onto the car after going out of control. Police reached the spot after receiving information about the accident. With the help of a crane, they removed the container from on top of the car. The police called out from outside, but there was no movement inside the car. They thought all five occupants had died. Meanwhile, the police saw movement inside the car. They then heard a child crying. The police personnel slowly removed parts of the car and pulled the child out. He was admitted to Coronation Hospital in a critical condition, where he is undergoing treatment. The police then called for a cutter, cut through the car's body and pulled out the four bodies. See 3 pictures... Now, read the full details Vishesh Kapoor, a resident of Gokul Enclave Colony on GPO Road in the Kotwali Sadar Bazar area of Saharanpur, was a sales tax lawyer. He had his office on Court Road. He was the elder of two brothers. His younger brother, Deepesh Kapoor, lives in Dehradun and is a builder. Vishesh's family lived in Mission Compound in 2004. Around four years ago, the family moved to their new house in Gokul Enclave. At around 4 p.m. on Wednesday, Vishwesh left home with his mother Kiran, wife Nisha and six-year-old son Maher. The family was going to meet Deepesh's pregnant wife, who lives in Dehradun. They had hired a driver for the journey. Neeraj was driving the car. The family was soon expecting more good news. They had set out hoping to check on Deepesh's pregnant wife and meet the new member of the family. However, an accident on the way turned their happiness into mourning. Police said: Driver did not apply the brakes CO Sadar Ankit Kandari said a road accident took place at Mohabbewala Chowk at 3:30 p.m. A family travelling from Saharanpur to Dehradun was in an i20 vehicle that was hit by a container truck. When the seriously injured people were taken to Coronation Hospital, the driver, mother, son and daughter-in-law died there. A six-year-old child survived and is in stable condition.

stories.title: Mother, daughter made to sit on car bonnet:Three men flee after crowd surrounds them during money recovery attempt in Mathura
stories.summary: In Mathura, young men drove a car at high speed for around 2 kilometres with a mother and daughter seated on its bonnet. CCTV footage of the incident, which took place on Tuesday night, emerged today. The footage shows the mother and daughter clinging to the car's bonnet. Police have arrested two boys named Prem and Puneet in connection with the case. The charge of attempted murder has also been added to the case. The incident took place in the Jamunapar police station area. Three youths had reached the house over a money dispute Pawan, the son of Sheila, the woman who was hanging from the car's bonnet, said, "Three youths arrived at our house in a Swift Dzire car while under the influence of alcohol. Prem and Puneet were among them, along with another youth. All three abused and assaulted us after reaching the house." The dispute was over money spent on an old case. Both sides had been fighting the case together. The three youths had come to demand payment for the money spent on the case. They drove away with the mother and daughter on the bonnet after being surrounded by a crowd Pawan said, "Hearing the noise, around 100 people from the neighbourhood gathered at the spot. They surrounded the car. The three youths then began driving away at high speed. During this, my mother, Sushila Devi, and my sister ended up on the car's bonnet." Despite this, the youths drove the car for around 2 kilometres. They then left my mother and sister near a petrol pump on Mant Road and fled. Woman said - They were asking for money, now they are threatening me Sheila said that a man named Prem had come to her house in a car. He was asking us for money. He threatened us when we did not pay. I have injuries to my chest, hands, legs and back. My body is aching, and I have also suffered bleeding. Police add attempted murder charge, two arrested Police began an investigation after CCTV footage of the incident emerged. Sadar Circle Officer Varun Mishra said the two sides had a dispute over money spent in a case. One side had gone to the other's house to demand payment. The CO said that a case had been registered on the victim's complaint. Based on the investigation, the section relating to attempted murder was added to the case. Police have arrested the accused, Prem and Puneet. Further action is being taken against them.

stories.title: Consumer forum's woman member dies after car overturns:She was driving when her car collided with another vehicle in Firozabad; she was a resident of Agra
stories.summary: A woman member of the District Consumer Commission died after her car overturned following a collision with another vehicle in Firozabad on Wednesday morning. She was driving from Agra to her office when the accident took place. Her car hit another vehicle from behind and overturned on the road. She suffered serious head injuries and died on the spot. According to information, the accident happened around 10:15 am in the Makkhanpur police station area. After receiving information from local residents, police reached the spot and called a crane to remove the damaged car. The family was also informed about the incident. The deceased was identified as Sonam Chaturvedi, 45, a resident of Taj Nagari Phase-1 in Agra. She had been a nominated member of the Firozabad District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission since 2022. The commission was earlier known as the District Consumer Forum. Sonam's husband, Vaibhav Raghavan, works in property dealing. They have a son, Shauryash, who studies in Class 10 in Agra. Driver of the other car flees Sonam was travelling in her Swift Dzire when she reached the Makkhanpur area. The driver of an Hyundai Accent car travelling ahead suddenly applied the brakes. Sonam lost control of her car and hit the vehicle from behind. The impact was so strong that her car overturned on the road. Makkhanpur police station in-charge Chaman Kumar Sharma reached the spot with a team and inspected the scene. Police moved both damaged cars to the roadside. The driver of the Accent car fled after the accident. Police are searching for him. Shikohabad Circle Officer Jaibind Gupta also reached the spot and inspected the scene.

stories.title: Office of professor who called SP spokesperson 'Gawar Ahir' demolished:Cow dung smeared on house walls, effigy burnt in Lucknow, photo trampled
stories.summary: A Delhi University professor's office was vandalised on Wednesday after he made insulting remarks against Samajwadi Party (SP) spokesperson Manoj Kaka during a TV debate. In Lucknow, protesters burnt the professor's effigy and trampled his picture underfoot. Professor Sangeet Kumar Ragi's office was vandalised in Delhi. Some people broke the office gate, smeared cow dung on the walls and gate, entered the office and scattered his belongings. The incident came a day after Ragi and SP spokesperson Manoj Kaka had a heated argument during a debate on a news channel on Tuesday. During the argument, Ragi used insulting words against Kaka, calling him "obscene", "uncouth" and an "Ahir". Kaka also called the professor a "donkey". Meanwhile, in Lucknow, protesters burnt Ragi's effigy and trampled his picture underfoot. Later, Ragi posted a clarification on X and apologised. He said, “Manoj Kaka abused me first. I used these words in response. My comment was not directed at the entire community, but at people who abuse others.” See two pictures below : Now find out what happened in the debate A heated argument took place between Professor Sangeet Ragi and Samajwadi Party spokesperson Manoj Kaka during a television debate on Tuesday. At the beginning of the debate, Sangeet Ragi called Manoj Kaka the "party's ridiculous Ahir". Manoj Kaka replied, "We call such magicians, who show insensitivity over corpses, uncouth." Ragi then called Manoj Kaka "uncouth", a "donkey" and the "son of a pig". He said, "Donkeys cannot speak. Donkeys engage in servitude. A donkey cannot say a single word." Manoj Kaka said, "The donkeys who sing praises of this country's government. We do not [belong to] any caste... we know how to respect every caste." He went on to make his point by referring to the Ahir community and Akhilesh Yadav. In response, Sangeet Ragi said, "Your language is that of a street dog. Donkeys like you... your language is that of a street dog." After videos of the debate emerged, a controversy began over Ragi's remarks. He faced particular opposition on social media over his use of the word "Ahir". Sangeet Ragi apologises after debate After the TV debate, Sangeet Ragi posted on the social media platform X at 7:37 p.m. In the post, he clarified his comment and apologised. He wrote that during the debate on ABP News, Samajwadi Party spokesperson Manoj Kaka had addressed him using abusive language. This was not the first time; Manoj Kaka had made personal remarks against him several times, using words such as 'behooda' and 'gadha'. Ragi wrote, "Today, when he used this word, I responded by saying that we use the words 'ganwar' and 'raad' for people like that. The word 'Ahir' was used alongside them. This was not directed at the entire community, but at abusers like him." He further wrote, "Some people may have been hurt by this, so I apologise. That was not my intention." Demand to suspend Sangeet Ragi, memorandum submitted to Vice-Chancellor Some people reached Delhi University on Wednesday. They raised slogans against Sangeet Ragi. They threw cow dung at the walls of his office. They broke the gate and scattered belongings. Some people also submitted a memorandum addressed to the Vice-Chancellor of Delhi University, demanding that Prof. Sangeet Ragi be suspended immediately and disciplinary action be taken against him. Protest against Sangeet Ragi also held at Lucknow University Activists of the Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha staged a protest against Professor Sangeet Ragi at Gate No. 3 of Lucknow University on Wednesday. During the protest, the activists burnt his effigy and trampled on his photograph. Immediately after the effigy was burnt, police personnel present at the spot took it away. The student organisation's activists demanded strict action against Professor Sangeet Ragi. Here are two pictures from the protest 'The comment was made about the Yadav community' Aditya Pandey, who was protesting at Lucknow University, said, "Sangeet Ragi has made a casteist remark against the Samajwadi Party's respected spokesperson. The remark was directed at the Yadav community. This is not an insult to an individual but an affront to the entire community." "We will not tolerate Samajwadi Party leader Manoj Kaka or the casteist remark made against him under any circumstances. Such an offensive remark is the result of a person's narrow-mindedness and mental bankruptcy." Now know who Manoj Kaka is Manoj Singh Kaka is the national spokesperson of the Samajwadi Party. His real name is Manoj Singh Yadav. He is a native of Mahura village in Uttar Pradesh's Chandauli district. His family comes from a farming background. He completed a BCom at UP College in Varanasi. He then studied for an LLB, LLM, MBA and MPhil at Lucknow University. He was also a gold medallist at Lucknow University. Manoj Kaka began his political journey through student politics. In 2010, he was appointed the Samajwadi Party's national secretary. In 2013, he became the party's state vice-president. He currently represents the Samajwadi Party in television debates as its national spokesperson. Now know who Sangeet Ragi is Professor Sangeet Kumar Ragi is a professor in the Department of Political Science at the University of Delhi. He is also a political analyst. He has also served as the head of the department. He teaches subjects related to Indian politics, public administration and Indian political thought. Sangeet Ragi is also known as a thinker associated with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS). He often shares his views on political and ideological issues during television debates and on news channels.

stories.title: Two Lucknow sisters found buried in snow at Kedartal:One was an influencer, the other a graphic designer; both had trekked to Nepal
stories.summary: Six of the eight people who went missing after being caught in an avalanche and snowfall on the Kedartal trek in Uttarkashi have died so far. Three more bodies were recovered during the search operation on Wednesday morning. They included trekking sisters Vartika Verma and Deepika Verma, residents of Gayatripuram in Lucknow. Both Vartika and Deepika were passionate about trekking in the mountains. The sisters had completed several treks in India and Nepal, but this journey to Kedartal became the toughest test of their lives. Their brother Atul Verma had travelled to Uttarkashi with family members in search of the two. The family learnt about the accident not from the trekking agency, but after seeing a report on social media. Read Vartika and Deepika's full story... They loved the mountains and had completed several treks Vartika and Deepika were passionate about trekking. The sisters had trekked at several locations in India and Nepal. They had returned from a trip to the Valley of Flowers and Hemkund Sahib around two months earlier. A year earlier, the sisters had also trekked to Kedarkantha in the Mori area of Uttarkashi with their brother Atul and friends. Despite being familiar with mountain trails and having completed several treks before, the conditions at Kedartal proved extremely challenging. Vartika is a freelance influencer, while Deepika worked as a graphics designer at a private company. Kedartal trek began on 27 October On 27 October, Vartika and Deepika set out from Gangotri for Kedartal with seven trekkers and five support staff members. Everyone was scheduled to return on 29 October after the three-day trek. However, an avalanche occurred along the route because the weather deteriorated and heavy snowfall began. This blocked the way back, leaving eight members of the group stranded. On 30 October, some members of the group informed the trekking agency that they were stranded near Kachchi Dhang and sought help. A rescue operation was launched after this. On 31 October, four members of the support team were safely evacuated. Brother learned about the accident through social media According to Atul Verma, the trekking agency did not inform the family about the accident. After seeing the news on social media, he travelled to Uttarkashi with his relatives. The family has also raised questions about the trekking agency's role. They allege that the trek was conducted despite the bad weather and that they were not informed in time even after the accident.

stories.title: Man dies by suicide in married girlfriend’s room:Brother-in-law locks door, he hangs himself fearing he would be caught in Kanpur
stories.summary: A 25-year-old man died by suicide at his married girlfriend's house in Kanpur late on Tuesday night. He had gone there to meet her and was sitting in a room when her brother-in-law became suspicious that someone was inside. The brother-in-law bolted the room from outside and called other family members. A commotion broke out in the house. Fearing that he would be caught in front of the family and face embarrassment, the young man died by suicide. The family informed the police, who reached the spot and got the room opened. The man's body was found inside. He was identified as Shiv Pratap Singh, alias Saurav, 25, a resident of Mohan Kheda in Fatehpur. The incident took place in the Ghatampur police station area of Kanpur. Read the full story below : The two became friends on Facebook According to the police, Shiv Pratap Singh (25), also known as Saurav, became friends with Pooja, a resident of Rawaipur, through Facebook. The two had been talking for the past three years. Their closeness gradually grew. Pooja is married. Her husband, Ashutosh Sonkar, is a revenue inspector with the Lalitpur Municipal Council. They have two children. Late on Tuesday night, Shiv Pratap reached Pooja's house to meet her. He parked his bike outside the village and went inside the house. Pooja made him sit in one room and went to another room, saying that she would put the child to sleep. Meanwhile, Pooja's brother-in-law, Paritosh, got up to drink water and suspected that a young man was inside the room. He locked the room's latch from outside and called the other family members. Paritosh and Pooja then began arguing. Hearing the noise, the rest of the family also reached the spot. Young man found hanging from a sari noose inside After the commotion at the house, the family members informed the police. When the police reached the spot and had the room opened, they found Shiv Pratap's body hanging from a sari noose inside. The police had the body brought down and sent it for a post-mortem examination. As news of the incident spread, a crowd gathered in the village. Father says son had gone to meet his girlfriend Shiv Pratap's father, Surajbhan Singh, said his son had gone to meet his girlfriend. He said that on Wednesday morning, Nauranga outpost in-charge Ravi called him, informed him about the incident and asked him to reach the post-mortem house. The father has demanded a fair investigation into the matter. Ghatampur Inspector Manoj Singh Bhadauria said the young man's body had been sent for a post-mortem. He added that further action would be taken after receiving a written complaint.

stories.title: See pictures of education minister Sandeep Singh’s bride-to-be:He will marry Meghna from Aligarh; their love story began at school
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Education Minister Sandeep Singh's engagement has been finalised. The ring ceremony will be held in Aligarh on 14 November. Invitations are also being distributed in political circles. As soon as the engagement invitation surfaced, people began discussing who the girl who is set to become the minister's bride is. Dainik Bhaskar looked into the matter and uncovered a film-like love story. Here is how a romance that began during their school days is now heading towards the wedding altar... Love story began at Aligarh's DPS Sandeep Singh's fiancée is Meghna Chaudhary. They first met while studying at Delhi Public School (DPS) in Aligarh. Sandeep was a senior at the school, while Meghna was his junior. Sandeep passed Class 12 in 2012 and left the school, but their acquaintance from their school days gradually turned into love. Meghna went abroad to study law. The distance between them grew, but they did not lose touch. They remained connected through phone calls and messages. Things went sour in 2024, then they convinced their families In 2024, Sandeep Singh's family learnt about the relationship. After this, Sandeep's family travelled to Ghaziabad to meet Meghna's family. Everything was going smoothly, and the family was fully prepared to finalise the relationship there. However, the matter fell through because one of the family members opposed it. But Sandeep Singh did not give up. He continued trying to persuade his family. Eventually, his efforts paid off and both families agreed to the marriage. Who is Meghna Chaudhary and what does her family do? When Bhaskar's team reached Tarapur in Gonda block of the Iglas Assembly constituency in Aligarh, Meghna's ancestral village, they met her grandfather, Radheshyam, and grandmother, Savitri Devi. Meghna's family has been living in Lajpat Nagar, Ghaziabad, for the past 15 years. Her father, Vijay Chaudhary, is a contractor and runs a footwear business. He also has a footwear shop in Ghaziabad. Meghna's mother's name is Vijaya Chaudhary. She also has a younger brother named Karan Chaudhary. Meghna's father is the eldest of three brothers; his two younger brothers are named Rakesh and Ajay. When the Dainik Bhaskar team showed Meghna's photograph to her grandmother, Savitri Devi, her face lit up with happiness. She said, "This is my granddaughter. Her marriage has been fixed with the minister." Both brothers' engagements to be held at the same mandap According to the engagement cards that have surfaced, the celebrations are set to double. Alongside Basic Education Minister of State Sandeep Singh, his younger brother Saurabh Singh's ring ceremony is also set to be held at the same time. A grand engagement ceremony for both brothers will be held at a ground near Sant Fidelis School in Talanagri, Aligarh. The wedding date has not yet been finalised. However, it has been learnt that the wedding will take place in Delhi. For now, the family is busy distributing the engagement invitations and making preparations for the function.

stories.title: Husband kills wife, locks house flees:Tells father-in-law, 'I have killed your daughter, come take her body'
stories.summary: In Barabanki, a husband strangled his wife to death at midnight on Tuesday. After the murder, he called his father-in-law and informed him that he had killed his daughter and that her body was lying in the room. He then locked the house and fled. About seven hours after the murder, the father reached his daughter's in-laws' home. The police were called, and when they broke open the lock, they found the woman's body lying inside the room. The woman was reportedly having an affair with a man who often visited the house when her husband was away. She had once eloped with him. This had led to frequent arguments between the husband and wife. The incident took place in Rasulpur locality under Nagar Kotwali, near the district headquarters in the city. See two visuals Now understand the entire case Sandeep, a resident of Rasulpur locality, had a court marriage with Seema (30) 10 years ago. They have an eight-year-old daughter. The daughter lived at the house of her grandmother, Sunita, next door. Sandeep's father married Sunita after his first wife died. Sandeep was their only son after three daughters. He had two auto-rickshaws operated by others. He himself drove someone else's car. His mother, Sunita, said, "My son married Seema in a court marriage of his own choice. We had distanced ourselves from Sandeep because he and Seema frequently quarrelled. In Sandeep's absence, his wife's lover used to visit the house. This often led to arguments between the husband and wife." Daughter-in-law's conduct was not proper According to the mother, her daughter-in-law's conduct was not proper. She had eloped with her lover a few days earlier. However, she returned after 10 days. Sandeep had been continuously opposing her. Father said – he told me, 'Do not contact me' Seema's father, Dharmesh, said, "Our house is in Safdarganj, around 18 km from the city. At around 12 a.m. on Tuesday night, Sandeep called us. He said there had been an argument. Later, he said, 'I have killed her. Her body is lying in the middle room of the house. Take her body away. I am leaving. Do not contact me.' He then locked the house and left." When Dharmesh reached the house around seven hours later, he found it locked from outside. After this, Brijesh, the husband of the ward councillor, informed Dial 112. Police reached the spot, broke open the lock and entered the house, where they found Seema's body. On receiving the information, ASP Vivek Tiwari and City CO Aftab Alam also reached the scene. They recorded statements from the family members. The forensic team also examined the scene. ASP Vivek Tiwari said: “The husband committed the murder. He told his father-in-law this himself. He is being searched for. The forensic team has conducted an investigation.”

stories.title: Thar runs over 5 people at 100 kmph:Two cousins killed, 3 critically injured as SUV hits 3 motorcycles in Amroha
stories.summary: A speeding Thar SUV ran over five people travelling on three motorcycles in Amroha on Tuesday night. Two cousins died, while three others sustained critical injuries. The accident took place around 9.30 pm in the Naugawan Sadat police station area, about 12 km from the district headquarters. According to the police, the Thar was travelling at around 100 kmph when it hit the motorcyclists. The impact was so severe that the riders were thrown into the air and landed nearly 10 feet away. The front of the SUV was also damaged. Hearing their screams, passers-by rushed to the spot, while the driver abandoned the vehicle and fled. Police rushed to the scene after receiving information and took the injured to hospital. Doctors declared two of them dead on arrival. Following the accident, the victims’ relatives created a commotion at the hospital for nearly two hours, demanding the immediate arrest of the Thar driver. The deceased were identified as Prashant, 21, and Rajeev, 22, both residents of Amroha. Prashant was the son of Rajeev’s paternal uncle. The three injured men have not yet been identified. Thar hits three motorcycles in succession Prashant’s family lives in the Dak Bungalow area of Peergarh, while Rajeev’s family resides in Jai Om Nagar. The two cousins had travelled to Naugawan Sadat on the same motorcycle on Tuesday. While they were returning home that night, a speeding Thar hit their motorcycle on Bijnor Road. The SUV then collided with two other motorcycles in succession. Two young men were riding the second motorcycle, while one person was on the third. Relatives block transfer of bodies for two hours After receiving information about the accident, police reached the spot and took the two youths to a Community Health Centre (CHC). They also informed their families, who rushed to the hospital. The relatives became agitated when police tried to send the bodies to the mortuary for post-mortem examinations. They refused to allow the bodies to be moved for nearly two hours, demanding the arrest of the Thar driver. They also staged a protest at the hospital. Police later pacified the family members after holding discussions with them. Police tracing occupants of seized Thar City CO Dr Pradeep Kumar said, “The police have taken the Thar into custody. The vehicle’s number plate showed that it is registered in Asmoli, in Sambhal district. The occupants fled the scene and have not yet been traced. We are gathering information about how many people were in the car at the time of the accident and where they live.”

stories.title: Kangana Ranaut says SP only promoted gun violence in UP:PM transformed Kashi; says, 'We will explore the city and go shopping'
stories.summary: BJP MP Kangana Ranaut from Himachal Pradesh's Mandi constituency arrived in Varanasi on Wednesday and responded to Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav's statement about starting a metro service in the city. Speaking to the media at the airport, Kangana praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi's work in Varanasi. She said, "PM Modi is investing lakhs and crores of rupees in Varanasi. He has transformed Kashi." Taking a dig at Akhilesh Yadav and his father Mulayam Singh Yadav, she said, "What did they do when they were in power? There was only gunfire in the city during their government. Uttar Pradesh is now progressing day by day, and the whole world is watching it." Says she will explore Kashi and go shopping Kangana said she had come to Varanasi for some work. She added that every time she visits Kashi, she feels excited to explore the city. "I will visit different places here, enjoy my time and go shopping in Kashi," she said. Before this, Bollywood actress Kangana Ranaut had also visited Kashi 11 months ago. She paid obeisance at the Baba Vishwanath and Kaal Bhairav temples. She then walked through Kashi's narrow lanes. She shopped at the stores and also bought a Shiva lingam. She ate chaat at Deena Chaat Bhandar and had tea in a kulhad.

stories.title: Drug smuggler's girlfriend arrested with ₹1.50 crore 'charas':Ran illegal trade from tea stall in Kanpur while boyfriend was in jail
stories.summary: A woman was arrested in Kanpur with hashish worth ₹1.50 crore on Wednesday. She had been running the drug trade since her boyfriend was sent to jail. She was selling hashish and cannabis from a tea stall to hide her illegal business. Acting on a tip-off, the Bajaria police and Crime Branch teams jointly raided the spot at around 11 pm on Tuesday. During the raid, they recovered around 3 kg of hashish from the woman. The case falls under the Bajaria police station area. Check out the visuals below : Started living with boyfriend after husband's death The accused, Shabnam Begum, also known as Chacha, is a resident of Kंघी Mohal. She was married to Rais Ahmed, who died around a year ago. After his death, Shabnam became friends with Riaz Khatola, a resident of Chamanganj. Riaz ran a tea shop in Chamanganj, which Shabnam often visited. Over time, the two started living together and began running the shop jointly. Police alleged that they used the tea shop as a front to sell charas and ganja. About a month ago, Riaz allegedly shot Shahzad Alam near Barfkhana Mosque. Police arrested him in the case and sent him to jail. After his arrest, Shabnam took over the drug business and continued running it on her own. Hashish found in a bag kept at the shop The police had been receiving information for a long time about the trafficking of narcotics. Acting on this information, the Crime Branch and Bajaria police teams raided Shabnam's tea shop. During the search, three kilograms of hashish was recovered from a bag kept at the shop. ACP Sisamau Anand Ojha said that Shabnam was being questioned. Information was also being gathered about other people involved with her in the business.

stories.title: SP Youth Brigade files complaint against Dhirendra Shastri:Demands FIR over insult to Lord Krishna in Lucknow
stories.summary: Workers of the Samajwadi Party's Mulayam Singh Youth Brigade staged a protest against preacher Dhirendra Shastri in Lucknow on Wednesday. They reached the Hazratganj police station, submitted a complaint against him and demanded that an FIR be registered. The workers alleged that Shastri had made a controversial statement about Lord Krishna, which hurt the religious sentiments of crores of devotees. Demand for FIR registration Pravesh Yadav, state secretary of the Mulayam Singh Youth Brigade, submitted a written complaint against Dhirendra Shastri and demanded strict action. He alleged that Shastri had made objectionable remarks about Lord Krishna's tribhanga posture, name and way of playing the flute. He also accused Shastri of comparing Lord Krishna with Lord Ram and using inappropriate language. Lord Ram and Lord Krishna have their own importance Pravesh Yadav said Lord Krishna's personality should not be mocked or compared with anyone. He said Lord Krishna represents love, compassion, justice, good values, courage and the protection of dharma. He added that Lord Ram and Lord Krishna are both highly respected in Sanatan Dharma, and each has their own importance, divine stories and teachings. Yadav said it was wrong to insult one deity to praise another. The workers demanded that the police take the matter seriously, register an FIR and start legal action against Dhirendra Shastri.

stories.title: Shankaracharya hits back at Amit Shah's Angad remark:Says his foot stood firm due to truth and dharma, not ego
stories.summary: Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati has hit back at Union Home Minister Amit Shah's statement about Angad's foot. He said Angad's foot remained firm not because of power or ego, but because of the strength of Lord Shri Ram's truth, dharma and justice. He said using stories from religious scriptures for political gain means ignoring their true meaning. The Shankaracharya said Angad had made it clear in Ravana's court that his foot remained firmly planted because of the values of dharma, truth and justice followed by Maryada Purushottam Shri Ram. He added that changing the meaning of religious stories to suit one's needs was not a sign of respect for dharma. Questions Yogi government's comparison with Ram Rajya Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand also criticised Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's government. He said a government facing allegations of pulling the topknots of young religious students, attacking saints and allowing the slaughter of millions of cows could not be compared with Ram Rajya. Makes statement before leaving Kashi for Gujarat The Shankaracharya made these remarks during his discourse before leaving Kashi for Gujarat. Referring to the episode of Angad, he said it was important to understand the original message and context of religious stories and symbols before interpreting them.

stories.title: Varanasi's AQI rises to 132, city enters yellow zone:Bhelupur records highest pollution level
stories.summary: Wednesday morning began with light mist in Varanasi. The temperature was recorded at 26°C, with wind speeds of 6 kmph and humidity at 60%. According to meteorologist Manoj Srivastava, dry weather is likely to continue in Varanasi and nearby areas for the next week. There is no chance of rain during this period. The cold is expected to increase in the morning and evening, while the weather will remain normal during the day. Meanwhile, the city's air quality has also started getting worse. Varanasi, which was in the green zone until Tuesday, entered the yellow zone on Wednesday with an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 132. Bhelupur recorded the highest pollution level in the city, with an AQI of 169. The morning began with light fog in the city. PM2.5 level reaches 348 in Bhelupur Bhelupur recorded a PM2.5 level of 348 and a PM10 level of 404 micrograms per cubic metre. Maldahiya recorded an AQI of 139, with PM2.5 at 167 and PM10 at 301 micrograms per cubic metre. Meanwhile, air quality in the BHU area remained in the green zone. Pollution levels in Ardali Bazar could not be recorded as the monitoring machine was faulty. Vehicle traffic and fog adding to pollution According to experts, the rising number of vehicles and morning fog are making the pollution worse in the city. Fog is preventing polluted particles from rising into the atmosphere, leading to a higher concentration of pollutants in the air. Professor GN Srivastava, former head of the Department of Chest and TB at BHU, has advised asthma patients to take precautions. He said they should wear a mask before stepping out of their homes.

stories.title: Akhilesh targets Dhirendra Shastri:Says he should be barred from UP over remarks on Ram and Krishna; SP seeks FIR
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav has targeted Dhirendra Krishna Shastri over his remarks about Lord Krishna and Lord Ram. Writing on social media on Wednesday without naming him, he said, "He has hurt the sentiments of both the Yaduvanshis and the Raghuvanshis. He will now be allowed to enter neither Braj nor Awadh." Akhilesh's statement is significant because Dhirendra Shastri's next religious discourse is scheduled to be held in Kunda, Pratapgarh, from 17 to 20 November. Raja Bhaiya is organising the event. Two videos of Dhirendra Shastri have gone viral, in which he appears to compare Lord Ram with Lord Krishna. In one of them, the head priest of Bageshwar Dham is heard saying, "Just look at a single photograph of your Thakurji. Even when he is standing, he is bent at three points. One foot over the other, sometimes swaying his waist, and playing the flute with his neck tilted." First, read what Akhilesh wrote on 'X'- Akhilesh wrote: "Now, neither a true Raghuwanshi nor a true Yaduvanshi will welcome them. A sign announcing their blockade should be put up at the Uttar Pradesh-Madhya Pradesh border, stating: 'Entry to the religious land of Uttar Pradesh is prohibited for those who commit blasphemy.'" Those who have not abandoned religion will not refrain from taking potshots at communities next time. There is no need to explain whose turn is next. The Nepal border will also have to be closed; otherwise, coming here from there will be more convenient. It appears that in Uttar Pradesh, someone is attempting to challenge a person's political-religious authority at the behest of an outsider. Why are political figures bringing God into their internal conflict?

stories.title: Husband shoots wife dead in Shahjahanpur:Called police himself; confessed he killed her over repeated arguments
stories.summary: “My wife would quarrel with me and repeatedly go to her parents’ home. I was fed up, so I killed her.” These were the words of 25-year-old Shivam Verma of Shahjahanpur, who allegedly shot dead his 22-year-old wife, Reshma, on Tuesday (3 Nov). The couple had married after a love relationship three years ago. Around two hours before the murder, Shivam persuaded Reshma to leave her parents’ home and return with him. However, soon after they reached home, the couple began arguing. During the altercation, Shivam allegedly opened fire with a country-made pistol. The bullet struck Reshma in the jaw, killing her on the spot. Shivam then called an ambulance and the police, saying, “Come and take my wife’s body.” He reportedly sat in front of her body for around 20 minutes. Police arrested him and sent him to jail. The incident took place in the Nigohee police station area, around 25 km from the district headquarters. Wife had been staying with her parents for two months Shivam Verma is a resident of Trilokpuri village, while his in-laws’ home in Chaudhera village, where his wife Reshma had been staying, is around 5 km away. His family includes his mother, Munni Devi, father, Shishupal, brother, Vipin, and sister, Nisha. The family is engaged in farming, while Shivam operated a combine harvester used for harvesting paddy. Brought wife home on pretext of collecting clothes before shooting her According to Shivam, disputes had continued between the couple since their marriage, and Reshma had been staying at her parents’ home for the past two months. Shivam had returned to his village from Sultanpur on Monday. The following morning, he went to his in-laws’ house and asked Reshma to accompany him home for five minutes to collect her clothes. Reshma took the clothes out of the cupboard and placed them on the bed. She then started returning to her parents’ home. Shivam asked her to maintain some distance from her family, leading to an argument. As the dispute escalated, he allegedly shot her. 'I had decided that I would kill her if we fought again' When the police arrived at the scene after the incident, Shivam did not try to flee. The clothes taken out of the wardrobe were still lying on the bed. During questioning, Shivam said he had already decided that he would kill his wife if they had another argument. Sister said - He broke my sister's hand, then shot her Reshma's younger sister Priya said that her brother-in-law's mother, sister and brother used to harass her elder sister together. Twenty days earlier, her elder sister had quarrelled with her brother-in-law over dowry. After that, she returned to her parents' home. On Tuesday morning, brother-in-law Shivam came to the house. He tried to persuade Reshma at length and asked her to return with him. Reshma then agreed to go to her in-laws' house. The two left on a motorcycle at 11:30 a.m. As soon as they reached the house, Reshma was assaulted, breaking her arm. She was then shot. Priya said that when people living nearby informed the family about the assault, the family members went there. The in-laws then bolted the door from inside. When the door was opened after the police arrived, Reshma's body was found inside. "My brother-in-law tried to assault me too" Priya said, "My sister's mother-in-law, sister-in-law and brother-in-law would harass her together. Her in-laws had demanded dowry. The family fulfilled their demands, but despite this, Shivam continued to assault my sister. "Once, Shivam came to my house carrying a country-made pistol to assault me. My family members saved me then, but they took my sister's life. We demand that he be killed in a police encounter." Mother said, ‘The brute killed my daughter’ After seeing Reshma's body, her mother Archana began crying and thrashing about on the road. She kept saying, "This brute has murdered my daughter." Reshma's two brothers, Raju and Rajiv, also clung to their mother and wept. Circle Officer Sadar Shubham Verma said: “After a dispute with his wife, the husband carried out the crime. He has confessed to it. He was arrested and sent to jail.”

stories.title: ‘Boycott SP’ banners target Akhilesh in Lucknow:Maurya community protests over Swami Prasad issue; questions PDA politics
stories.summary: Banners carrying messages such as ‘Boycott Akhilesh Yadav’ and ‘Boycott Samajwadi Party’ have appeared at several locations in Lucknow, reflecting growing opposition to Samajwadi Party national president Akhilesh Yadav among sections of the backward communities. The protest stems from Akhilesh Yadav’s alleged remarks about Swami Prasad Maurya and objectionable comments reportedly made by Samajwadi Party workers. Members of the Maurya, Shakya, Saini and Kushwaha communities have questioned the party’s PDA politics, raising concerns over respect and political representation. Questions raised over the PDA slogan and the dignity of backward communities The protesters have questioned Akhilesh Yadav's politics of PDA (Backward Classes, Dalits and minorities). They say that the Samajwadi Party speaks of respect for the Backward Classes and social justice, but its stance in the case of Swami Prasad Maurya appears different. Through the banners, they have asked whether the PDA slogan is limited to electoral politics or whether the party also gives equal respect to leaders from the Backward Classes. Solidarity rally in support of Maurya raises issue of political participation Those protesting say the issue is not limited to Swami Prasad Maurya but is linked to the dignity and political participation of the entire backward community. They allege that the Samajwadi Party leadership did not take an effective stance against offensive remarks made against community leaders. Expressing this anger, members of the Maurya, Shakya, Saini and Kushwaha communities put up banners to register their protest. Through the banners, questions have been raised about the Samajwadi Party's policies and the PDA slogan. Linking the issue to the dignity of the backward community, the protesters expressed their anger against the Samajwadi Party.

stories.title: Akhilesh calls himself Gen Z during Kashi visit:Says Dalmandi would have been spared injustice with a metro; links jail terms to donation fraud
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, who arrived in Varanasi on a one-day visit, launched a scathing attack on the BJP government. He targeted the government over the demolition drive in Kashi's Dalmandi and the Ram temple donation embezzlement case. Showing pictures of Dalmandi, he said the BJP had demolished 181 houses and more than 500 shops. If the government had brought in a Metro project, it would not have had to commit this injustice against Dalmandi. Akhilesh also questioned the clean chit given to Champat Rai by the Sant Committee in the Ram temple donation embezzlement case. He said, "When will God give a clean chit? The government formed an SIT and sent employees to jail. This makes it clear that the donations were embezzled." Describing himself as a member of Gen Z, Akhilesh Yadav said, "I am still Gen Z." During his visit, he went to the home of the party's late leader Rajesh Yadav Natthu and paid tribute to him. After this, he went to the residence of former district president Satish Fauji. He was welcomed at several places. During a press conference in Sundarpur, he targeted the BJP. They then reached the residence of Ashfaq Ahmed W, the former assembly candidate from Shehar North, to offer condolences on the death of his brother. In the Kotwali area, they also visited the home of party worker Lalu Yadav. They then left for Lucknow. If there had been a metro, there would have been no need to run a bulldozer in Dalmandi Questioning the demolition drive in Dalmandi, Akhilesh Yadav said the BJP had demolished 181 houses and more than 500 shops. He said, "Could this be happening anywhere on earth? If the metro had been built, you would not have had to commit this injustice against Dalmandi." He alleged that people in Dalmandi were first made to fight among themselves, after which targeted action was taken. Referring to the High Court's order, Akhilesh said that the government was not even following it. A ₹5 lakh fine was imposed on the DM, and a lawyer charging ₹50 lakh had to be engaged in the Supreme Court to challenge it. On Ram temple donation theft: When will God give a clean chit? Akhilesh Yadav questioned the clean chit given to Champat Rai by the saints' committee in the case involving the alleged theft of donations for the Ram temple. He said, "When will the Almighty give a clean chit? It is certain that the donations were stolen. That is why they formed an SIT and then formed another SIT over it." He said he had nothing to do with any individual's name. The question was that the offerings made to Lord Shri Ram had been stolen. This was a very serious matter. How many devotees must have come to make offerings with faith and devotion? Akhilesh said the government had formed an SIT in the case and employees had been sent to jail. When the government took action and sent people to jail, what kind of clean chit was that? The Almighty alone would decide the matter.

stories.title: Woman bank employee arrested for ₹10 crore fraud at PNB:CBI also arrests her friend; used officials' logins in Noida
stories.summary: The CBI arrested two people on Tuesday in connection with the disappearance of ₹10.24 crore from accounts at Punjab National Bank in Greater Noida. The accused include the bank’s female office assistant, Deepanshi, and her associate, Ashutosh Kumar Pathak. The two allegedly colluded to withdraw money from customers’ accounts without their permission and misappropriate the funds. The CBI arrested Ashutosh in Pune, Maharashtra. The location where Deepanshi was arrested has not yet been confirmed. According to the CBI, Ashutosh Pathak was produced before a court in Pune after his arrest on Tuesday. The court granted him transit remand. Both accused are being questioned as investigators examine the transactions and probe the possible involvement of other suspects. Funds transferred from customers’ accounts without authorisation Deepanshi allegedly conspired with Ashutosh and other unidentified people to withdraw crores of rupees from bank accounts and transfer the money elsewhere. Debit transactions were carried out without the account holders’ authorisation or the bank’s approval. Following a complaint, the CBI registered a case on 29 October and launched an investigation. Both Deepanshi and Ashutosh have since been arrested as part of the probe. Mobile numbers and email addresses of account holders whose money was withdrawn were also changed CBI probes possible involvement of other suspects In its press release, the CBI said the investigation is still underway. The case alleges that the bank’s female office assistant colluded with a private individual and other unidentified people. Investigators will question both accused to establish which accounts received the money withdrawn from customers’ accounts and identify anyone else involved in the alleged fraud. The probe will also examine the bank’s internal transactions, unauthorised debit entries and the transfer of funds. How the case came to light Transporter Vineet Bhati, a resident of Aichhar village, visited Punjab National Bank’s branch in Sector Pi-1 on Tuesday. He runs a firm called Jai Shiv Transport and holds a current account at the branch. Bhati said he had approached bank employees to invest in a mutual fund. “At the branch manager’s request, I signed the cheque and the relevant brochure. “However, instead of being transferred to my savings account, the fund amount of ₹25 lakh was sent to another account. That account was also shown as being in the name of Vineet Bhati, but it did not belong to me,” he said. He subsequently lodged a complaint at Beta-2 police station, seeking an investigation into the role of bank employees and the return of ₹25 lakh. Meanwhile, five or six other account holders present at the branch began protesting. It was then discovered that money had also gone missing from several other accounts. Now, hear from those whose accounts were emptied... ₹1.29 crore received as compensation, more than ₹1 crore missing Brijesh said, "My mother's land was acquired for the Noida airport. She received compensation of around ₹1.29 crore in her account in return." The family withdrew only ₹15 lakh from it. Now more than ₹1 crore is missing from her account. The balance is showing as zero. They used to ask for KYC in the name of withdrawing money Elderly man Dharmveer said, "I had ₹17.5 lakh. The bank had not allowed me to make any entries for two years. They defrauded me extensively. Sometimes they closed the account, sometimes they said there was a problem with my PAN card. At other times, they asked me to complete Aadhaar KYC." "I came to the bank yesterday. The manager showed me that there was nothing in the account. My grandmother also has an account in the same bank. It has ₹61 lakh in it, but I do not know whether that money is still there. I also have an FD of ₹2.25 lakh." Bank account emptied: What should be done now? Elderly woman Santosh, who was sitting outside the bank with her sister, said, "I had received ₹1 crore 29 lakh. My sister had received the same amount as compensation." We had withdrawn some money from it, but the rest remained. Now ₹1 crore 18 lakh of our money is missing. It is showing a zero balance. The bank officials are not telling us anything either. When we ask them, they say, "We have only recently joined." My house is being built, and my children are living in rented accommodation. My daughter was ill. When my husband retired, he received ₹32 lakh, which was spent on her treatment. My daughter also died. Now we do not have a single penny left. We have been completely ruined. Bank officer said, "I will lose my job; do not come here again." Santosh's sister Saroj said, "We had received ₹1.29 crore in compensation. Of this, we withdrew ₹10 lakh in cash and had ₹20 lakh transferred. When we asked to withdraw more money from the bank, the madam said, 'There will not be that much available; get it arranged.' When we came later, she said, 'If you need a large amount, inform us two days in advance. We will be able to provide it then.'" Funds missing from several account holders' accounts Shrichand said, "We had a fixed deposit of ₹1.16 crore in the bank. This money was embezzled. Several account holders in Biraunḍi Chakrasenpur and nearby areas were similarly defrauded." Two fixed deposits belonging to a person named Kartari were misappropriated by ₹9.87 lakh and ₹6.89 lakh, while ₹10.34 lakh was misappropriated from Amichand's fixed deposit. More than ₹1 crore went missing from Vijaypal's account, more than ₹1 crore from Subhash's account and around ₹1.18 crore from Santosh's account. ₹88 lakh was misappropriated from Bijendra Singh's account and ₹25 lakh from his fixed deposit, while around ₹90.43 lakh was misappropriated from Ranpal's account. Around ₹40 lakh is missing from Hanif Khan's account, around ₹1.07 crore from Sonu's account, and ₹23 lakh and ₹80 lakh from Jagdish's and Sunita's fixed deposits, respectively.

stories.title: Dogs drag newborn's body from Banda hospital:Father finds only limbs; 3 guards face termination
stories.summary: "The doctors had handed the baby over to us. I nodded off at around 3 a.m. In that short time, the dogs dragged the baby away. The baby was between two women." "When we woke up and searched, we found only the hands and legs. The dogs had torn apart and eaten the entire body. This has happened to us today; tomorrow, it will happen to someone else. This must be improved." This was said by Ganesh Prasad Kushwaha of Banda, whose newborn baby's body was dragged away by dogs at around 3 a.m. on Sunday (1 November). Meanwhile, on Tuesday, questioning the arrangements at the medical college, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav wrote, "When there is no one to care for the living, what can be expected for the dead? Is the Ministry of Health on 'sick leave'?" The Dainik Bhaskar team spoke to the child's family to understand the full matter. Read the report... Three years ago, their daughter died Ganesh Prasad Kushwaha (38) lives with his wife, Gudiya (35), in Barokhar Buzurg village, under the Girwan police station area. Ganesh works as a confectioner. Ganesh said, "We had a daughter five years ago, but she died three years ago. My wife Gudiya was pregnant again." Wife gave birth in the ambulance Ganesh said that Gudia developed stomach pain at around 10 p.m. on Saturday (31 October), so they called an ambulance. They were on their way to the hospital for the delivery, but Gudia gave birth to a son inside the ambulance near Tindwara. The baby was stillborn. They immediately reached the medical college. In the emergency department, Dr Sushil admitted Gudia. After some time, she was shifted to the labour room. Family sat with the body for three hours At around 12.30 a.m., hospital staff handed over the body of the deceased newborn to us. My sister-in-law Meera, daughter-in-law Usha and nephew Chandra Prakash were also with me. As it was late at night, we stayed in the hall of the OT (operation theatre) block. We sat there with the baby's body for a long time. Body placed between two women At around 3 a.m., my nephew and I fell asleep while sitting in chairs. My sister-in-law and daughter-in-law lay down with the baby's body between them. We woke up after half an hour and the baby was missing. We started looking around frantically and found both of the baby's hands lying nearby. Both legs were visible around 40 metres away. We could not find the rest of the body or the face anywhere. This is negligence on the part of the hospital administration. If this has happened to us today, it will happen to someone else tomorrow. This must be rectified. On Monday morning, we immersed the baby's body parts in the Ken River without telling anyone. Nephew said - We dozed off because of exhaustion Ganesh's nephew Chandra Prakash said, "As soon as we reached the hospital, my aunt was admitted. At the place where deliveries take place, we were not allowed to stay even for a minute and were immediately sent outside. We came outside and lay down there." We dozed off because of exhaustion. When we woke up half an hour later, the child's body was missing. Only two arms and two legs were lying there. There were four or five dogs there. The guards' arrangements are very poor. When we were looking for the child, two guards arrived. Instead, they started blaming us, saying, "Were you people asleep?" Akhilesh wrote - The Health Department is on sick leave Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav has also targeted the government over the matter. He wrote on Twitter, "When there is no one in the BJP rule to care for the living, what can be expected for the dead?" Those coming to Bareilly for the rally should also visit neighbouring Shahjahanpur, where they had once gone to lay the foundation stone. They should see how the entire state of Uttar Pradesh is passing through an era of 'medical anarchy' under BJP rule. Samajwadi Party state president reaches medical college Samajwadi Party state president Shyam Lal Pal reached the medical college at around 12 noon on Tuesday. He spoke to the woman and enquired about her well-being. He then provided the family with financial assistance of ₹10,000. They said, "This is a very serious incident. Dogs carried the body of a newborn baby out from inside the hospital. This is entirely due to the administration's negligence. I am appealing to the administration officials and the government not to ignore such incidents. Immediate action should be taken." Principal says: Action will be taken if negligence is found Medical College Principal Sushil Kaushal said the deceased child is handed over to the family. The family then performs the last rites according to its religious customs. Guards and CCTV cameras have been installed for security on the college premises. If anyone is found negligent, action will be taken. Three security guards to lose their jobs Principal Dr SK Kaushal said the incident took place in the corridor of the OT block. Three security guards had been assigned duty there. A letter has been sent to the company seeking the termination of all three guards' services. DM Amit Aseri said he had spoken to the department and the college principal. Instructions had been issued to take strict action and ensure that such an incident does not occur in the future.
