stories.title: Husband and wife burnt alive in house fire in Hathras:Couple were asleep when the fire broke out; children had gone out to attend a wedding party
stories.summary: A massive fire broke out at a house in Hathras around 2 am on Wednesday night, killing a 71-year-old man and his 65-year-old wife. The couple were asleep when the fire started and did not get a chance to escape. Neighbours noticed flames and thick smoke rising from the house and alerted the police, fire brigade and State Disaster Response Force (SDRF). Firefighters brought the blaze under control after nearly two hours of efforts. During the rescue operation, two bodies were recovered from inside the house. They were so badly burnt that identifying them proved difficult. According to the police, a short circuit caused the fire. The family was engaged in tailoring work and had stored a large quantity of material at home for the festive season. The material is believed to have helped the fire spread rapidly, engulfing the entire house within minutes. The deceased have been identified as Shahzad (71) and his wife, Salma Begum (65). Other family members had gone to attend a wedding ceremony when the incident occurred. The fire broke out in the Sadabad Kotwali area, around 20 km from the district headquarters. 2 pictures of the incident- First, learn about the family- Shahzad (70), a resident of Kaharan locality in Sadabad, owns a two-storey house. He used to work as a tailor. He married Salma Begum (65) for the second time a year and a half ago. His first wife, Hasina, died of an illness two and a half years ago. They had four sons-Sanu, Salman, Saddan and Sabbu. All of them are married. The youngest son, Sabbu, lived with Shahzad along with his wife and children. The other sons live elsewhere with their families. Sabbu and Salman sell goods by hawking, while Sanu does sewing and embroidery work. Saddan, meanwhile, runs a business selling imitation anklets. Neighbours said Sabbu had gone to Mathura on Wednesday to sell goods by hawking. He then went to his in-laws' home in Agra, where there was a wedding. His wife and children were already in Agra. Now, let us understand the entire matter in sequence- According to police, the husband and wife slept on the lower floor of the two-storey house, while their younger son lived with his family on the upper floor. As the son was not at home on Wednesday, the couple were sleeping on the first floor. They had dinner and went to sleep at night. The house caught fire at 2 a.m. As it was the festive season, a large stock of new clothes for stitching had been stored in the house. Because of this, the fire spread rapidly. On receiving the information, the police and fire brigade teams reached the spot. Given the intensity of the fire, an SDRF team also reached the site and began relief and rescue operations. SDRF officer Rajat Kumar said, "His team was on duty in Vrindavan. As soon as he received information that a house had caught fire in Sadabad, he reached the spot with the personnel and had the rescue operation started." Couple died of suffocation after inhaling smoke, doctor says Dr Neeraj Verma of Sadabad Community Health Centre (CHC) said both bodies had suffered burns covering more than 50% of their surface. Initial findings indicate that the couple died of suffocation after inhaling smoke. Several parts of their bodies were also badly burnt.

stories.title: Fog engulfs 10 UP cities, cold to intensify on Diwali:Visibility drops to 10 metres on roads; air quality deteriorates in Noida and Ghaziabad
stories.summary: Light chill is now being felt in the mornings and evenings in Uttar Pradesh, and fog has begun to form in several districts. On Thursday morning, fog covered 10 cities, including Lucknow, Sambhal, Shravasti and Deoria. In Shravasti, visibility fell below 10 metres, making it hard to see anything on the roads. Weather scientists say the cold will deepen across the state in the week of Diwali. Temperatures to fall further in Diwali week Prof Manoj Srivastava, a weather scientist at Banaras Hindu University (BHU) in Varanasi, said temperatures were likely to fall further during Diwali week. “Fog may persist in the mornings. With the change in weather, the morning and evening chill will increase,” he said. See the weather pictures- Four districts’ air unfit to breathe as GRAP-2 comes into force Air quality in NCR districts has entered the red zone ahead of Diwali. Noida’s AQI has crossed 400, while the air in Ghaziabad, Hapur and Baghpat has also reached the red zone. The second stage of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP-2) has been imposed across the NCR. Under the measures: Jhansi hottest, Muzaffarnagar coldest According to figures for 4 November, Jhansi recorded the state’s highest maximum temperature at 33C. Varanasi and Bahraich followed with 32.2C, while Prayagraj logged 32C and Gorakhpur 31.6C. Among minimum temperatures, Varanasi recorded 20C. Lakhimpur Kheri registered 20.2C, Ayodhya 20.5C, Ballia 20.7C and Fatehpur 22C. Muzaffarnagar felt the coldest, with the mercury dipping to 15.3C on Tuesday night. CM orders immediate compensation for crop losses Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has taken up the damage caused to crops by continuous rain from Storm Arnab between 29 and 31 October. He has directed all district magistrates to go into the field and assess the losses immediately. He also ordered prompt compensation for farmers and said the government would bring a special package for them. With rain likely in November, farmers have been advised to be cautious in managing rabi crops. In Purvanchal in particular, they should keep drainage in fields in good order while sowing wheat, gram, peas and mustard. Farmers urged to take care while sowing rabi crops Waterlogging in low-lying fields can damage crops. Farmers should avoid unnecessary irrigation in fields that already have enough moisture from the rain, and decide on sowing and irrigation based on the weather and soil moisture. stories.title: Lucknow to run buses every 10 minutes for Diwali, Chhath:Fleet to be expanded from November 6 to 17, making travel to Delhi and Gorakhpur easier
stories.summary: Passengers travelling home for Diwali and Chhath will get relief from the shortage of roadways buses. The Uttar Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (UPSRTC) has arranged around 900 regular buses and more than 350 additional buses for 13 major cities from Lucknow. The services will operate from November 6 to 17. The frequency of buses to Delhi, eastern Uttar Pradesh and neighbouring districts will also be increased according to passenger demand. Buses will be available from Alambagh, Kaiserbagh and Awadh bus stations. Five additional pick-up points have also been designated for passengers. 107 buses for Delhi, 44 for Gorakhpur The highest number of buses, 107, will operate between Lucknow and Delhi during the festive period. The arrangements include 44 buses for Gorakhpur, 37 for Azamgarh and 36 for Bahraich. Additionally, 23 buses each will be available for Prayagraj and Gonda-Balrampur, 20 each for Rae Bareli and Mathura, and 17 for Kanpur. The corporation has also arranged 11 buses for Dehradun and 10 each for Haridwar and Varanasi. These are route-wise bus allocations. Buses available from three major bus stations Passengers will be able to board buses from three major bus stations in Lucknow. The number of buses will be increased depending on passenger demand. Five additional pick-up points designated Apart from the main bus stations, passengers can board buses from five designated pick-up points across the city: These locations will make it easier for passengers living in different parts of Lucknow to board buses without travelling to the main bus stations. Seats available in 120 AC buses UPSRTC has announced that seats are currently available in 120 AC buses. Passengers can book advance or Tatkal tickets through the corporation's official website and the Rahi app. Booking is available for journeys up to November 17. The corporation has advised passengers to purchase tickets only through authorised channels to avoid paying extra money to touts. Ticket booking and helpline details: Drivers and conductors to get incentives of up to Rs 4,800 To ensure uninterrupted bus services during the festive rush, UPSRTC will also provide incentives to drivers and conductors. Employees completing 11 days of duty and covering an average of 300 km per day will receive Rs 4,400. Those completing 12 days and meeting the prescribed criteria will get a lump-sum incentive of Rs 4,800. Contractual and outsourced employees have also been included in the scheme. For every kilometre travelled beyond the prescribed distance, they will receive an additional payment of 55 paise. Drivers operating electric buses and covering 3,300 km in 11 days will be eligible for an additional incentive of around Rs 1,000.

stories.title: Two sisters from Lucknow die in snowfall:Brother learns of tragedy through social media; bodies to reach home today
stories.summary: Two sisters from Lucknow died after being caught in heavy snowfall and an avalanche during a trek to Kedartal in Uttarkashi district of Uttarakhand. The bodies of Vartika Verma and Deepika Verma were recovered during a search operation on Wednesday morning. Of the eight people who went missing in the incident, six have died so far. After the post-mortem examination on Wednesday evening, the family members left for Lucknow with the sisters' bodies. They are expected to reach home at around 1 pm on Thursday, after which the last rites will be performed. The sisters had set out from Gangotri for the Kedartal trek on October 27, along with seven other trekkers and five support staff members. The three-day trek was scheduled to end on October 29. However, the weather deteriorated during the expedition. Heavy snowfall and an avalanche blocked the return route, leaving eight members of the group stranded. On October 30, some members of the group contacted the trekking agency and sought help, reporting that they were stranded near Kachcha Dhang. A rescue operation was subsequently launched. Four members of the support team were rescued safely on October 31. Three more bodies were recovered on Wednesday morning, including those of the two sisters. Both sisters were passionate about trekking Their father, Shree Narayan Verma, originally from Sarai Pandey in Barabanki, is retired from the Agriculture Department. He has three children. Vartika worked for a private company in Noida and was also a freelance influencer. She had gone on the Kedartal trek as part of a tour package provided by her company. Deepika worked as a graphic designer with a private company in Mumbai. She was currently staying in Lucknow while working from home. Both sisters were passionate about trekking and had completed several treks in India and Nepal. Around two months ago, they had returned from a trip to the Valley of Flowers and Hemkund Sahib. A year earlier, they had also completed the Kedarkantha trek in Uttarkashi's Mori area with their brother Atul and some friends. Brother learnt about the tragedy through social media Atul Verma, the sisters' brother, travelled to Uttarkashi with other family members to search for them. According to Atul, the trekking agency did not inform the family about the incident. He learnt about the tragedy after seeing news reports on social media. The family has raised questions about the trekking agency's role. They allege that the trek was allowed to proceed despite bad weather and that the agency failed to inform them promptly after the incident. The family said that if they had received the information in time, they could have reached the area immediately to seek help.

stories.title: Miscreants flee after stealing ₹4,000 worth of petrol in Lucknow:Drag sales attendant for 500 metres before pushing him to the ground
stories.summary: After getting the car's tank filled at a petrol pump in Lucknow, miscreants fled without paying. When the sales attendant tried to stop them, the car occupants dragged him for around 500 metres. They then pushed him onto the road and drove away. The sales attendant was seriously injured in the fall and has been admitted to a trauma centre, where his condition remains critical. The incident took place at around 4:19 a.m. on Sunday at a petrol pump on Sultanpur Road in the Gosainganj police station area. The petrol pump operator lodged a report at Sadar police station. With the help of CCTV footage, police are working to identify the accused based on the car's registration number. See three pictures related to the incident... Read the details now... According to the staff, a black car had stopped at nozzle number five at the petrol pump. The occupants had filled the car with around ₹4,000 worth of petrol. After this, when employee Satyanam asked for payment, the driver began distracting him by pretending that he was going to pay. Employee had reached the car window with the swipe machine According to the pump's CCTV footage, Satyanam reached the driver's side window of the car carrying a swipe machine. At around 4:21, he extended his hand to collect the payment, when the driver suddenly sped away. In an attempt to save himself and stop the car, Satyanam clung to the window. Despite this, the driver did not stop and dragged him for about 500 metres along the highway. The accused then pushed the employee onto the road and fled. Employee found bleeding on road The other petrol pump employees who ran after the car found Satyanam unconscious some distance away. He was bleeding. His colleagues took him to the Gosaingunj Community Health Centre. After providing first aid, doctors referred him to the PGI Trauma Centre in view of his serious condition. His condition is currently reported to be critical. Police investigating based on CCTV footage The petrol pump manager filed a complaint at Gosaingunj police station against the unidentified occupants of the car. The incident was recorded by two CCTV cameras installed at the pump. Police are working to identify the car and the accused based on the footage. Footage from other cameras installed along Sultanpur Road and the highway is also being examined.

stories.title: WATCH | Muslim women celebrate Diwali by performing Ram's aarti:Say, 'Lord Ram is ancestor of everyone living in India'
stories.summary: Today is Diwali. People will light lamps and celebrate in the evening. There will be plenty of fireworks. Before this, Chief Minister Yogi celebrated Diwali with forest-dwellers (Vantangia) in Gorakhpur district. He set off fireworks by pressing a button from the stage. On Sunday morning, Yogi worshipped at the Ram temple and Hanumangarhi in Ayodhya. He ate with the saints. The Chief Minister met Nritya Gopal Das, president of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Trust. He celebrated Diwali with people in a Nishad settlement. He went from house to house distributing fruit and sweets. Meanwhile, Muslim women in Kashi worshipped Lord Shri Ram. They offered bhog. They performed an aarti for Shri Ram and Mata Janaki. They then recited the Hanuman Chalisa. With folded hands, they sought the Lord's blessings. Nazneen Ansari, national president of the Muslim Mahila Foundation, said, "Changing our religion will not make us Arab, Turkish or Iranian. The ancestors of everyone living in India are Shri Ram. Religion may change, but ancestors and traditions do not." WATCH the video…

stories.title: Home Guard candidates break down in tears on Diwali:Cover heads with shrouds, lie on the ground as police drag them into vans at protest
stories.summary: Candidates for the Uttar Pradesh Home Guard Recruitment-2025 protested in Lucknow on Sunday. Several candidates broke down and started crying during the protest. They said the final result of the recruitment examination had been released without a waiting list. If a waiting list was not released, many candidates who applied for the recruitment would become overage. The protesters suddenly gathered near the Gandhi statue in Hazratganj at around 2 p.m. They were carrying banners and posters, and all of them had tied white cloth around their heads. The candidates said they had come to Lucknow with shrouds tied around their heads. They said they would die but would not leave the place. When the police tried to remove the protesters from near the Gandhi statue, the candidates lay down on the road. Despite this, the police continued trying to remove them. The police grabbed the clothes and hands of the protesters one by one, dragged them along the road and lifted them into vehicles. During this, the candidates kept pleading with the police with folded hands. Later, the police took everyone to the protest venue at Eco Garden. See 3 pictures- Candidates say those excluded from final selection should be given a chance The Uttar Pradesh Police Recruitment and Promotion Board had announced recruitment for 41,424 Home Guard posts in 2025. The written examination was held on 25, 26 and 27 April. Medical verification of the selected candidates has begun at the police lines in the respective districts from 12 October. The candidates said those excluded from the final selection should be given a chance. 'If we do not get the job, we will take our own lives' Uma Verma, who came from Rampur, made an emotional appeal for a job. She said, "I have left my sick mother alone at home and come here on a festival day. We have come with shrouds tied around our heads. We will die, we will take our own lives, but we will not leave without a job. Life is worthless without a job. "Yogi ji is sending greetings, but our Diwali has turned black. So many lamps are being lit in Ayodhya-will that get us a job? We will either leave with a job or our funeral procession will be taken out. The administration may shoot us in the chest if it wants, but we will not return empty-handed." 'We are demanding our rights, not begging' Candidate Deepak Rajvanshi, who came from Sitapur, said tearfully, "There is no Diwali for us. I have crossed the age limit. If my name does not make it in this recruitment, I will not get a government job. Despite the continued protests, no one is listening. We have all the qualifications. We are eligible in every respect. We are not begging for a place on the waiting list. It is our right." Between 15,000 and 20,000 Home Guard posts may remain vacant The protesting candidates claim that recruitment drives for Home Guards, the Uttar Pradesh Police and UPSSSC are being conducted at the same time. As a result, many candidates may be able to appear for more than one recruitment drive. They say that after being selected for other posts, 15,000 to 20,000 Home Guard posts could remain vacant. The candidates are demanding that a waiting list be released under the recruitment rules and that eligible candidates be given an opportunity to fill the vacant posts. They say this would provide employment to rural youth and reduce the fear of missing out on future recruitment opportunities because of becoming overage.

stories.title: Husband called her 'ugly', wife dies by suicide:Mother alleges daughter was murdered and hanged in Kanpur; married 9 months ago
stories.summary: A 30-year-old woman's body was found hanging from a noose in Kanpur on Sunday. Her husband called her family and informed them. The woman's mother, who reached the spot, said- My daughter was harassed by her in-laws. My son-in-law taunted her by calling her dark. He also assaulted her frequently. My daughter could not have committed suicide. She was murdered. The woman was identified as Ruchi Mishra, a resident of Sisamau. She had got married only about nine months ago. Wedding took place in February; began harassing her after three to four months Sushil Trivedi, who lives in Baikunthpur village in the Bidhnu police station area, is a private-sector employee. His family includes his wife, Manju Trivedi, sons Manish and Ashwani, and daughter Ruchi. Sushil said, “I married my daughter Ruchi to Gopal Mishra, son of Rajesh Mishra, who lives in Jawahar Park in Sisamau, on 18 February.” Rajesh makes television circuits at a factory in Dadanagar. Gopal also helps his father with work at the factory. Everything remained fine for the first three to four months of the marriage. After that, her in-laws began harassing his daughter in various ways. At times, she was taunted about her complexion, while at other times she was insulted for allegedly receiving insufficient dowry. Her husband often told her, "You are dark." When she protested, his daughter was also assaulted. Ruchi told family members about her problems several times. Woman's maternal family created a ruckus, alleging murder The woman's maternal family created a ruckus, alleging dowry harassment and murder. The police managed to pacify the family members and sent the body for a post-mortem examination. Late on Saturday evening, a day before her death, Ruchi called her mother, Manju Trivedi, and told her that she was being harassed at her marital home. She told her mother, "Mummy, take me away from here. These people harass me a lot." Her mother assured her that she would bring her home after Diwali, but the news of her death came the very next day. Brother says, ‘My sister was killed and hanged’ Rajesh Trivedi said, "My sister was murdered. She was killed and hanged. We now want justice for ourselves and for that girl. She was always harassed." Sometimes it was because of her dark complexion, and sometimes over something else. She had been reduced to living like a domestic worker. We feel that the boy was involved in something else. He did not even speak properly. ACP says-Action will be taken based on the post-mortem report ACP Sisamau Anand Ojha said that the body of the newlywed woman was found hanging from a noose. The police have sent the body for a post-mortem examination. Her family have alleged murder. The family have not filed a complaint so far. As soon as a complaint is received, a case will be registered and strict action will be taken.

stories.title: Mahakumbh’s ‘Daatun Boy’ marries for love:Fears for his life, releases video seeking protection from Jaunpur SP
stories.summary: Akash Yadav (21), who became famous as the 'Datoon Boy' at the Prayagraj Maha Kumbh, married his girlfriend Manisha (18) in Jaunpur. Akash got married at the Sheetla Mata temple on Saturday. Immediately afterwards, the couple released a video saying that their lives were in danger. Akash said, "We are both adults. We got married of our own free will. The girl's family is harassing our family. The administration is not supporting us. We could be killed at any time. Therefore, Jaunpur SP Dr Yashveer Singh should provide us with security." Manisha is the same person who gave Akash the idea of selling datun at the Maha Kumbh. Before getting married at the temple, the two had also had a court marriage on 13 October. Two pictures from the wedding- Aakash became famous selling tooth-cleaning twigs at the Maha Kumbh Akash Yadav said, "I am a resident of Madiyanv in the Barsathi police station area of Jaunpur. I am my parents' only son. I have three sisters. My father works in a private job in Mumbai. I have completed a BSc degree and make reels on social media." I have 3 lakh 10 thousand followers on Facebook and 1 lakh 70 thousand on Instagram. I sold datun in large numbers during the Maha Kumbh. After this, I became known as the 'Datun Boy'. He became friends with his girlfriend on social media 3 years ago Aakash became friends with Manisha (18 years and nine months old) through social media three years ago. They then began talking to each other. Gradually, their friendship turned into love. They decided to get married. Aakash said that he and Manisha got married in a court in Jaunpur on 13 October without informing their families. When Manisha's family learnt about it, they began harassing her. It is alleged that her family kept Manisha locked in a room. They did not let her go outside. They beat her when she protested and did not give her food either. Manisha told me about this. Aakash said, "I made a plan to get Manisha out of her house. As planned, Manisha left home and came to me on 6 November. On 7 November, we got married according to Hindu customs at the Sheetla Mata temple. Since the wedding, Manisha's family have been looking for both of us." Manisha said-My family is harassing my husband A 37-second video of Akash and Manisha has emerged. Both are seen wearing garlands. Manisha says, “Jaunpur SP sir, my husband and his family are being harassed. My family is harassing them. I request you not to harass them.”

stories.title: Over 100 people fall seriously ill after eating golgappas:Patients rushed to hospital in buses private vehicles as their condition worsens
stories.summary: More than 100 people have been admitted to various hospitals in Siddharthnagar after complaining of vomiting, diarrhoea and fever. According to villagers, they fell ill after eating golgappas on Dhanteras. As their condition worsened, the sick were taken to hospital by bus and private vehicles. Everyone is currently in stable condition. One young man is reported to be in critical condition. The incident occurred in Kanlakhore and Pedari Buzurg villages, about 35 kilometres from the district headquarters. Around 31 people have been admitted to the district hospital and medical college, while more than 70 are receiving treatment at local hospitals and from doctors. Meanwhile, the health department was thrown into a tizzy after such a large number of villagers fell ill. Medical teams have reached both villages. See 3 pictures... Read the full story... Nearly 100 people fell ill after eating golgappas in Kanlakhore and Pedari Buzurg villages in Khesraha development block. Sukhai (40), a resident of Kanlakhore, said that Sandeep, who is from the village, had been selling golgappas from a cart. He lived in Mumbai and had come to the village only four or five days earlier. It was the first time he had set up a phulki cart in the village. Sukhai said he had also eaten the golgappas, after which he fell ill and began suffering from vomiting and diarrhoea. Initially, people bought medicines from medical stores and treated themselves, but as a large number of people continued to fall ill, they began being taken to hospital on Sunday. At around 1 p.m., villagers were brought to the hospital in a bus. Thirty-one people have been admitted to the district hospital and medical college. More than 70 people are also receiving treatment at private hospitals. In view of the seriousness of the situation, a team from the Health Department reached the village and began monitoring the sick. 'Children fall ill after eating golgappas' Ravikant from the village said a golgappa vendor had come to the village on Dhanteras. A large number of children had eaten golgappas. Some children began falling ill at night, while others fell ill during the day. I have three children as well. My two daughters and one son are unwell. I brought medicine from a medical shop, but they are not getting any relief. I will now have to take them to the district hospital. 10 children admitted to district hospital The children admitted to the district hospital include Divya (five), Diksha (eight), Siddhi (five), Kartik (two), Babita (19), Sarita (18), Anita (20), Meena (19), Priya (17) and Sharmili (25). 17 patients being treated at medical college Seventeen people have been admitted to the medical college. They include patients ranging from two-year-old children to 60-year-old elderly people. The admitted patients include Anita (16), Nisha (18), Mahesh (20), Radhika (35), KamleshwarI (60), Sarmila (25), Divya (five), Priya (17), Meena (19), Babita (19), Sarita (18), Anita (21), Dikshi (eight), Siddhi (five), Satyam (nine), Kabyansh (two) and Kartik (two). 20 people from Pedari Buzurg village also fall ill The health of 20 people from Pedari Buzurg village also deteriorated after they ate golgappas. They include Sunita (45), Mukesh (16), Rupesh (14), Khushboo (18), Pushpa (20), Manisha (22), Vidyawati (45), Nisha (15), Asha (20), Mahima (14), Aniket (eight), Mamta (15), Manju (35), Urmila (35), Satyam (eight), Rajan (12), Kavya (three), Sajan (11), Gyanmati (five) and Ramrati (seven). One youth in critical condition Dr SN Upadhyay, chief medical superintendent of the district hospital, said Mahesh (22) was in a more serious condition than the other admitted patients. He has been kept under special observation. However, all the other admitted patients are out of danger. It is suspected that people fell ill because the water used for the golgappas was contaminated. Most of the patients have complained of stomach pain, vomiting and diarrhoea. CMO sends Health Department team to village CMO Dr Sanjay Dohre said he would visit the village himself to take stock of the situation. The health department team has already been sent to the spot. The sick children are being monitored continuously. Inspector-in-charge of Khesarha, Ramkrishna Mishra, said, “No complaint has been received in the matter so far. The accused golgappa seller, Sandeep, son of Triloki, is being questioned.”

stories.title: 'Modi' firecrackers see rising demand in Lucknow:Green crackers and fancy fireworks popular, prices range from ₹10 to ₹7,000
stories.summary: The demand for 'Modi' firecrackers has increased in Lucknow this Diwali, with customers buying varieties across different price ranges. People are also preparing for fancy fireworks using green crackers. Fancy items that release colourful stars into the sky, drone crackers and sky boosters are attracting buyers. From sparklers, flower pots and small firecracker strings for children to large aerial shots, customers are purchasing a wide range of crackers. Prices in the market range from ₹10 to ₹7,000. Firecracker trader Rajesh Singh said he had been in the business for 20-21 years. This year, demand for green crackers is higher in line with the Supreme Court's orders. Their popularity has increased over the past two years. These crackers produce less smoke because they contain fewer chemicals. Prices range from ₹50 per box to ₹5,000-6,000. Demand for green crackers rises this year This year, drone crackers and fancy items that release stars of different colours into the sky have also hit the market. Drone crackers rise into the air like drones before bursting with a loud sound. Glow-in-the-dark glasses are also available to protect people's eyes while bursting crackers. See 3 pictures... Multiple rounds of shots make 'Modi' crackers popular Shopkeeper Ajay Kumar said he had been in the firecracker business for 35-40 years. His shop offers crackers priced from ₹10 to around ₹7,000. Demand for 'Modi' crackers is particularly high this year. Customers are showing interest in varieties with 12, 15, 60, 13 and 24 shots. Pankaj Sharma, who has been setting up a firecracker shop for 8-9 years, said a large number of customers visit every year. This time, prices have seen a difference of around ₹19-20. Sky boosters with 60 and 130 shots are in the highest demand. After lighting them, people can sit back and enjoy the fireworks in the sky. Good fireworks available even on a ₹2,000 budget Abhinav Singh, who came to buy firecrackers, said he had purchased a 240-shot skyshot, a 354 One in Four skyshot, classic items, flower pots and Tiger bombs. He said firecracker prices increase every year and had gone up again this time. Aviral Mishra, who arrived with his friends from Indira Nagar, said he had come to buy a 70-cm chakri, flower pots, skyshots and firecracker strings. He would also buy sparklers and smaller crackers for home so that his mother and sister could enjoy fireworks during Diwali. He said discounts of up to 50-60% were available in the market. Good fireworks could be purchased even on a budget of ₹1,500-2,000. Pankaj Sharma said that he had been running a firecracker shop for eight to nine years. Every year, large numbers of customers come to shop. This time, a difference of around ₹19-20 in prices has been seen. The greatest demand is for the 60-shot and 130-shot Sky Booster fireworks. After setting them off, people sit back and enjoy the fireworks lighting up the sky. Firework prices rise every year. Prices have gone up this year as well. He will also buy sparklers and small firecrackers for the house so that his mother and sister can enjoy fireworks during Diwali. He said discounts of up to 50-60% were available in the market. Good fireworks can also be bought on a budget of ₹1,500 to ₹2,000. Came to buy sparkling anar and 100-shot fireworks Ayush, who came from Alambagh, said that good prices and discounts were available here. He had come to buy sparkling anar and 100 shots. Sufficient fireworks are available for ₹2,000 to ₹2,500, which can be used for two or three days of celebrations. His mother brings the items for the puja at home, and his younger sister also lights fireworks. He shops for fireworks with his friends. stories.title: Firecracker explodes in palm within 3 seconds, fingers severed:Mother couldn't bear son's shock; celebrate Diwali with caution
stories.summary: Diwali fell on 14 November that year. It was a Wednesday. I had gone out in the evening to set off a country-made firecracker. I was holding a lit candle in one hand and the firecracker in the other. Suddenly, my attention was diverted and the candle and firecracker ended up in the same hand. Before I could understand what had happened, there was a loud blast. The firecracker exploded in my hand. My left hand was severely injured. The flesh of my palm was blown away, and three fingers were severed and fell to the ground. That blast left me disabled in just three seconds. My life had changed forever. The shock of the accident affected not just me but the entire family. My mother could not bear the pain. She died on Holi in 2002, four to six months after the accident. That is why I strongly urge people not to be careless while setting off firecrackers during Diwali. Lucknow's Amit Srivastava became emotional while recounting this pain. On the special festival of lights, Dainik Bhaskar spoke to him in detail about the incident that happened to him 25 years ago. Read this report.. The blast was so powerful that his palm was blown off; his life changed in 3 seconds Amit, a resident of Vishesh Khand in Gomtinagar, said that at the time of the incident, his younger brother Anup was standing near the boundary wall inside the house. Neighbours were also watching from their homes as fireworks were being lit. Amit said, "I do not know how my attention was diverted and both things ended up in the same hand. I felt some rustling. Before I could understand where the candle had gone, the blast had already occurred. Everything happened in less than three seconds." The blast was so powerful that his hand was thrown into the air before coming back down. His palm was torn open. Three fingers were severed and fell to the ground. Two had been completely severed, while one was partially severed. His thumb and one finger were spared. Much of the flesh on his palm had also been blown away. He remained conscious as blood poured from his hand Amit says that chaos broke out at home after the sudden accident. His father screamed. He could not understand what had happened. Blood was continuously pouring from his hand. Before the news could reach his mother, their neighbour, Mr Pandey, who lived opposite them, immediately took out his car and rushed him to hospital. When the doctors saw the condition of his hand, they began treatment immediately. After providing first aid, they tied the hand upwards with a wooden support to reduce the bleeding. He then underwent surgery. Amit says he remained conscious until the operation was performed. His thumb also had to be amputated after the operation Amit said that if the severed fingers had been picked up and placed in ice, it might have been possible to use them during plastic surgery. But the family was so panicked at the time of the accident that no one realised this. The fingers were later found lying at home. Doctors also tried to save the thumb. They had told the family that it might have to be amputated. The father told the doctors to do for his son what they would do for a member of their own family. The doctors tried to save the thumb, but it did not recover and began to turn black. Later, after another examination and surgery, the thumb also had to be amputated. Mother went into shock, died four to six months later Amit says the accident changed his life completely. He used to drive, but doctors advised him not to. His mobility decreased. He says, "I felt inferior for a long time. I would walk around hiding my hand from people. If someone asked, I had to tell them about the accident. The plans I had made for my life were also affected after I became disabled." The accident also affected his parents. According to Amit, his father was shocked, while his mother also remained deeply distressed after seeing her son's condition. He feels that the dreams his mother had for her elder son's future were shattered. Mother suffered deep shock after the accident Amit says, "I met with an accident in November. Four to six months later, in 2002, my mother died on Holi. She did not have any illness. I realised that my accident had deeply shocked her. Seeing how much the family suffered made my own pain seem small." Now advises people to stay away from fireworks Amit says that after the accident, he decided to make sure he told people he knew about the harm caused by fireworks. He says that even a moment of carelessness while lighting fireworks can cause a lifetime of pain. He says, "A calm and focused mind is essential when setting off fireworks. Never light a firework while holding a candle in one hand and the firework in the other. It is also dangerous to repeatedly look at a firework after lighting it. It is better not to set off fireworks. If people do set them off, they should do so in an open field with great caution." Amit advises organising fireworks displays collectively. He says that if a professional fireworks operator is hired to put on a display in a park or open field, people can enjoy it from a safe distance. This will reduce the risk of accidents. Firework also exploded on nephew's face Another fireworks-related accident occurred in Amit's family. Around 2019-20, his younger brother's son was lighting fireworks on the roof during Diwali. According to Amit, a box of fireworks had been placed on the roof at around 7 p.m. The fireworks did not ignite for three to four hours. After considerable effort, some of them finally went off. After this, the child was trying to light a spinning firework. When it still did not ignite despite several attempts, he turned it over and tried to light it again. The firework then exploded directly in his face. He suffered burns around his face and eyes, followed by swelling and blisters. The family brought him downstairs and consulted the family doctor. Amit says that a moment of carelessness turned into a lifetime of pain for them. He now wants to ensure that such an accident never happens again in his family or in anyone else's home.

stories.title: Beef row leads to suspension of 3 policemen in Amroha:VHP worker cries holding severed cow parts; police register FIR against 8 shopkeepers
stories.summary: Protests broke out in Amroha after beef was reportedly found in an e-rickshaw. Workers of the Bajrang Dal and Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) vandalised the vehicle and overturned it in the middle of the road. The protesters then placed pieces of meat on the road and staged a demonstration. During the protest, a VHP worker was seen holding a severed body part of a cow, beating his chest and crying. Police teams from four police stations rushed to the spot after receiving information about the incident. Meanwhile, the meat seller fled, while police detained the e-rickshaw driver. The City Circle Officer attempted to pacify the protesters, but they refused to relent. They demanded the immediate demolition of meat shops and accused the police of facilitating cow slaughter. They also sought action against the police personnel allegedly involved. As tensions escalated, ASP Akhilesh Bhadauria reached the spot. He suspended Razzak police outpost in-charge Sandeep Baliyan and head constables Sajid and Mohit Bhadana. Following the action, the protesters called off their demonstration. On Sunday morning, police registered an FIR against eight meat sellers. The incident took place around 100 metres from the Razzak police outpost, under the jurisdiction of Nagar Kotwali police station. Beef scattered on road after bike collides with e-rickshaw At around 9 p.m. on Saturday (7 Nov), beef was being unloaded from an e-rickshaw in Machhli Wali Gali, 4 kilometres from the district headquarters. During this, a bike collided with the e-rickshaw, causing the beef to scatter across the road. As soon as they received information about the incident, workers of the Bajrang Dal and Vishva Hindu Parishad arrived. They created a disturbance, alleging that cow slaughter was taking place on a large scale in the area. They dragged an e-rickshaw to the intersection, placed meat on the road and blocked traffic The activists dragged the e-rickshaw loaded with meat to Lakda intersection. They placed the meat on the road and blocked traffic. This led to long queues of vehicles on both sides. As soon as the information was received, a large police contingent reached the spot. Hindu activists demand demolition of house where cow slaughter took place City CO Dr Pradeep Kumar and city Kotwal CP Shukla also reached the spot. They tried to pacify the protesters. The activists then demanded that the house where the cow slaughter took place be sealed and demolished using a bulldozer. They also demanded that the nearby houses be searched. After this, ASP Akhilesh Bhadauria reached the spot. He assured the activists that action would be taken. The commotion ended at 11:15 p.m. SP Lakhan Singh Yadav said, “Chowki in-charge Sandeep Baliyan and two constables have been suspended for alleged negligence. One accused has been taken into custody. Two accused fled the spot and are being searched for. An FIR has been registered against eight accused in the case.”

stories.title: Campaign to run for one year in memory of the:Kakori Centenary Sacrifice Memorial year campaign to begin on 19 December
stories.summary: A nationwide campaign will be launched from 19 December in memory of the four immortal martyrs of the Kakori Train Action. The campaign, titled 'Kakori Centenary Martyrdom Remembrance Year', will feature various programmes. The Gurukripa Institute and the All India Revolutionary Honour Struggle Front will organise the campaign to mark 100 years since the great sacrifices of Pandit Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Thakur Roshan Singh and Rajendra Nath Lahiri, who gave up everything for the nation. Brijesh Ram Tripathi, regional minister of the BJP's Gorakhpur region and chief coordinator of the Kakori Centenary Sacrifice Remembrance Year National Campaign 2026-27, said that revolutionaries played a crucial role in freeing the country from the chains of slavery. He said that on 19 December 1927, Pandit Ram Prasad Bismil made the supreme sacrifice for the nation at Gorakhpur Jail, Ashfaqulla Khan at Faizabad Jail and Thakur Roshan Singh at Naini Jail. Rajendra Nath Lahiri, meanwhile, was hanged at Gonda Jail on 17 December 1927, before the scheduled date. He said that this year, the Kakori Centenary Sacrifice Remembrance Year would be conducted as a national public awareness campaign. They said that Rajendra Nath Lahiri Martyrdom Day would be observed on 17 December 2027, while the concluding programme of the centenary year, marking the martyrdom days of Pandit Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan and Thakur Roshan Singh, would be held on 19 December 2027. He said the campaign's primary objectives were to acquaint the new generation with the sacrifice, dedication, patriotism and philosophy of life of the revolutionaries; awaken national consciousness among young people; strengthen national unity and social harmony; and bring the historical significance of the sites of sacrifice to the public. Brijesh Ram Tripathi called upon the country's social, cultural, educational and nationalist organisations, young people, educational institutions and enlightened citizens to actively participate in this historic centenary campaign and take the ideals of the immortal martyrs to every section of society.

stories.title: Haze blankets Lucknow, Kanpur as AQI crosses 300:Cold intensifies in UP, fog covers 15 cities; temperature drops below 15°C
stories.summary: Cold has intensified in Uttar Pradesh. Haze covered Lucknow, Kanpur, Gorakhpur and seven other cities on Diwali morning. Air pollution reached dangerous levels. Lucknow's air quality index (AQI) crossed 300. The air in Gorakhpur and Kanpur is also in the red zone. Meanwhile, fog covered 15 cities, including Shravasti, Deoria, Maharajganj, Bijnor, Gonda and Sambhal. Visibility fell to 50 metres in several places. Over the past 24 hours, the night-time temperature fell below 15°C across the state. Hardoi was the coldest, recording a minimum temperature of 14°C. Meanwhile, the highest temperature was recorded in Jhansi at 33.5°C. Prof. Manoj Srivastava, a meteorologist at Varanasi's BHU, said: Cold will intensify further in Uttar Pradesh. The temperature will fall by up to 5°C over the next seven days. Fog may persist in the morning and at night. Here are pictures of the weather: Here is the situation in major cities- Lucknow: Air quality in Lucknow is deteriorating ahead of Diwali. Haze has persisted for the third consecutive day on Sunday. Visibility fell below 500 metres. Kanpur: Cold winds have been blowing since morning. Haze is also visible on the roads. Visibility is low. Weather expert Dr S.N. Sunil Pandey said the temperature would rise during the day due to the sunshine. Gorakhpur: Light haze was seen in the morning due to pollution. The maximum temperature today may be 29°C, while the minimum may be 19°C. Over the coming days, the night-time temperature is expected to fall to between 16°C and 18°C. stories.title: SSB jawan shoots himself with rifle:Deployed along Nepal border in Maharajganj; brother died two-and-a-half months ago
stories.summary: A 33-year-old Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) jawan posted at the India-Nepal border in Maharajganj died by suicide on Saturday night. He allegedly shot himself in the chest with his service rifle. Manjeet had taken his service rifle before leaving for duty. However, when he failed to report for duty, a search was launched. He was later found dead beneath a staircase inside the camp. The incident took place at the Khanua border post at around 2 am on Saturday. Manjeet, a native of Bihar, had returned to duty just five days earlier after taking leave. He was reportedly under mental distress since his return. Manjeet had got married two years ago and had a two-and-a-half-month-old son. His elder brother had also died around two-and-a-half months ago. He was posted with the 66th Battalion of the SSB. Following the incident, police personnel and senior SSB officials reached the spot. The authorities have informed Manjeet's family about his death. Manjeet joined the SSB in 2014; his father had also passed away Manjeet joined the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) on June 23, 2014. He belonged to Jamhor village in Bihar's Aurangabad district. His father, Suresh Ram, had also passed away. His mother is Nagina Devi. He is survived by his mother, two brothers and a sister. According to the SSB, Manjeet was scheduled to be on duty from 1 am to 7 am. At around 2 am, the duty commander found him missing from his assigned post. The camp authorities were informed, following which a search operation was launched. During the search, Manjeet was found dead beneath a staircase inside the camp, with his service rifle beside him. Following the incident, the Station House Officer (SHO) of Sonauli and the Circle Officer (CO) of Nautanwa reached the Khanua camp. A forensic team also collected evidence from the spot.

stories.title: Yogi celebrates Diwali with Vantangiyas, joins fireworks:Takes a dig at Ravi Kishan jokingly; tells people, ‘Go party at his Sheesh Mahal’
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath celebrated Diwali with the Van Tangia (forest-dwelling) community in Uttar Pradesh's Maharajganj district on Sunday. He pressed a button from the stage to set off fireworks. Taking a dig at MP Ravi Kishan, he told the gathering, "All of you should visit his Sheesh Mahal. Arrangements for sweets and food have been made for 5,000 people." He further said, "Just now, an elderly woman told me to ask the MP that she wants to work in his films." The CM inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for 52 development projects worth Rs 82.41 crore for the community. Earlier, Yogi offered prayers at the Ram Temple and Hanuman Garhi in Ayodhya and had a meal with saints. The CM also met Nritya Gopal Das, president of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust. He celebrated Diwali with residents of the Nishad settlement and distributed fruits and sweets by visiting their homes. See the pictures- Yogi's key points from his address 1. No Manthara or Mareech should cast an evil eye on Ayodhya CM Yogi said in Ayodhya that people must take just one pledge. The pledge should be that, in the coming years, no Manthara or Mareech should cast an evil eye on Ayodhya. No conspiracy should be allowed to loot the city's glory or tarnish its image once again. 2. Ram devotees will no longer be fired upon in Ayodhya Yogi said that Ram devotees will no longer be fired upon in Ayodhya. No one will be beaten with sticks for chanting 'Jai Shri Ram'. No restrictions will be imposed on the Panchkosi, 14-Kosi or 84-Kosi Parikrama. 3. Gandhi-Nehru family for one, Saifai family for the other Yogi said in Gorakhpur that Uttar Pradesh has 56 Vantangia villages, but their residents did not get freedom even after Independence. Neither the Samajwadi Party nor the Congress provided them with any facilities. “I have been visiting these villages continuously since 2007-08. This is the difference between the BJP-led NDA and the SP-Congress-led PDA. For one, the Gandhi-Nehru family is everything, while for the other, it is the Saifai family,” he said. 4. Politics of SP and Congress will be buried Yogi said some people were trying to tarnish Ayodhya's image. “They know that if the journey of development and heritage continues in this manner, the politics of the Samajwadi Party and the Congress will be buried. They will face a crisis of identity,” he said.

stories.title: Munshi Premchand's 'Maiku' family still makes Diwali diyas:Descendants say their work will light up 10,000 homes, but their lives remain in darkness
stories.summary: As Varanasi celebrates Diwali, the family of Maiku Prajapati, the potter immortalised in a story by renowned Hindi novelist Munshi Premchand, continues its traditional occupation of making earthen lamps. Premchand wrote a story about Maiku, who worked at his house, making him a memorable character in Hindi literature. Generations later, Maiku's descendants, living in Pandeypur area of Varanasi, are still making diyas to light up homes during the festival. However, despite their family's association with the celebrated writer, the descendants say they have received little support and continue to struggle with rising costs and poor earnings. The family has received an electric pottery wheel and monthly ration supplies as government assistance. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Maiku's descendants to understand their living conditions and the challenges they face. Read the report... 'We are just getting by' Maiku Prajapati had four sons. His eldest son, Khallu Prajapati, has passed away. The other three are Kailash, Rajendra and Jittu Prajapati. When the Dainik Bhaskar team visited the family's home in Nai Basti, it met Jittu Prajapati, Maiku's youngest son. He has given up pottery and now sells pakoras from a small shop outside his house in the evenings. Jittu said the family was not receiving any meaningful government assistance. They do not even receive an old-age pension, he claimed. "We are somehow managing to make ends meet," he said. 'Our association with Premchand has brought us no benefits' Jittu said his father used to work at Munshi Premchand's house. The family maintained contact with the writer during his grandmother's lifetime, but that connection gradually faded. "We are invited to events on his birth anniversary, and we attend. But being associated with him has brought us no benefits. We have neither a pension nor any support," Jittu said. He also alleged that someone had taken ₹500 from the family on the promise of arranging a pension but had failed to get the work done. Made 30,000 diyas, but rain damaged the stock Rukmini Devi, wife of Maiku's grandson Rajendra, was seen making earthen lamps on a pottery wheel when the team visited. She said the family had made around 30,000 diyas this year, but rainfall damaged their stock. Rising prices have also affected sales. "Earlier, people who bought 1,000 diyas are now purchasing only around 200. This has caused us losses," she said. Rukmini added that the government had provided an electric pottery wheel but no other significant assistance. She said the family also had daughters to marry but lacked the money to meet the expenses. 'When will our lives see some light?' Rukmini said that despite the family's connection with Munshi Premchand, no officials came forward to ask about their problems. "You people are the only ones who visit us once a year. The facilities we receive are an electric wheel and monthly ration. We keep wondering when our own lives will see some light," she said. 'We still have to pay the electricity bill' Rama Devi, wife of Maiku's grandson Kailash, also spoke about the family's financial difficulties. She said around 30,000 diyas had been made, but much of the stock remained unsold. "We have not received any assistance from the government apart from the pottery wheel. But when we use it, we still have to pay the electricity bill," she said. She added that the family continued to face difficulties because of rising living costs and a lack of support.

stories.title: Gorakhpur-Mumbai special train to run after Diwali and Chhath:Check dates, timings and route for passengers returning to Mumbai
stories.summary: Indian Railways will operate a festival special train between Gorakhpur and Mumbai's Lokmanya Tilak Terminus (LTT) to accommodate the rush of passengers travelling to Mumbai after Diwali and Chhath. The train, numbered 05097/05098, will make two trips in each direction. It will depart from Gorakhpur on November 11 and 18, while return services from Mumbai will operate on November 13 and 20. The additional service will provide relief to passengers travelling to Mumbai and nearby cities after the festive season. Gorakhpur-Mumbai train schedule According to the Railways, train number 05097 (Gorakhpur-Lokmanya Tilak Terminus Festival Special) will depart from Gorakhpur at 8.55 pm on November 11 and 18. It will travel through Khalilabad, Basti and Gonda before reaching Lucknow. From there, it will pass through Kanpur Central, Orai and Virangana Lakshmibai Jhansi. The train will then travel through Bina, Bhopal, Itarsi and Khandwa before entering Maharashtra. On the third day, it will pass through Bhusawal, Nashik, Igatpuri, Kalyan and Thane before reaching Lokmanya Tilak Terminus at 8.30 am. The journey from Gorakhpur to Mumbai will take approximately 36 hours. Return train to depart Mumbai at 12:30 pm Train number 05098 (Lokmanya Tilak Terminus-Gorakhpur Festival Special) will depart from Mumbai at 12.30 pm on November 13 and 20. It will pass through Thane, Kalyan, Igatpuri, Nashik and Bhusawal before entering Madhya Pradesh. The train will then travel through Khandwa, Itarsi, Bhopal, Bina and Jhansi before reaching Kanpur Central and Lucknow. On the second day, it will reach Gonda at 9.30 pm, followed by Basti at 10.37 pm and Khalilabad at 11.07 pm. It will arrive in Gorakhpur at 11.50 pm. The service will provide an additional travel option for passengers returning from Mumbai. Train to have 20 coaches The Railways has decided to operate the special train with 20 coaches. These will include: Additional option for passengers after festivals Passengers travelling to Mumbai after Diwali and Chhath often face difficulties securing confirmed seats on regular trains. The special service will provide an additional option, particularly for passengers travelling to or from Lucknow, Kanpur, Jhansi, Bhopal and Nashik.

stories.summary: A political war of words has erupted between Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav over the latter's planned visit to Ayodhya to offer prayers to Ram Lalla on December 12. After news of Akhilesh's proposed visit emerged on Saturday, Yogi criticised the SP chief, saying that those who ordered firing on Ram devotees should certainly visit Ayodhya but must apologise before coming. Akhilesh hit back at Yogi late on Saturday night. He said people in Ayodhya were asking the Chief Minister when the truth would come out in cases involving the alleged theft of offerings, donations and contributions. He questioned whether the matter would ever be investigated to establish the truth. Watch the special VIDEO on the war of words between CM Yogi and Akhilesh Yadav...

SP inactive in 53 seats, organisation collapsed in 9 districts:Infighting, ticket manoeuvring or PDA formula; why are district president appointments stuck?
stories.summary: With preparations underway for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the Samajwadi Party appears to have lost momentum across 53 constituencies. The reason is the complete breakdown of the party organisation in nine districts. Over the past three months, party chief Akhilesh Yadav has taken action against indiscipline, factionalism and inactivity, dissolving the organisational units in seven districts. In two other districts, key posts have remained vacant for a long time. At present, former district presidents are managing affairs in these districts in an acting capacity. As a result, grassroots activities, including booth management and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, have come to a standstill. This has raised questions about the delay in making fresh appointments. Sources within the party suggest that the list of new appointments is held up by local factionalism, rival claims over Assembly election tickets and the challenge of maintaining a balance within the PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) social coalition. Why are organisational posts vacant in these nine districts? The reasons behind the vacant posts and dissolved party units in the nine districts are as follows: Etah and Kasganj: A dispute broke out among party leaders on September 19 in Lucknow in the presence of party chief Akhilesh Yadav. Following the incident, Etah district president Wahid Mahmood Zuberi and Kasganj district president Vikram Yadav were removed, and both district units were dissolved. Mathura: On September 16, an FIR was registered against a state office-bearer of the Samajwadi Party’s Minority Wing over allegations of harassment of a woman bank employee. Following this, Akhilesh Yadav directed the dissolution of the party’s district, city and all frontal organisations in Mathura. Gorakhpur: Party workers were involved in a scuffle over a chair during a press conference in the city. Following the incident of indiscipline, both the district and city units were dissolved. Kannauj: The district organisation was dissolved on the instructions of state president Shyamlal Pal after the PDA conference held on October 17 failed to draw the expected crowd. Organisational inactivity was also cited as a reason. Hardoi: On June 13, an objectionable audio-video clip of then district president Sharafat Ali went viral. It contained derogatory remarks about former public representatives. Following this, the entire district executive was dissolved. Sant Kabir Nagar: Action was taken after the district organisation remained inactive during a controversy linked to MP Pappu Yadav. Budaun: The district executive was dissolved a year ago due to internal factionalism. Fresh appointments have yet to be made. Prayagraj (Yamunapar): The post has remained vacant since the death of district president Pappu Lal Nishad. Caste equations complicate the appointment process According to party sources, Akhilesh Yadav may finalise the appointments before Diwali. He wants to ensure balanced representation across all districts under the PDA (backward classes, Dalits and minorities) formula. Of the nine district presidents and two city presidents who were removed, five belonged to the Muslim community, three were Yadavs, one was a Vaishya, one was a Nishad and one was from the Gautam (Dalit) community. The party is now considering new faces while taking local caste equations into account. Ticket aspirants may be moved out of organisational posts: Party sources say district presidents and general secretaries seeking tickets for the upcoming Assembly elections will be replaced once their candidacies are finalised. New individuals will then be given organisational responsibilities to ensure that election-related work is not affected. Five key activities hit by the dissolution of party units

stories.title: Akhilesh’s PDA strategy and Swami Prasad Maurya:From Ramcharitmanas to remarks on Dimple, the story behind his controversial statements
stories.summary: Changing political loyalties is nothing new in Uttar Pradesh politics, but the bitterness between SP chief Akhilesh Yadav and Swami Prasad Maurya has now reached a point of no return. Akhilesh Yadav recently signaled that the doors of the party and alliance are permanently closed for Swami Prasad. Akhilesh stated that Swami Prasad Maurya is no longer a part of their alliance. Having navigated a political journey spanning nearly 45 years, Swami Prasad may now be looking toward the Congress with hopeful eyes, but he appears completely 'unfit' in the current equations due to SP's core electoral strategy 'PDA' (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak / Backward, Dalit, Minority) and Akhilesh's personal displeasure. Three main reasons have emerged behind this political tension and the breakdown of relations between the two prominent leaders: Akhilesh 'Politically Unfit' and a Supporter of 'Gunda Raj' Following the 2024 general elections, Swami Prasad Maurya appeared most aggressive against the Samajwadi Party and its leadership. During a podcast, he launched a sharp attack on Akhilesh. When asked who among the major figures in Indian politics is completely unfit for politics, Swami Prasad named Akhilesh Yadav without hesitation. He claimed that Akhilesh's body language and decisions clearly suggest he has entered the wrong field. Swami Prasad Maurya did not stop his aggression there; questioning Akhilesh Yadav's political ideology, he said: "Akhilesh Yadav is a completely confused leader. He is neither a Lohiaite nor a true Socialist. It is deeply tragic that despite being the son of former Chief Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav, he couldn't even become a 'Mulayamite.' He is an expert at ruining a ready-made political advantage. Nowadays, he is merely focused on pleasing the Brahmin community because a Brahmin predicted he would become Chief Minister. The truth is that Akhilesh Yadav favours 'Gunda Raj' (lawlessness)." 'D' in PDA stands for 'Dimple': Personal jibe soured relations In Uttar Pradesh's political circles, it is widely believed that Akhilesh often ignores political attacks directed at him; however, when it comes to his family, wife, or children, he tolerates it at no cost. On February 2, 2026, during the 'Samvidhan Samman Aur Janhit Hunkar Yatra' organised in Lakhimpur Kheri district, Swami Prasad took a direct jibe at Akhilesh's biggest political card, 'PDA' (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak / Backward, Dalit, Minority). Addressing a public rally, Swami said that Akhilesh himself is not clear about his PDA formula. In this, the 'D' sometimes stands for 'Dalit' and other times becomes 'Dimple,' depending on convenience. He alleged that Akhilesh never speaks openly on the issues of backward classes and Dalits. Sometimes he says 'P' stands for Pichhda (Backward), sometimes Pandit, and other times he claims that whoever is aggrieved (Pedit) is PDA. Prior to this, on February 20, 2024, when Swami Prasad resigned from the SP and his MLC post, he had similarly remarked that Akhilesh himself had deflated the momentum of PDA through his decisions, and that no outsider, but the party chief himself, was responsible for weakening SP. Continuous controversial remarks on Hinduism, Ramcharitmanas, and deities Until the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, Swami Prasad Maurya had not made many statements on religious matters. However, after losing his own election from the Fazilnagar seat in Kushinagar, his rhetoric changed completely. Right after losing the election, he stated, "Buddhism is the oldest religion in the world, followed by Christianity, and then Islam came into existence." In this statement, he deliberately refrained from mentioning Hinduism. Following this, wherever he went in 2023, he continued to criticise Hindu beliefs and scriptures. Swami Prasad Maurya’s 4 most controversial statements that sparked a storm: 'How is a statement personal?' — Left SP over this very issue Due to Swami Prasad’s continuous rhetoric, the Samajwadi Party was facing political discomfort. Whenever SP spokespersons tried to corner the BJP on TV debates over Hindutva, development, or employment, BJP leaders would immediately bring up Swami Prasad's statements to put SP in the dock. Gradually, discontent began brewing against Swami Prasad within SP itself. During an event in Raebareli, a youth even slapped Swami, and on two separate occasions, shoes were thrown at him. When the media questioned Akhilesh Yadav regarding Swami's statements, Akhilesh dismissed them as his 'personal views' rather than the party's official stance. Akhilesh’s posture did not go down well with Swami Prasad Maurya. Expressing his displeasure, he remarked, "When I am the party's National General Secretary, how can my statements be 'personal'?" Following this, he resigned from the party. Akhilesh Yadav accepted his resignation immediately without any persuasion, and the doors of SP were closed to him permanently. Outspokenness ruined political career According to Rajkumar Singh, a senior political analyst and journalist from Lucknow, Swami Prasad Maurya's loose talk and controversial rhetoric are nothing new; it has been going on since the Bahujan Samaj Party rule. Back then, Mayawati's government was strong in the state, which prevented an open atmosphere from building against him. When he joined the Bharatiya Janata Party in 2017, his statements were somewhat restrained. However, after joining the Samajwadi Party in 2022 and losing the election, his political frustration came out into the open. Due to his uncontrolled language and remarks, he not only lost his own election from Fazilnagar, but also severely damaged the political career of his daughter, Sanghmitra Maurya, who was a BJP MP. Speculation: Congress brought Swami to boost bargaining power Now seeing a ray of hope in the Congress, he has moved there. However, given the kind of personal attacks he launched against Akhilesh Yadav and his family, Akhilesh will never take him back. By commenting on Dimple Yadav, Swami Prasad closed all doors for dialogue with his own hands. Ahead of the upcoming elections, there are clear indications that Congress has brought Swami Prasad Maurya along to increase its bargaining power in Uttar Pradesh. Nevertheless, Congress also appears to be distancing itself from Swami’s ongoing statements, with its state in-charge Ramji Lal also describing his remarks as 'personal.' Swami Prasad has been a prominent face in Uttar Pradesh's ruling and opposition politics for the last four and a half decades. However, over the past five years, his political track record has been completely turbulent.

stories.title: Blue-drum accused Muskan learning stitching and embroidery in Meerut jail:Hoping to escape the death penalty, she plans to start a business after release
stories.summary: Muskan Rastogi, convicted in the widely discussed Blue Drum murder case, is learning sewing and embroidery at Meerut jail. She has already completed a beautician course. While in prison, Muskan has also learnt to make rakhis, kandils (decorative hanging lanterns) and candles. The way Muskan is training herself while in jail suggests that her focus is now on her future. She appears to believe that her death sentence will be commuted. She is thinking that she will be released from jail soon. Once out, she plans to support herself through self-employment. That is why Muskan is continuing to learn various skills in prison. On October 14, the Meerut district court sentenced Muskan and her boyfriend Sahil to death for the murder of Saurabh. Sahil’s family has taken responsibility for seeking commutation of their death sentences. They have filed a petition in the High Court. Muskan has been in jail for 20 months Muskan Rastogi has been lodged in Meerut district jail for around 20 months. She was convicted of murdering her husband, Saurabh Rajput. Muskan and her boyfriend Sahil killed Saurabh on March 3, 2025, cut up his body, and stuffed it into a blue drum. Muskan gave birth to a daughter in jail. Under the prison manual, she cannot be made to perform strenuous work until her daughter turns six. That is why Muskan is doing routine work in jail and learning sewing and embroidery. Training sessions are also organised from time to time for women inmates, and Muskan participates in them alongside other women prisoners. Expressed a desire to learn a new course from a women's organisation Sanjeevani Mahila Sanstha, an NGO that provides vocational training to women inmates in jail, has trained Muskan in these self-employment skills. Muskan had expressed a desire to learn all the new courses. Parul Bansal, secretary of the organisation, which visits the jail to train women inmates, said Muskan had learnt beautician skills, how to make kandils, decorative door hangings known as bandanwars, and rakhis. She is currently learning sewing and embroidery. Parul said, “Our organisation has been helping women inmates at the district jail develop vocational skills for more than 20 years. This enables them to start a new life after leaving prison and earn a living through the skills they have learnt.” Parul said Muskan had first learnt the beautician course from the organisation. She had herself expressed a desire to learn beauty parlour skills. Later, during Raksha Bandhan, Muskan learnt to make rakhis. Now, for Diwali, she has learnt to make kandils and bandanwars. In this way, Muskan is participating in every training programme. The same lawyer is fighting Muskan and Sahil's cases in the High Court The same lawyer is representing Muskan and Sahil in their efforts to get their death sentences commuted. Sahil’s family hired advocate Sushil Shukla in Allahabad. Senior advocate Sushil Shukla is representing both Muskan and Sahil in the High Court. He has filed petitions seeking commutation of their death sentences. The matter is scheduled to be heard on November 30. Sahil’s family has also taken responsibility for trying to save Muskan from the gallows. This suggests that Muskan is now less concerned about arranging legal assistance for her release or seeking commutation of her sentence herself. Her focus appears to be on her life after prison. That is why she is working to secure her future. Muskan believes her death sentence will be commuted because of her young daughters Muskan firmly believes that her death sentence will be commuted and that she will soon be released from jail. She repeatedly referred to the care of her two young daughters before the judge. Rekha Jain, who represented Muskan in the case, also appealed to the court to consider that Muskan had two young daughters who needed care. Muskan therefore believes that the emotional aspect of her daughters’ welfare will help save her from the death penalty and secure a reduction in her sentence. She expects Sahil’s family to handle the remaining legal work. Once released, she plans to open her own beauty parlour and earn a living.

stories.title: Brij Bhushan’s daughter gifts him a helipad:Built for ₹50 lakh, she says, 'Papa made me capable of this'
stories.summary: The daughter of former BJP MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh gifted him a helipad in Noida two months before his birthday. At around 5 p.m. on Sunday, Brij Bhushan inaugurated the helipad by breaking a coconut after performing the traditional puja rituals. Brij Bhushan's birthday is on 8 January 2027. His daughter, Shalini Singh, wrote in a post on Facebook and Instagram, "Today, we presented Papa with a newly built helipad in Noida as a birthday gift." Brij Bhushan owns three helicopters. One of them will always remain at this helipad in Noida. It is being said that the helipad was built at a cost of ₹50 lakh. However, the land on which the helipad has been built is estimated to be worth crores of rupees. Brij Bhushan's daughter is currently the executive president of the Noida Citizen Forum. See two pictures... Daughter said, 'Papa made me capable of this' Dainik Bhaskar, Shalini said, "Dad has always loved me very much and given me gifts since my childhood. He made me capable of reaching a position where I can give him something today." "That is why I thought I would give him this gift before his birthday. This helipad will help Dad travel between Gonda and Noida." "Dad has always supported me. No amount of praise for him would be enough. I do not want to reveal the cost of this helipad, because the value of something given as a gift is never disclosed." 3 helicopters in Brij Bhushan's fleet Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh has 3 helicopters in his fleet. The black helicopter will remain at Noida's new helipad at all times, while the saffron and white helicopters will remain at his home in Gonda. Two helipads have already been built at Brij Bhushan's home. This facility will make it easier for Brij Bhushan to travel between Gonda and Noida. It will also make it easier for his daughter, Shalini Singh, to travel to and from her marital home in Bihar. Shalini's Parents-in-Law Were Former MPs from Bihar; She Lives with Her Husband in Noida Former MP Brij Bhushan Singh married Shalini Singh to Vishal Singh, the only son of former Ara MP late Ajit Singh and former MP Meena Singh. Vishal Singh currently lives in Noida. He is also a BJP leader. He is also the chairman of the National Cooperative Consumers' Federation (NCCF). Besides this, he is the president of the Bihar State Cooperative Marketing Union (BISCOMAUN). Shalini and Vishal have a 14-year-old son, Atharv. The book they have written is titled "I Am Fearless, Not Disrespectful". Shalini Singh is currently the executive president of the Noida Citizen Forum and is also a BJP worker in Noida. She is also preparing to contest the election from Noida.

stories.title: Two Air India flights diverted to Lucknow:Flights on Delhi-Kathmandu route affected due to bad weather
stories.summary: Two Air India flights were diverted and landed at Lucknow airport because of bad weather in Kathmandu. They included flight AI-213, which was travelling from Delhi to Kathmandu, and flight AI-223, which was travelling from Kathmandu to Delhi. Return flight to Delhi took off Air India flight AI-213, travelling from Delhi to Kathmandu, took off from Delhi at 7:04 a.m. It landed at Lucknow airport at 10:04 a.m. The flight was diverted because of bad weather in Kathmandu. Diversion caused inconvenience to passengers Flight to Kathmandu was later cancelled. The aircraft took off from Lucknow for Delhi at 11:19 a.m. Meanwhile, the second flight, AI-223, was also diverted to Lucknow because of bad weather in Kathmandu. The diversion of both flights caused inconvenience to passengers.

stories.title: Woman dies immediately after receiving injection in Lucknow:She underwent leg surgery three days earlier, family accuses doctors of negligence
stories.summary: A woman died after doctors administered injections at Highway Hospital in Madiyaon, Lucknow. She had been admitted for five days for leg surgery, which had been performed three days earlier. According to her family, her condition was normal until Sunday morning. She was laughing and talking with her family members. During this time, she informed the doctor that she was experiencing mild pain in her leg. The family alleged that the doctor gave her an injection. The woman died suddenly shortly afterwards. Her family members created a commotion at the hospital, alleging negligence. She was supposed to go home from hospital today According to Mohit Sharma, a resident of Munshiganj in Sitapur, his mother, Usha Sharma, had suffered an injury. He admitted her to Highway Hospital on 26 October. Her leg was operated on 28 October. He said that they were due to be discharged from the hospital today, 1 November. They were at home when the hospital called to say that his mother had died. Mohit accused the doctors of withholding the body for two hours. Police reached after receiving information, investigation begins Following the woman's death, chaos broke out at the hospital. On receiving the information, Madiyaon police station in-charge Alok Rao reached the scene with a police team and calmed the family members.
