stories.title: BMW worth ₹2.86 crore sold in Lucknow on Dhanteras:4 cars cross ₹2 crore; Mercedes, Audi sell 100+ units each
stories.summary: Luxury car purchases in Lucknow saw a major spending spree this Dhanteras. Around 2,500 cars were sold in the city between 20 October and 6 November. These included four cars priced at more than ₹2 crore and 20 cars priced above ₹1 crore. The most expensive car, a BMW X6, was sold for ₹2.86 crore. The on-road price of the BMW i7 is as high as ₹2.80 crore. During this period, demand for electric vehicles also rose sharply alongside luxury cars. Mercedes and Audi cars were also in high demand. Around 45 cars were delivered at BMW showrooms, while 15 MG Majestor vehicles and between 80 and 100 MG Windsor vehicles were sold. 3 pictures of luxury cars... Customers opened their wallets for cars worth crores This festive season, the luxury car market in Lucknow saw strong interest in cars worth crores. Customers bought cars worth crores of rupees on Dhanteras this year. Twenty cars priced above ₹1 crore were sold. This clearly shows that the luxury car market in the city is continuing to expand. Large business owners, industrialists and customers in the premium segment are showing a preference for expensive cars. BMW X6 has an on-road price of ₹2.86 crore Around 45 cars were delivered at BMW's showroom in Chinhat during this festive season. According to the showroom's marketing head, Parampreet Kaur, bookings increased significantly this year compared with last year. Cars from BMW's MINI brand also received a good response from customers. According to information from the showroom, the BMW X6 has an ex-showroom price of ₹1.77 crore and an on-road price of around ₹2.86 crore. The BMW i7 has an ex-showroom price of ₹2.65 crore and an on-road price of around ₹2.80 crore. The BMW M4 has an ex-showroom price of ₹1.10 crore and an on-road price of around ₹1.30 crore. Meanwhile, the BMW i5 has an ex-showroom price of ₹79.60 lakh and an on-road price of around ₹84 lakh. Pictures of people who arrived to buy the cars... Demand for cars such as the M2 and M40i as well According to Parampreet Kaur, models such as the BMW M2, M4 and M40i were in demand among ultra-luxury and performance cars. Three to four ultra-luxury cars were delivered around Dhanteras. Around 45 cars were handed over to customers at BMW showrooms during this festive season. These included SUVs, sedans and electric models. She said that compared with last year, demand for BMW cars had increased this year not only in Lucknow but also in Agra and Kanpur. Customers buying luxury cars are no longer limited to petrol models and are also showing interest in electric cars. Electric cars becoming the preferred choice of doctors and business owners The biggest change in the luxury car market is visible in customers' preferences. According to Parampreet Kaur, doctors, clinic operators and business owners who travel daily within the city are prioritising electric cars. However, demand for petrol cars remains strong for long-distance travel and other requirements. BMW's electric portfolio is receiving a good response for the i5. Its on-road price is around ₹84 lakh. Customers are now showing a growing preference for environmentally friendly mobility alongside luxury. 15 MG Majestor deliveries worth ₹54 lakh, Windsor sales reach 100 Premium and electric vehicles also recorded good sales at the MG showroom this Dhanteras. According to Abdul Rahman, around 15 units of the company's premium SUV, the Majestor, were delivered. Its ex-showroom price starts at around ₹46 lakh, while the on-road price is approximately ₹54 lakh. Demand for the MG Windsor was the highest in the electric vehicle segment. Around 80 to 100 Windsor cars were sold during this festive season, with an average ticket size of around ₹20 lakh. Meanwhile, MG's new electric model, the Tomahawk, received more than 300 bookings. However, deliveries could not be made for all the bookings due to a supply shortage. Customers shifted from petrol and diesel to electric and hybrid vehicles According to Abdul Rahman, the electric vehicle market has undergone a major transformation over the past five to six years. EVs previously accounted for a very small share, but demand for them is now steadily increasing. In addition to petrol and diesel vehicles, customers are also considering electric, hybrid and CNG options. He said customers are no longer making purchases based solely on a vehicle's price, but are also prioritising features, running costs and better technology. This is why demand for electric cars is rising in the premium segment. Mercedes-Benz and Audi also sold more than 100 units In Lucknow's luxury car market, demand remained strong for brands such as Mercedes-Benz, Audi, Volvo and Jaguar Land Rover, besides BMW. According to available market data, Mercedes-Benz and Audi sold more than 100 units each. Expensive models such as the Audi RS7 and RSQ8 were also among customers' choices. SUVs and premium cars dominated the automobile market this time. When buying a car, customers are now considering not just the price and mileage, but also the EMI, maintenance, safety, charging facilities and resale value.

stories.title: 3 killed as truck rams bus carrying 50 passengers:Bus was travelling from Delhi to Kushinagar; victims were heading home for Diwali
stories.summary: A bus and truck collided in Kushinagar early on Saturday, killing three passengers and injuring six others. The passengers were travelling to their respective homes for Diwali and Chhath Puja. The collision was so severe that the front of the bus was completely mangled. People seated at the front broke through the windscreen and fell onto the road. Police reached the spot after receiving information from passers-by and pulled the passengers out. The passengers were taken by ambulance to Tamkuhiraj CHC, where doctors declared three of them dead. The accident occurred near Labania village in the Patherwa police station area. According to the police, the bus was travelling from Anand Vihar in Delhi to Muzaffarpur. There were 50 people on board. Two killed after speeding vehicle collides with sleeper bus Shiva Travels' AC sleeper bus had departed from Anand Vihar at 1.30 pm on Friday. Dharmendra, a resident of Kamalpura village in the Paru police station area of Muzaffarpur, Bihar, said he and other passengers were asleep when the accident occurred. More than 60 people were travelling on the bus. At around 4.30 am, they suddenly felt a strong jolt. Several passengers fell from their seats, triggering panic and screams inside the bus. When they stepped outside, they saw that the bus had been hit on its left side. A young girl and a man had died on the spot. According to the police, the deceased girl was identified as three-year-old Nandini, daughter of Pawan, a resident of Taryal Chhiram village under the Taraya Sujan police station area of Kushinagar. Her father, Pawan, was also injured in the accident. The identity of the second victim, a man aged around 40, is yet to be established.

stories.title: Inspector and CO jailed for 20 years for gang-raping woman:Victim was two-and-a-half months pregnant; had gone to Saharanpur to secure her husband's release
stories.summary: A court has sentenced a retired Deputy SP (CO) and an inspector to 20 years each for gang-raping a two-and-a-half-month pregnant woman at a police station in Saharanpur. The court sent both convicts to jail. They were seen hiding their faces with gamchas and towels. The case dates back to 2015. The police had sent the woman's husband to jail in a case. The woman alleged that her husband had been falsely implicated. She had gone to the police station to seek information about her husband and ask for help. During this time, the then station house officer, Brajmohan Yadav, and Inspector Vegpal Singh gang-raped her. Brajmohan Yadav was later promoted to Deputy SP and retired from that post. The woman has finally received justice after a legal battle that lasted around 11 years and three months. Read the full story now Lawyer says investigating agencies had given them a clean chit Advocate Rajeev Tomar said that on 6 August 2015, the then SHO Brajmohan Yadav, SI Vegpal Singh, police officer Pankaj Dhama and a constable gang-raped a woman from Deoband in the police station's government quarters. The victim received no hearing anywhere after the incident, and even her FIR was not registered. She then approached the High Court. A case was registered and the investigation was handed over to the CBCID on the High Court's orders. However, the investigating agency gave the accused a clean chit and filed a final report. Rajiv Tomar said a protest petition was filed against this. The court then summoned the accused again. The trial was first heard in the CJM court and then in the fast-track court. The court had convicted both accused on 5 November. After hearing arguments on the quantum of sentence on Friday, it sentenced both to 20 years' imprisonment and fined each ₹1 lakh under Section 376D. They were also sentenced to five years' imprisonment and fined ₹20,000 under Section 506 of the IPC. The advocate said the court considered the victim's statement and the testimony of her husband's sister important. The sister-in-law was an eyewitness to the incident. Victim said: "I had gone to the police station to get information about my husband; the policemen gang-raped me there" The survivor said she was a resident of Deoband. On 6 August 2015, police personnel had picked up her husband in a false case. She had gone to the police station with her sister-in-law to seek information about him and ask for help. There, a constable said that the outpost in-charge was calling them. Pankaj Dhama then took her and her sister-in-law to the police station. According to the survivor, Brijmohan Yadav, Pankaj Dhama, a revenue official and a constable gang-raped her in the police station's station house officer's room behind the station. The survivor alleged that she was attacked during her fight for justice and that false cases were also registered against her husband. She demanded an impartial investigation into all these cases so that she could receive complete justice. Outpost in-charge claimed he was mentally ill In the case, outpost in-charge Pankaj Dhama had told the court that he was mentally ill. He had presented several claims in this regard. Therefore, proceedings could not be initiated against him. Meanwhile, no hearing was held against the constable either because his identity could not be established and he could not be traced. Both convicts had previously been jailed Both retired police personnel had previously been jailed in this case. They were later granted bail by the High Court and the Supreme Court. After the court sentenced them, both were sent back to jail. The victim's lawyer alleged that the woman and her husband were subjected to continuous pressure during their struggle for justice. They were also accused of being assaulted and of attempts being made to cause an accident. Some cases have also been registered against the victim and her husband at Deoband police station, and are still pending trial.

stories.title: Fire breaks out at an RO shop in Gorakhpur:Triggering panic; electronic goods gutted, fire brigade brings blaze under control
stories.summary: A fire broke out at an RO shop in the Tiwari Pur police station area of Gorakhpur late on Friday night, causing panic. Nearby shopkeepers kept trying to douse the flames by throwing water with buckets. Police and fire brigade personnel arrived after receiving the information. After around 45 minutes of arduous efforts, the fire was brought under control. No one was killed in the incident. The electronic goods kept in the shop were reduced to ashes. The cause of the fire is being investigated. A sudden fire broke out at around 11 p.m. in the Shivanshi Enterprises (RO) shop in Suryavihar Colony. On receiving the information, Tiwari Pur police and the fire service reached the spot and brought the fire under control in time. At the time, people were shopping at the Dhanteras market at Suryavihar Crossing. As soon as the fire broke out, hundreds of people gathered along the roadside. The fire did not spread to the nearby shops or houses. The cause of the fire is being investigated. Swift action by the police and fire brigade prevented major damage.

Ferry service to operate on Ramgarh Tal:Tourists can travel from one bank to the other by paying fare
stories.summary: A water taxi service will soon be introduced at Ramgarh Tal alongside the existing boating facilities. Passengers will be able to travel from one side of the lake to the other for a fare of ₹50. Two floating jetties will also be built to support the service. The water taxi will operate as a ferry and will also be available for private parties at night. It will be a modern catamaran ferry boat, and the firm selected to operate the service has already received the work order. GDA Chief Engineer Kishan Singh said, “The Transport Department had provided financial assistance of ₹3.06 crore, including GST, for the project. The plan includes one ferry boat and two floating jetties.” He added, “The boat will be built in Gorakhpur with the help of technical experts and skilled workers. The firm aims to begin operations in around three months, while the project’s construction and operational work is scheduled to be completed within six months.” Air-conditioned cabin, seating for 50 and food facilities planned The ferry’s main feature will be its fully air-conditioned cabin. Built on a catamaran design, it will carry up to 50 passengers at a time. It will have comfortable seating and facilities for food and beverages. The ferry will run along a designated route from morning to evening. In the evening, it can also be hired for private events, offering families and tourists a different experience on the lake. Floating jetties will be built in front of the convention centre and near the RKBK bridge. These will have waiting rooms, ticket counters, a kitchen, a food preparation area and toilets. The ferry will follow a route covering Nauka Vihar Phase 1, the convention centre, RKBK, Sahara Estate, the zoo and Nauka Vihar Phase 2 before returning to its starting point. The service will give tourists an option to reach key attractions by lake instead of travelling by road. Zero-waste system planned to protect lake environment According to the chief engineer, environmental protection will be a key priority in operating the ferry and jetties. A zero-waste disposal system will be introduced, under which waste generated on the ferry will be collected, segregated and disposed of through authorised channels. No waste will be allowed to enter the lake. The selected firm will be permitted to operate the service for 10 years. The contract may be extended by another five years if the prescribed standards are maintained. The project is also expected to create local employment opportunities and help develop technical skills. GDA aims to develop Ramgarh Tal as a water transport hub GDA Vice-Chairman Abhinav Gopal said steps had been taken to develop Ramgarh Tal as a new centre for water transport alongside tourism. A ferry service will be introduced to make travel from one side of the lake to the other easier.

stories.title: ‘The slap was against the entire upper-caste community’:Youth in Prayagraj say they would have protested against any minister; ‘We will not tolerate pressure from those in power’
stories.summary: Rohit Tiwari, who raised the UGC issue, said, “We are opposing UGC. We protested in front of Keshav Prasad Maurya too, but his supporters slapped me. This is wrong. Anyone who works against our community will face opposition. We will not tolerate pressure from those in power.” Rohit Tiwari and Ankit Pandey said Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Maurya, who was the chief guest at a conference of the upper-caste community, should have expressed his views on UGC and issues concerning the community. However, he was talking politics, which prompted Rohit to speak up. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, the two said they were being silenced for raising community issues. They vowed to continue opposing UGC. Read the full conversation… First, read what the young men said... Rohit says: Deputy CM should clarify whether he supports or opposes UGC Rohit Tiwari, a resident of Koraon, is a lawyer by profession. He is also associated with the Brahmin Upper Caste Protection Organisation. Rohit said, “We have been opposing UGC since it was introduced. We protested in front of Keshav Prasad Maurya when he came here, but his supporters assaulted us. This is wrong. “Even if another minister had come here, we would have protested against him. Anyone who works against our community will face opposition. I wanted to know Keshav ji's views on UGC. He should clarify whether he supports or opposes it. “If the Deputy CM himself had spoken on UGC, there would have been no need for me to question him. He was talking about the BJP, SP and Congress, so I had to put forward my views.” We did not boycott the event because it was organised by Brahmins Rohit said, “We could have boycotted the event, but we did not because it was organised by Brahmins.” On being slapped, Rohit said, “They are representatives of Keshav ji. They want to become his close associates and gain something from him. “He did not just slap me; he slapped the entire community. He is also a Brahmin, but he has no concern for the community. He only cares about money and personal gains. He will stand wherever he gets benefits. “I am under no pressure and will not give in to anyone's pressure. I will continue to fight for my community until my last breath. I am fighting for the community, and today the entire upper-caste community across India is standing with me.” Ankit says: As chief guest, he should have spoken in the interest of the upper-caste community Ankit Pandey, also a resident of Koraon, said, “I work for society. Wherever the common people are treated unfairly, I stand against it. I live for the upper-caste community. If needed, I am ready to die for it. “Keshav Prasad Maurya was invited as the chief guest at the conference of the upper-caste community. He should have spoken about issues concerning the community. He was talking about what the BJP had done and how long it had been in power, but he did not say anything about the issues faced by the upper-caste community. “When no one spoke about the community's interests for a long time, we raised questions. We asked the Deputy CM to speak about the upper-caste community and clarify his views on UGC.” Rohit was slapped for raising questions Ankit alleged that before Keshav Maurya could respond, the administration and BJP workers misbehaved with them. BJP councillor Vinay Mishra slapped Rohit. “We will not tolerate this insult. Our fight will continue,” he said. Ankit said, “Keshav ji did not answer anything about UGC. He only asked us to remain silent. We felt he wanted us to leave the venue. And then the same thing happened to us. We will not tolerate pressure from the government, administration or those in power. “We had reached the venue with our entire team. Around 40% of our team members were from the Koraon Assembly constituency, while the remaining 60% had come from other areas. Despite this, we were treated this way.” They say: Will take the fight to a decisive stage Sankatmochan Tripathi, who was with Rohit Tiwari, said, “The hand raised against Rohit Tiwari was not just an insult to him personally. It was an insult to Ankit Pandey, Sankatmochan Tripathi and the entire upper-caste community. “Taking a pledge from the land of Prayagraj, we will take this fight to a decisive stage. Vinay Mishra will also have to answer to the community for his actions.” He also said they would take on Keshav Maurya politically. Now, here's what happened... A conference of prominent Brahmins was organised by the Rashtriya Parshuram Sena (Brahm Vahini) at Parade Ground on Sunday. Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya attended the event as the chief guest. He was addressing the gathering when two young men, Rohit Tiwari and Ankit Pandey, raised their hands and asked him to clarify his views on UGC. They asked whether Keshav Maurya supported or opposed UGC. In response, Maurya asked them to remain silent and sit down. He said, “Be quiet, sit down. I will speak about everything. I never stop myself from speaking on any issue.” This was followed by a commotion. Police began taking the two young men out of the venue. During this, BJP councillor Vinay Mishra slapped Rohit Tiwari. The police then took both men outside. The incident came into focus on Monday after a video of the confrontation surfaced.

stories.title: SP outperforms UP BJP on social media:Videos get 22 times more views, Instagram followers grow 5 times faster; will this impact the elections?
stories.summary: Whether the BJP will form the government in Uttar Pradesh for a third consecutive term or the Samajwadi Party (SP) will emerge stronger will only become clear after the elections. However, when it comes to social media engagement, measured by likes, shares and comments on posts, the SP is ahead of the BJP's Uttar Pradesh unit. The BJP has separate accounts for its national organisation and individual states across all social media platforms. The SP, on the other hand, has a single account on each platform for the entire country, rather than separate accounts for different states. As a result, the BJP's national account is ahead of the SP in both followers and engagement, but the BJP's Uttar Pradesh unit is lagging behind. The seriousness of the issue can be gauged from the fact that RSS joint general secretary Arun Kumar had to hold a meeting on the subject during his recent visit to Lucknow on 22 October. He was told that the Uttar Pradesh BJP's social media engagement had declined by 35% in 20 days. However, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath is far ahead of Akhilesh Yadav on social media. Over the past month, every Reel posted on Yogi's Instagram account received more than 1.5 million views. In comparison, Akhilesh's Reels averaged just 55,000 views. In today's UP Explainer, we will examine what rising and falling social media engagement means and how it could affect the 2027 Assembly elections… Now, let's understand what these figures mean… Question 1: How much will social media popularity influence the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections? Answer: Higher social media engagement for a political party does not necessarily mean that election results will favour it. There are several reasons for this. Amitabh Tiwari, founder of Vote Vibe, a political analysis organisation, says, “We often see accounts with 2.1 million followers on Instagram, but they may not even get 21 votes in an election.” During the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the Congress had higher social media engagement than the BJP. However, the results are there for everyone to see. Social media has a loophole: it is impossible to know where the engagement on an account is coming from. For instance, people in Delhi may extensively like and share SP content. This would increase the account's engagement, but it would have no direct impact on the Uttar Pradesh elections because those people cannot vote in the state. Similarly, if memes about Yogi, Modi or Akhilesh receive a lot of reach, they do not necessarily reveal voters' mood. People may be liking and sharing them simply for comedy and entertainment. According to Amitabh, people who support the government tend to watch traditional media, particularly television. In contrast, those opposed to the government are more active on social media. He says that if you look at the top 20 political channels on YouTube, not one supports the BJP or the right wing. Voters aged 18 to 35 use social media more frequently and account for 40% to 45% of the electorate. Meanwhile, voters above 35, who are more inclined to watch television and are considered more supportive of the government, account for 55% to 60% of the electorate. Question 2: If social media does not directly affect election results, why do political parties spend crores of rupees on it? Answer: Although extensive social media reach may not directly translate into votes, it helps parties mobilise their workers and counter the narratives promoted by their opponents. Today, being digitally invisible can mean being politically irrelevant. There are deeper psychological and strategic reasons behind this. Social media is not just a means of publicity; it is one of the fastest tools for setting the narrative. It allows parties to communicate their message directly to the public. A party with extensive social media reach can create the impression that “the wind is blowing in its favour”. Perception matters greatly in politics because many neutral voters tend to gravitate towards the party they believe is likely to win. Seeing their party dominate social media also boosts the morale of party workers. By spending crores of rupees, parties build databases that help them understand voters' likes and dislikes. They then run targeted social media campaigns based on caste, age and location. For instance, young people may be targeted with messages about employment, while women may be targeted with content on safety. This level of targeting is not possible through rallies alone. Question 3: Why has the decline in the Uttar Pradesh BJP's social media reach become such a major issue that the RSS had to intervene? Answer: The narrative that the Constitution was under threat harmed the BJP during the Lok Sabha elections. The RSS believes that if the BJP falls behind on social media, the Opposition could succeed in shaping the narrative among young and first-time voters. Political analyst Siddharth Kalhans says the BJP pioneered the use of social media to shape political narratives in India during the 2014 Lok Sabha elections. For a long time, no other party came close to matching its influence. However, from 2023–24 onwards, the social media presence of other parties and leaders also began to grow. The BJP's IT cell strategy, which relies on platforms such as Facebook and WhatsApp groups, is now becoming outdated. Generation Z is more active on Instagram. The Uttar Pradesh BJP has not been equally successful in adapting to new algorithms and understanding young people's preferences. As a result, its reach has declined. The RSS intervened not merely to improve social media performance but also to address a broader sense of organisational inertia. The Uttar Pradesh BJP had not formed its regional social media teams for a long time. The teams were announced just hours after the joint general secretary's meeting. According to Siddharth, the RSS views social media not simply in terms of likes and views but as a measure of organisational preparedness. A decline in digital reach may indicate a lack of activity at the grassroots level. The RSS stepped in to address the issue before it worsened.

stories.title: How will BJP resolve UGC row ahead of UP elections?:RSS calls circular ‘unbalanced’; Vinod Tawde signals possible changes
stories.summary: The UGC issue could become an election issue in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Signs of this emerged from the ballot papers used in the Legislative Council (MLC) graduate constituency elections. Instead of voting for BJP candidates, voters wrote ‘UGC Roll Back’ next to their names and dropped the ballot papers into the ballot boxes. The message read: ‘Withdraw the UGC rules, then we will talk.’ The Election Commission rejected thousands of such ballot papers. However, the anger displayed by educated young voters sent a strong message to the BJP that it could face resentment among upper-caste voters in the Assembly elections. Following this, senior leaders of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and the BJP sprang into action. At the RSS executive committee meeting in Indore, the circular was described as ‘imbalanced’. The organisation called it a threat to ‘social unity’ and urged that strict steps be taken. Meanwhile, BJP state in-charge Vinod Tawde called for a permanent resolution to the controversy before the elections. The question is: how will the BJP resolve the dispute over the UGC’s ‘Equity Regulations 2026’ before elections in five states, including Uttar Pradesh? Read the report… According to BJP sources, the central government has already started working on the issue. The government is believed to be considering four steps to resolve the controversy before the Assembly elections in five states. First: Effective representation in the Supreme Court could be used to restore the previous system, ensuring a balance between the interests of upper-caste, backward-class and Dalit communities. Second: The central government could issue an order withdrawing the controversial UGC circular. Third: During the court proceedings, the government could argue that the new rules are impractical and allow them to be struck down. Fourth: The UGC could issue a new circular completely removing the controversial and imbalanced provisions. BJP MLA says upper-caste communities have the right to oppose UGC The latest controversy over the UGC came to the fore on 1 November, when the issue triggered a major uproar at an upper-caste and Brahmin conference at Parade Ground in Prayagraj. Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya attended the event as the chief guest. During his address, two young men from the upper-caste community raised their voices against the UGC rules and asked Keshav Prasad to clarify the party’s stand on the issue. The Deputy Chief Minister tried to calm them down and continued his speech. However, the matter did not end there. BJP councillor Vinay Mishra, who was present at the event, argued with the young men protesting against the rules and slapped one of them. The incident triggered widespread anger among attendees and young people at the conference. BJP MLA Harshvardhan Bajpai, who represents the Allahabad North constituency, reacted to the incident involving a councillor from his own party and to the opposition to the UGC rules. BJP trying to address resentment through ‘student dialogue’ sessions The BJP has deployed its youth wing, the Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM), to address the issue. The organisation is holding ‘student dialogue’ sessions at 294 universities and colleges across Uttar Pradesh. Discussions are being held on the theme ‘Democracy versus anarchy’. In the coming days, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and other senior BJP leaders are expected to visit university and college campuses to interact with young people. The aim is to ensure that the party retains the strong support it previously enjoyed among young voters. RSS acknowledges that new UGC rules pose a threat to ‘unity’ At the RSS’s three-day All India Executive Council meeting, which began in Indore on 2 November, office-bearers expressed concern over feedback received from Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand. The feedback indicated that a large section of society was unhappy with the UGC rules. The issue could also affect the Assembly elections following the MLC polls. At the meeting, the RSS emphasised three points: 1. Any steps taken by the government in the future must be balanced and inclusive of all sections of society. 2. The Supreme Court has stayed the UGC rules, so the government must consider both their legal and social implications. 3. Any new rules or circular must not undermine social unity and mutual harmony. Two days before the meeting, the RSS held a press briefing. Its all-India publicity chief, Sunil Ambekar, described the UGC circular as imbalanced. He said: “The RSS had informed the concerned authorities about this issue, following which the government and the UGC took note of it. The Supreme Court has stayed these regulations. Any further decision must be completely balanced so that society remains united.” Tawde signals a resolution The BJP’s state working committee meeting was held in Lucknow on 30 and 31 October. Party national general secretary and Uttar Pradesh in-charge Vinod Tawde said the controversy surrounding the UGC would be fully resolved before the election dates were announced. The party will address the confusion among upper-caste voters over the UGC issue. It will reach out to voters and hold discussions with them. Understanding the resentment On 13 January 2026, the UGC issued new regulations to prevent caste-based discrimination at universities across the country. Following protests, the Supreme Court stayed the regulations on 29 January. Concerns of upper-caste communities Clause 3(c) of the circular included only SC, ST and OBC students in its definition of caste-based harassment. Members of upper-caste communities argue that students from any social group can face harassment and that students from the general category should also be protected under the rules. The regulations directed institutions to take strict action within 24 hours of receiving a complaint. Students from upper-caste communities feared that they could face false allegations and action without a proper investigation, with no strong safeguards available to protect them. They also believed that the rules could lead to students from the general category being treated as potential offenders by default in educational institutions, affecting social harmony. Argument put forward by backward-class communities Students from OBC, Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe communities argue that they frequently face caste-based discrimination, taunts and unequal treatment at higher educational institutions. They believe that equality and a fair environment on campuses cannot be ensured without strict legal provisions and equity committees. According to them, the circular provides a concrete mechanism for reporting and seeking justice against any form of harassment or discrimination during their studies.

stories.title: NEET aspirant shoots herself dead in Prayagraj:Father is a retired engineer; family says she had cleared the entrance exam
stories.summary: An 18-year-old NEET aspirant, Ritu Sharma, died in Prayagraj on Monday evening. She had qualified for NEET. The results of the third round of counselling for the examination were announced on Monday, and her name was on the list. Despite this, the reason behind her taking this step remains unclear. Ritu’s father, Devraj Sharma, is a retired engineer with the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI). During initial questioning, the family told the police that Ritu had been under mental stress for some time. The police said the case was being investigated. The cause of death would be determined based on the post-mortem report and other findings. The incident took place in Trivenipuram, under the jurisdiction of Jhunsi police station. See some pictures related to the incident… Family moved from Ghazipur to Prayagraj six years ago Retired engineer Dr Devraj Sharma originally belongs to Ghazipur. Around six years ago, he had a house built in the Ganga Sector of Trivenipuram, under the jurisdiction of Jhunsi police station. His family comprises his wife and their twins, Ritu and Rishiraj. Rishiraj is currently living in Dehradun, where he is pursuing a BTech degree. ACP Arun Kumar Parashar said the student may have died by suicide during the night. She used to study throughout the night, go to sleep in the morning and wake up at around 2 or 3 pm. Today, when the door did not open, the family called out to Ritu, but received no response. They then broke a window to gain access. The family found Ritu lying dead on the floor, with blood spread all around her. A pistol was lying beside her. The ACP said that during the initial questioning, the family told the police that the student had been under mental stress for some time. However, they could not explain why they had not heard the gunshot. The ACP said the cause of death would be determined based on the post-mortem report and other findings. MBBS seat allotted at Sonbhadra Medical College Ritu completed her Class 10 education at DPS in Prayagraj in 2022 and Class 12 in 2024. She then began preparing for NEET. In the NEET exam held in 2026, she secured an All India Rank of 10,74,272. On Monday, she was allotted an MBBS seat at the government medical college in Sonbhadra under the EWS-Persons with Disabilities (EWPH) quota. Father owns two licensed firearms Ritu’s father, Dr Dev Raj Sharma, owns a .32-bore pistol and a .315-bore rifle. The firearms were issued all-India licences by the Ministry of Home Affairs and the East Siang district administration in Arunachal Pradesh. ACP Arun Parashar said Ritu had appeared for the NEET examination before as well. According to information provided by her parents and other family members, she was worried about the counselling results. She was also under stress because she had not secured her preferred outcome in the previous round of counselling.

stories.title: ‘OP Rajbhar is an incompetent minister, will take him on':Protest in Lucknow over panchayat elections; police dragged protesters away
stories.summary: A massive protest was held in Lucknow on Monday, demanding that panchayat elections be conducted in Uttar Pradesh. The protesters said, "Om Prakash Rajbhar is an incompetent minister. We will bring the government down brick by brick. The government is deliberately not holding the panchayat elections." During the protest, the protesters attempted to enter the State Election Commission office. When the police stopped them, a scuffle and heated exchange followed. The police then dragged the protesters and put them into a van. See 3 pictures... Protesters say 8 lakh candidates are waiting for the elections The protest was organised by the Panchayat Rights Association. It was attended by village heads, area panchayat members, district panchayat members and other panchayat representatives from across the state. They raised slogans against the government. Panchayat representative Anand Kumar said, "The term of the village heads ended on 26 May 2026. It was then extended by six months. That extended term is also due to end soon. The three-tier panchayat elections should therefore be held in the state as soon as possible." Nearly 13 crore people in the state's rural areas and 8 lakh prospective candidates are waiting for the election date. Anand Kumar said that if the government did not provide a written assurance, the panchayat representatives would intensify their agitation. After this, a campaign would also be launched to ensure the government's ouster. "We have been demanding elections from the government for a long time, but we are being ignored," he said. Protesters say OP Rajbhar is an incompetent minister The protesters said that Om Prakash Rajbhar is an incompetent minister. He does nothing. They also levelled serious allegations against Chief Minister Yogi, saying that he was not holding the elections. They said, "If the elections are not held soon, we will bring this government crashing down." Both the candidates and the villagers are troubled because the elections have not been held. Against another extension of the term The protesters said the current government was opposed to the Constitution. That is why, by disregarding the Constitution's basic spirit, it was not holding the panchayat elections on time. The elections were supposed to be held by 26 May. The term had ended. After this, the government granted a six-month extension. Now the government wants to grant another six-month extension, which we will not tolerate. Every person who believes in the Constitution is demanding that the elections be held on time.

stories.title: ₹8.5 lakh swindled on promise of helping woman get PM:: Loan fraudulently obtained in her name in Gorakhpur; FIR filed against three
stories.summary: A case of fraud has come to light in Gorakhpur after an unemployed woman was lured with the promise of securing her benefits under the Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Yojana. The accused got a loan of ₹8 lakh 50 thousand sanctioned in her name on the pretext of setting up an oil and spice-grinding machine. After that, instalment payments began to be deducted from the woman's account, but even after several months, she did not receive the machine. It was then that the victim realised she had been defrauded. On Sunday, an FIR was registered against three people at Cantt police station on the instructions of the SP City. The victim was questioned further on Monday. Police are searching for the accused. Here is the full case… The victim, Sadrun Nisha, a resident of Chaksa Hussain in Jamunahiya Bagh Tola, under Gorakhnath police station limits, said she had met Santosh Sonkar, a resident of Adhiyari Bagh in Tiwari­pur, in 2021. Santosh had misled her by saying that loans were being provided at a low interest rate under the Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Yojana. He promised to arrange a loan for the woman, citing his acquaintance with Ashutosh Kumar Srivastava, the then branch manager of Punjab National Bank (PNB), Mohaddipur. Believing him, the woman handed over her Aadhaar card, PAN card and electricity bill. After this, Santosh took the woman to the bank, got an account opened and had a loan of ₹8 lakh 50 thousand sanctioned in her name to set up a machine for extracting oil and grinding spices. ₹9,300 was to be deducted every month Bank manager Ashutosh Kumar Srivastava had told the woman that the loan amount would be sent to the machine-supplying firm, 'Shyam Trading Company' (Dharmshala Road, Golghar), and that she would receive the machine from there. Even after considerable time had passed and the machine had not arrived, Santosh Sonkar told the woman to continue paying the EMI of ₹9,300 every month, saying that she would receive the machine soon. The woman continued paying the instalments. Woman was also made to sign a blank cheque During this period, the accused, Santosh, also got the woman to sign a blank cheque on the pretext of arranging the money. When the machine did not arrive, the victim herself went to Shyam Trading Company, where the firm's owner told her that documents in their name had not been issued from there and that they would not be able to provide any machine. The woman then realised that she had been duped. Accused of preparing forged documents It is alleged that the then bank manager, currently posted at PNB Faizabad, Santosh Sonkar and the owner of Shyam Trading Company colluded to prepare forged documents and divided the entire loan amount among themselves. The bank manager released the loan amount without conducting any physical verification. When the victim asked Santosh Sonkar to return her money, he began abusing her and threatened to kill her, claiming to have high-level connections in the police. Police begin investigation Cantt police station in-charge Jitendra Singh said that, following the City SP's instructions, an FIR has been registered against three people. Police are carrying out further investigation and taking action.

stories.title: Meat-filled van seized in Lucknow, VHP creates ruckus:Meat found in 7 plastic sacks; 6 samples sent to lab for testing
stories.summary: A van loaded with meat was intercepted in Lucknow on Monday. Workers of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad and Bajrang Dal created a commotion, alleging that the van was carrying prohibited meat. They demanded action against the four named accused. Police have registered a case against four people. The meat was packed in seven plastic sacks inside the van. A veterinary department doctor who reached the spot after receiving the information sent six pieces of meat to a laboratory for examination. The case concerns the area under Rahimabad police station. See two photographs... Read the full story... Caught near the railway crossing; had brought it from Malihabad Bhupendra Arkvanshi, a Ruseena resident and department minister of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad and Bajrang Dal, said he was travelling to Rahimabad at 8:30 a.m. on Monday for organisational work. During the journey, he received information that three unidentified people were carrying suspected meat in a white-and-silver van. After receiving the information, he reached the area near the Rahimabad railway crossing with his associates. He said that when they spotted the van, they stopped it and tried to make inquiries. It is alleged that a large quantity of meat was stored in seven plastic sacks inside the van. He then informed the police about the matter. Two companions fled after seeing the police The van driver, Mohammed Faizul, is alleged to be a resident of Tikra Barar in Sandila, Hardoi district. During questioning, the driver said that they were bringing meat from Irshad's place in Chaudharana, Malihabad town. Two companions, Rizwan and Islam, were following them on a motorcycle. They fled the spot after seeing the police. Could not produce any valid documents for the meat After receiving the information, police reached the spot and took the Omni van into custody. They called Rahimabad veterinary officer Neeraj Kumar and had samples of the meat collected. The veterinary officer said six samples had been sent to the laboratory. It will be confirmed which animal the meat came from only after the laboratory report is received. One and a half quintals of meat destroyed and buried Malihabad Inspector Surendra Mishra said Irshad, a resident of Chaudhrana, cuts and sells buffalo meat in the town. Around 15 kg of meat was found at the spot. Irshad and the other accused are being traced. The remaining one and a half quintals of meat was destroyed and buried. Rahimabad Inspector Arun Kumar Trigunayak said that, based on the complaint received, a case had been registered under serious charges against the accused driver Faizul, Irshad, Rizwan and Islam. The accused driver Faizul has been taken into custody and is being questioned.

stories.title: Man arrested for snatching chain:Threw chilli powder into elderly man's eyes; accused caught under under-construction Green Corridor bridge
stories.summary: Police arrested an accused on Monday in connection with the robbery of a gold chain after chilli powder was thrown into an elderly man's eyes in Wazirganj, Lucknow. The accused had carried out the crime with an accomplice on 26 October. Police recovered pieces of the stolen gold chain from his possession. According to police, Jawahar Nagar resident Ashish Kumar Verma lodged a case at Wazirganj police station on 26 October. He said that two unidentified youths had thrown chilli powder into his father's eyes and fled after snatching the gold chain from his neck. Police registered an FIR and began searching for the accused. Acting on an informant's tip-off, a police team arrested Khushal Kashyap, alias Tushar, alias Shooter (19), a resident of a hut in Madeyganj on Mohan Making Road, near the railway line close to the fruit market beneath the under-construction Green Corridor bridge, on Monday. Committed the crime after falling into bad company During questioning, the accused said he became involved in the crime after falling in with the wrong crowd. According to the police, pieces of the stolen chain were recovered from his possession. Further legal action is being taken in the case.

stories.title: Maulana says BJP govt’s return will bring back bulldozers:Alleges rioters cut open pregnant women’s stomachs during Gujarat riots
stories.summary: Maulana Jargis Ansari of Etawah, who had called Lord Krishna a namazi, has once again made an inflammatory statement. Without naming Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, the Maulana said, "Under no circumstances should this government be formed again. If this government is formed again, Muslims' homes will be set on fire and bulldozers will be deployed." Referring to the case registered in Lucknow four months ago, the Maulana said, "At that time, we started receiving calls from Bihar: 'Maulana sahib, he is finished now. Like Abdullah Salim, the Maulana's back will also be bent.' But because of those Cockroach people (Cockroach Janata Party), we received some relief. They started staging a protest at Jantar Mantar, so our news was suppressed. Everything was over. We are aware." Maulana says children were killed by repeatedly stabbing them with tridents The Maulana said, "A riot took place in Gujarat in 2002. On one side, shops were set on fire, houses were burnt, women were dishonoured after people broke into homes, and their honour was violated. The atmosphere of fear was such that pregnant women had their stomachs ripped open on Gujarat's soil, their babies were taken out and those children were not spared either. The children were also killed by repeatedly stabbing them with tridents." Even today, an atmosphere of fear comes over us and passes by. I do not know what will happen if this government comes back to power again-our homes will be set on fire, bulldozers will be deployed and our houses will be demolished. Maulana called on Muslims to demonstrate unity The Maulana said, "When elections come around, there is an atmosphere of fear, but even at that time we remain fragmented and divided. We lack unity, we do not stand together on one platform, and then the same thing happens: someone else takes advantage of our wrong decisions, after which that atmosphere passes through our midst." Referring to Palestine, the Maulana said, "Just look at the Muslims there-the atmosphere of fear remains with them 24 hours a day. When night falls, they do not imagine waking up alive in the morning because they cannot be sure that they will wake up alive." Yusuf Pathan targeted, said BJP gifted him land Without naming cricketer Yusuf Pathan, the Maulana said, "Let me give you an example-it may sound a little bitter, and if anyone is his fan, they may feel offended. There was a Muslim MP in Bengal who had been brought from Gujarat. You understand, don't you?" And just look at how an atmosphere of mild fear emerged. When Bengal was lost, seized or looted-whatever the circumstances may have been. And just look at how that man, too, was swept along in the same direction as the prevailing wind. The land over which there had been a dispute for years was handed over to him. In a way, the land was gifted to him by the very side in whose direction he had been swept. He got the land. Yusuf Pathan Got Land Worth ₹20 Crore for ₹5.5 Crore The Gujarat government approved the allotment of a 978-square-metre plot in Vadodara to MP Yusuf Pathan around two weeks ago. Its total value is said to be ₹20.53 crore. Of this, 500 square metres will be provided free of cost, valued at ₹10.50 crore. For the remaining 478 square metres, 55% of the stipulated price-around ₹5.52 crore-will have to be paid. The necessary orders have been issued to the municipal corporation in this regard. The municipal commissioner has placed the plot allotment proposal before the standing committee for approval. However, final approval is still pending for the ownership rights to the plot to be transferred. The Gujarat government and Yusuf Pathan had been involved in a dispute over this land for 14 years. Yusuf Pathan had left the Trinamool Congress (TMC) and joined the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) on 14 June. It was claimed that 19 other TMC MPs had also left the party with him. stories.title: Former cricketer Sehwag tours Kashi:Visits Baba Vishwanath and says, "It is a privilege to go wherever Mahadev calls you"
stories.summary: Former Indian cricket team player Virender Sehwag arrived in the holy city of Kashi on Monday. He visited the Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple, had darshan of Baba Vishwanath and performed the prescribed rituals. Sharing pictures from his visit to Kashi on social media, Sehwag wrote, "When Mahadev calls you, going there is a blessing in itself." Wore a cap and mask and moved around like an ordinary devotee Sehwag roamed the lanes of Banaras disguised as an ordinary devotee, wearing a cap and a mask. No one recognised him during this time. He also visited and worshipped at several temples in Varanasi. At the Kashi Vishwanath Temple, he sat and worshipped Lord Shiva for around half an hour. He chanted "Om Namah Shivaya". He walked 1 km from Chowk police station to the temple's Gate No. 4. India's first triple century was scored in Multan Virender Sehwag is regarded as one of international cricket's most aggressive batsmen. Known as the 'Nawab of Najafgarh' and the 'Sultan of Multan', Sehwag carved out a distinct identity with his explosive batting. His 'watch the ball, hit the ball' style changed the way opening batsmen approached Test cricket. Sehwag made his ODI debut in 1999 and his Test debut in 2001. He began his Test career with a century against South Africa. In March 2004, he became the first Indian batsman to score a triple century in Test cricket after making 309 runs in Multan, Pakistan. He began to be called the 'Sultan of Multan' after this innings. Set a record by scoring 319 runs off 278 balls In the 2008 Chennai Test against South Africa, Sehwag scored 319 runs off 278 balls. It was the fastest triple century in Test cricket history. He is among the select group of batsmen in the world to have scored two triple centuries in Test cricket. Sehwag also set several records in ODI cricket. In December 2011, he became the second batsman to score a double century in ODIs after making 219 runs against the West Indies in Indore. His aggressive batting helped the Indian team secure several memorable victories. From the Arjuna Award to the Padma Shri and ICC Hall of Fame Sehwag was named Wisden Leading Cricketer in the World twice in a row, in 2008 and 2009. In 2010, he received the ICC Test Player of the Year award. The Government of India honoured him with the Arjuna Award in 2002 and the Padma Shri in 2010. He was inducted into the ICC Hall of Fame in 2023. In October 2015, Sehwag announced his retirement from all formats of international and competitive cricket.

stories.title: Ruckus at Brahmin conference as Keshav is interrupted:Asked to speak on UGC, Deputy CM says, ‘Keep quiet’; councillor slaps a man
stories.summary: A ruckus broke out during Deputy CM Keshav Maurya’s speech at a conference of prominent Brahmins in Prayagraj. Maurya was addressing the gathering when two young men raised their hands and said, “Keshav ji, please say something about the UGC issue as well.” The Deputy CM became angry and replied, “Keep quiet, come on. I will speak about everything. I never hold back from saying anything.” The police then detained both young men. BJP councillor Vinay Mishra slapped one of them. As the dispute escalated, the police took both young men out of the venue. The incident took place at Parade Ground on Sunday, and a video of it surfaced on Monday. The conference was organised by the Rashtriya Parshuram Sena (Brahm Vahini). The young men have been identified as Rohit Tiwari and Ankit Pandey. Both are residents of Koraon in Prayagraj. See 2 pictures- Young man says, ‘I am in the BJP. If I don’t ask questions now, when will I?’ The video shows Keshav Maurya listing the government’s achievements while speaking about preparations for the Magh Mela, which is held at the Sangam. Meanwhile, two young men standing near the stage raised their hands. They asked, “Keshav ji, will you say something about the UGC issue as well?” Police personnel tried to stop the two men from speaking, but they refused to back down. They repeatedly demanded that the UGC issue be addressed. During this, Vinay Mishra, a councillor from Allapur, asked the two young men why they were asking questions. One of them replied, “I am in the BJP. If I don’t ask him questions now, when will I?” Meanwhile, councillor Vinay Mishra slapped one of the young men. Youth who questioned deputy CM says, ‘There is nothing wrong with asking questions’ Rohit Tiwari, who questioned the Deputy CM, released a video and said, “A Prabuddh Mahakumbh was organised in Prayagraj. My elder brother, Vimal Tiwari, organised the event. During his speech, Keshav Prasad Maurya was talking about the BJP, SP and Congress. I told him, ‘Keshav ji, this society, stage and event belong to us. So please speak about our community.’ We have not come here to listen to discussions about the BJP, SP and Congress. We have come to know what your vision is for us. What does your government think about our community, and what does it want to do for us? I had only asked him to speak about our community. After that, 40–50 police personnel came to detain me and surrounded me from all sides. Meanwhile, a local councillor slapped me.” BJP MLA opposes slapping of youth BJP MLA Harshvardhan Vajpayee, who represents the Allahabad North constituency, supported the questions raised by the young men and opposed the slapping of Rohit Tiwari. He said, “Every Brahmin and member of the upper castes has the right to oppose the UGC. Those who resorted to violence against members of their own community yesterday to score brownie points should know that no one names their child Vibhishan.”

stories.title: Yogi says SP supporters and butchers should mourn at home:Calls Samajwadi Party a curse on UP; IAS officer Durga Shakti presents him with a trident
stories.summary: In Gonda, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath targeted the Samajwadi Party and said, "The Samajwadi Party is a curse for Uttar Pradesh. Whenever it has come to power, it has wreaked havoc. Riots took place under its rule, curfews were imposed, and the safety of daughters-in-law and daughters was compromised. SP workers and butchers used to oppose Durga Puja. This time, I said that anyone seeking permission to install an idol should be granted it. If any SP worker or butcher has a problem, they should mourn at home." On Monday, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for 69 projects worth ₹520.83 crore in Gonda. He also distributed sanction certificates to beneficiaries of various schemes. Divisional Commissioner Durga Shakti Nagpal presented him with a trident while welcoming him. Yogi said, "During the Samajwadi Party government, rioters were invited to their homes and honoured. Now, under the BJP's double-engine government, if anyone causes a riot, we will teach them such a lesson that several generations will remember it." Read the 10 key points from Yogi's speech... 1. The SP is a curse on Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi said, "The land that showed the world the light was itself left in darkness. Development remained out of reach. Young people became unemployed and people were dying of hunger. The biggest scam also took place under the SP government. The SP is a curse on Uttar Pradesh. Whenever it came to power, it brought devastation." 2. SP members and butchers used to oppose Durga Puja The CM said, "Under the Samajwadi Party government, the pandals of Goddess Durga in Devipatan had been turned into a subject of controversy. People were not even allowed to offer prayers. If someone worshipped Goddess Durga at home in Gonda, an SP supporter or a butcher would object. When the person submitted an application, the SP government sitting in Lucknow would ban the worship. These people did not allow Kanwar yatras to be taken out and did not allow festivals to be celebrated either." 3. If idols are a problem, mourn at home Yogi said, "This Navratri, 67,000 idols were installed in Gonda alone. I had told the Gonda administration that no permission was needed to install idols. Anyone who wanted to keep an idol at home should be allowed to do so. If this troubles an SP supporter or a butcher, they should mourn at home. They should not trouble anyone else." 4. We showered Ram devotees with flowers, not bullets The Chief Minister said, "On 2 November 1990, during the Ram Janmabhoomi movement in Ayodhya, Ram devotees were shot at under the government led by the then Chief Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav. We showered Ram devotees with flowers, not bullets, and built the Ram temple in Ayodhya. We also developed Ayodhya." 5. UP is now free of riots and curfews Yogi said, "The largest Kanwar Yatra takes place between Ghaziabad and Haridwar. This time, 4.5 crore devotees took part in the pilgrimage. The Samajwadi Party used to stop it, saying that riots would break out. There will be no riots during our tenure. You invite rioters to your residence and honour them. That is why they dared to riot. If anyone riots under the BJP's double-engine government, we will teach them such a lesson that several generations will remember it. UP is now free of curfews and riots." 6. Earlier, development meant only Saifai He said, "Earlier, development meant only Saifai. Today, development means all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh. There is no discrimination in development now. Electricity will be available not only in Rampur and Saifai, but also in Gonda and Balrampur. Ration and cooking gas are no longer distributed based on a person's appearance. Every poor and needy person will receive gas. Before Diwali, we are going to provide one full cooking gas cylinder free of cost." 7. Uttar Pradesh became the growth engine of the country's economy The CM said, "Development will no longer move at a snail's pace. We will accelerate it because this speed is the basis of our progress. As a result, Uttar Pradesh is no longer a BIMARU state; it has become the growth engine of the country's economy. Uttar Pradesh is no longer among the bottom five states. In terms of the economy, it is counted among the top three states." 8. Breach security and jail or hell awaits Yogi said, "No one can now compromise the security of daughters and traders. If a development project comes to Gonda, no one can hijack it along the way. This is because we have consigned the mafia to the dust. Firm arrangements have been made to ensure the security of daughters and traders. If anyone breaches security, they will either go to jail or to hell." 9. SP-Congress are parties that bring in criminals The CM said, "The BJP stands for faith. It is a party that respects your faith and brings change to your life. The SP and Congress are parties that stand for crime and bringing in criminals. They bring in criminals; we bring change. We provide funds for every site associated with your faith." 10. Win medals, take up posts He said, "Employment opportunities are open for young people. I told Akhilesh recently that if he knows how to count, he should count and tell us. We will give government appointment letters to 1 lakh young people in the next six months." “There are schemes for sportspersons as well. We say, ‘Win medals for the country and take up posts’. Those who have won medals have been made officers. When Agniveers return after four years of service, we are going to provide them with 20 per cent reservation in various departments of the Uttar Pradesh government. They will not have to take any examination; there will be direct recruitment.”

stories.title: Employees seek euthanasia after eight years without pay:They announce an indefinite sit-in at Lucknow’s Eco Garden from 22 October; write to the President
stories.summary: Employees of Uttar Pradesh's primary agricultural cooperative societies (B-PACS) have sought the President's permission for collective euthanasia, citing years of unpaid salaries and financial hardship. Shailendra Tiwari, state president of the M-PACS Employees' Association, has sent a letter to the President in this regard. The employees have been staging an indefinite sit-in at Lucknow's Eco Garden since 22 October. They say that, because they have not received regular salaries for eight to 10 years, it has become difficult even to support their families and educate their children. The association alleges that after the agitation began, attempts were made to prevent employees in all 75 districts of the state from participating in the protest. Notices are being issued to employees involved in the agitation. Some have also faced action such as suspension and the filing of FIRs. The employees say they are being subjected to mental harassment despite holding a peaceful protest. Demand for salaries since 2018, three rounds of talks end inconclusively According to the union, the employees have been demanding regular salaries since 2018. Memoranda have been submitted to departmental officials several times in this regard. After a memorandum of demands was submitted on 7 September, talks were held at the departmental level on 21 September, 5 October and 29 October. Despite this, no concrete decision could be reached on arrangements for salary payments. The employees allege that each time they were given assurances and asked to call off the agitation, but their demands were not met. Questions raised over salary system in Cooperative Department Employees have accused the Cooperative Department of discrimination in its salary payment system. They say that other employees of the department are paid from the state treasury, while B-PACS employees have been kept outside the regular salary system by citing the Act. The employees ask why they are not being paid on time even after working for years. Appeal to the President to intervene on seven demands In a letter to the President, the employees have demanded the immediate payment of outstanding salaries and the implementation of a regular salary system. They have also appealed for a review of the FIRs and other punitive action against the protesters, a fair investigation into the notices and suspensions, an end to mental and financial harassment, amendments to the relevant Act, and directions to the Uttar Pradesh government to resolve the problem.

stories.title: Candidates in 68,500-teacher recruitment protest UP Assembly in Lucknow:Lie down and ring bells, clash with police; say they have been struggling for 8 years
stories.summary: Candidates for 68,500 assistant teacher posts surrounded the Legislative Assembly on Monday, demanding appointments in Lucknow. The candidates lay on the road and began ringing bells. Sloganeering and chaos continued for around 20 minutes. During this time, a scuffle broke out between the police and the protesters. The police carried away and dragged the candidates. The protesters continued chanting slogans such as, "What is the compulsion? This is theft of reservation," and "The Backward Classes Commission has acknowledged it; this is a reservation scam." The candidates accused the police of tearing their clothes and behaving indecently. See 3 pictures of the protest... 'Ministers and officials admitted irregularities in recruitment' Navin, who took part in the protest, said he had met Basic Education Minister Sandeep Singh and Secondary Education Minister Gulab Devi on 10 September. Several senior officials from the Basic and Secondary Education departments were also present at the meeting. Navin claims that both ministers and the officials admitted at the meeting that there had been irregularities in the recruitment process. He said, "When the State Backward Classes Commission and the National Commission for Backward Classes have also acknowledged the irregularities, ministers and officials in the government are accepting them too. Why, then, are we not being given appointments?" Candidates have been seeking jobs for 8 years Utkarsh Singh Patel, who came from Basti, said he had been seeking a job for the past eight years. He alleged that there had been large-scale irregularities related to reservation in the recruitment of 68,500 assistant teachers. The state and national Backward Classes Commissions have also directed that the rules be followed, but appointments have not been made so far. '8 years have passed in the hope of getting a job' Candidate Ashutosh said they demanded that the commission's orders be implemented. Recruitment was announced in 2018, and they applied at the time. Since then, 8 years have passed in the hope of getting a job. He said, "From the Chief Minister to the MLA, there is no door left that we have not approached to put forward our demand. We protested several times and made repeated appeals, but have still not received employment."

stories.title: Polytechnic student harassed in Gorakhpur:Man tries to snatch her phone and follows her to hostel over unrequited love
stories.summary: A case of molesting a polytechnic student and snatching her mobile phone in front of the Asuran police outpost in Gorakhpur's Shahpur area came to light on Saturday evening. It is alleged that a youth who had been harassing the student out of one-sided love molested her and snatched her mobile phone. When the student raised an alarm, the accused threw the phone and fled after seeing the crowd that gathered. The victim submitted a written complaint to Shahpur police along with her family members. Police are investigating the entire matter. Student studies while living in hostel The student, who is from a village in the Harpur Budhat area, is pursuing a polytechnic course while living in a hostel in Asuran. It is alleged that a youth from her village has been harassing her out of one-sided love and molesting her while she travelled to and from places. Troubled by this, the student had informed her family. Following the family's complaint, an FIR was registered against the accused at Harpur Budhat police station on 3 June. Young man traced her to the hostel After this, the student began living in the city to continue her studies. It is alleged that despite an FIR being registered, the young man continued searching for her. On Saturday evening, the student left the hostel to get photocopies of documents required for an online examination. After getting the photocopies at a shop opposite the Asuran police outpost, she was walking back. Meanwhile, the young man arrived on a Pulsar motorcycle and began harassing her. When the student protested, the accused snatched her mobile phone and tried to flee. She raised an alarm, prompting people nearby to gather. Seeing the crowd, the young man threw away the mobile phone and fled. Frightened by the incident, the student called her family and informed them. Some time later, she reached the Asuran police outpost with her father. She was told there that the site of the incident did not fall under its jurisdiction, but under the jurisdiction of the Kauwabagh police outpost. After she reached Kauwabagh, she was told to submit a written complaint at Shahpur police station. The victim has submitted a written complaint to the Shahpur police.

stories.title: ‘Akhilesh ji, stop carrying big brother’s flag’:Rajbhar says, 'Rahul will leave the country, and you will be left dealing with Swami Prasad'
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh government Cabinet Minister and Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP) national president Om Prakash Rajbhar has once again targeted Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav. Taking a dig at Rahul Gandhi, he advised Akhilesh to clarify his position instead of pursuing politics with the Congress. In a social media post, Rajbhar wrote, "Akhilesh Yadav ji, it seems you understood by evening what I said in the morning. How long will you continue doing politics under someone else's influence? You no longer need to fear Big Brother. This is the time-the right time." You never know when Rahul may leave for abroad He said that Akhilesh should at least stop carrying Big Brother's flag. Taking a dig at him, Rajbhar wrote that Rahul Gandhi would leave for Thailand, Vietnam or Mongolia again after holding a rally, while Akhilesh would have to negotiate with Swami Prasad Maurya here over seat-sharing. Referring to Swami Prasad Maurya, Rajbhar said that he gets photographed with Rahul Gandhi and goes around telling people what Akhilesh's standing is. He alleged that Akhilesh gave Swami Prasad full respect, but received only humiliation in return. The worker is disappointed every time Taking a dig at Akhilesh, the SBSP president said that his stature was declining day by day. Workers were waiting in hope that Akhilesh would make a big impact, but he turned out to be a damp squib. In the end, he asked Akhilesh to clarify his position and took another dig at him, saying that instead of doing so, he would keep making trips to Delhi. Dig at the war of words between Akhilesh and Swami Prasad Maurya OP Rajbhar was taking a dig at the ongoing war of words between SP chief Akhilesh Yadav and Swami Prasad Maurya. A war of words has broken out between Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav and former minister Swami Prasad Maurya over joining the INDIA alliance. Akhilesh said clearly on Friday that Swami Prasad Maurya was not part of his alliance. When asked about this, he said, "They cannot be included among our seats. Avoid them, ignore them." Swami Prasad Maurya hit back at Akhilesh Yadav's statement on 31 October. He said Akhilesh Yadav was not the INDIA alliance. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge played an important role in the alliance and took the final decisions. Maurya had said: Who is Akhilesh to give me a certificate? Swami Prasad Maurya said, "Akhilesh Yadav is not the INDIA alliance. Congress national president Mallikarjun Kharge has a role in the INDIA alliance, and the final decision rests with him. He is neither important nor influential. Who is he to give us a certificate?" Maurya said he had not spoken to Akhilesh Yadav. He had spoken to Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi and Congress state in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam. He questioned why, if Akhilesh Yadav was so capable, he would meet Rahul Gandhi instead of speaking to him.

stories.title: Dhirendra Shastri apologises with folded hands over ‘Krishna Tedhe’ remark:Had said ‘your Thakurji is 'Tedhe' at 3 places’; Mathura saints say Braj residents will not forgive him
stories.summary: Bageshwar Dham head Dhirendra Shastri has apologised with folded hands for his remark describing Lord Krishna as ‘crooked’. He said Lord Ram and Lord Krishna are one and there is no difference between them. His comment was not intended to create any division or discrimination. He apologised if his remarks had hurt anyone's sentiments. On October 29, during a Ram Katha in Karera, Shivpuri, Dhirendra Shastri had said, “Our Ram is straight, while your Krishna is crooked. Your Thakurji's head is crooked, his name is crooked, and even the way he walks and stands is crooked.” Saints in Mathura express anger over Dhirendra Shastri's remark Saints in Mathura had expressed anger over Dhirendra Shastri's statement. Dinesh Falhari Maharaj said that even Ravana's arrogance did not last forever and that Dhirendra Shastri should apologise. Sadhvi Indulekha and Pandit Rajesh Pathak also expressed displeasure, saying that people from Braj would not tolerate such remarks. Dhirendra Shastri says, ‘Your Lord bends his waist and even his head’ Pandit Dhirendra Shastri told devotees attending the Katha, “Just look at a single picture of your Thakurji. Look at how he sits... in different postures. Your Lord stands bent at three places, with one foot over the other, his waist bent and his head tilted in different ways, while playing the flute.” Comparing Lord Krishna with Lord Ram, he said, “Our Lord stands perfectly straight. His name is straight, his walk is straight, and even his appearance is straight. Your Lord's name is crooked, his walk is crooked, and he even stands crooked.” ‘Playing the flute is child's play, but shooting an arrow is not’ While comparing Lord Ram and Lord Krishna, Pandit Dhirendra Shastri also referred to playing the flute and shooting arrows. He said, “Playing the flute is child's play, but shooting an arrow is not.” He then told the devotees, “All those who worship Thakurji are present here. Today, you must be very happy.” Pointing towards a flute player performing at the event, he said, “Listen, what does your Thakurji do? Play the flute? Playing the flute is not a big deal.” Shastri says, ‘Artists here can also play the flute’ He said, “Grazing cows is child's play, but making monkeys dance is not. Playing the flute is not a big deal. Artists here can also play it. Look, he is playing it too.” He then asked the flute player to continue, and the musician played for a while. Pandit Dhirendra Shastri also asked devotees who worship Lord Ram to raise their hands. He said, “How many of you worship Ramji? Raise your hands. Yes! Today, you will be overjoyed.” He repeated that playing the flute was child's play, but shooting an arrow was not. ‘Grazing cows is child's play, but making monkeys dance is not’ Pandit Dhirendra Shastri also referred to Lord Krishna grazing cows and lifting a mountain. He said people would argue that their Lord grazed cows. Responding to this, he said anyone could graze cows. He sang, “Grazing cows is child's play, but making monkeys dance is not.” ‘Grazing cows is child’s play, but making monkeys dance is no game’ Pandit Dhirendra Shastri also referred to Lord Krishna grazing cows and lifting a mountain. He said people would argue that their God grazed cows. Responding to this, he said anyone could graze cows. Singing a line, he said, “Grazing cows is child’s play, but making monkeys dance is no game.” He then referred to Lord Krishna lifting Govardhan Hill and said, “You will say that your God can lift a mountain. Is that such a big deal? One of our Lord’s disciples blew away an entire mountain.” He was referring to Lord Ram’s devotee, Hanuman. At the end of his remarks, Dhirendra Shastri denied being opposed to Lord Krishna. He said, “This does not mean that we are against Thakur Ji.” Dhirendra Shastri says, ‘I said it out of love’ Dhirendra Shastri clarified his remarks. He said, “I said that Krishna Ji is crooked and our Ram Ji is straight. What is wrong with saying that? Thakur Ji is crooked, isn’t he? I said it in that spirit. Even my name includes Krishna. When you love someone deeply, you say such things to them. I said it out of love.” Referring to Lord Krishna lifting Govardhan mountain, he said, “You will say that your Lord lifts mountains. Is that such a big deal? A disciple of our Lord lifted an entire mountain and flew away.” He was referring to Lord Ram's devotee Hanuman. Supriya Shrinate says calling Thakurji ‘crooked’ is a sin Congress national spokesperson Supriya Shrinate said, “Was dividing people not enough that now they have started dividing their revered deities too?” She said Lord Ram is Maryada Purushottam (the ideal of righteousness), while Lord Krishna is a complete yogi. Both are incarnations of Lord Vishnu. Lord Ram incarnated in the Treta Yuga, while Lord Krishna appeared in the Dwapar Yuga. Both represent truth and justice. Calling Thakurji crooked is a sin.
