stories.summary: Uppal, 46, was taken into custody by authorities in Dubai on the basis of an Interpol Red Notice issued at the request of Indian investigating agencies, officials told PTI. The CBI and the ED are now coordinating efforts to secure his extradition to India. Investigators have also alleged that Uppal, like Chandrakar, secured a passport from Vanuatu, an island country in the South Pacific.

stories.title: Texas parents honor daughter’s rescuers through a foundation that has awarded 67 scholarships
stories.summary: Tragedy struck when 18-year-old student Kenli Riney died in a highway accident in Texas, with the Argote family making valiant attempts to save her. To commemorate her spirit, they founded the Kenli Foundation, which offers scholarships to young individuals showing courage and kindness. Additionally, they introduced the Argote Award Scholarship to recognize and reward the remarkable bravery of those who come to the aid of others.

stories.title: Texas court reopens Houston home ownership dispute after foreclosure and reverse mortgage
stories.summary: A Texas appeals court has reopened a lengthy dispute over home ownership in Houston, which has complicated legal issues. The case involves multiple foreclosures, reverse mortgages, and unclear ownership claims spanning twenty-five years. Key questions remain about the validity of a 2011 mortgage after a previous foreclosure occurred in 2001. This ruling requires lower courts to thoroughly examine competing ownership claims before making decisions.

stories.title: UN report finds huge gap in adaptation finance ahead of COP31
stories.summary: Developing nations require approximately $305 billion annually by 2035 for climate change adaptation efforts. Rich countries' collective pledge could only reach $85-120 billion each year by 2035. While current financial contributions are around $28.2-31.7 billion, this is still inadequate. UN Environment Programme emphasizes the urgent need for increased adaptation financing and overcoming institutional barriers. Action on climate adaptation is essential to mitigate worsening impacts from extreme weather events.

Ed Sheeran gets approval to restore six historic barns for private music archive and studios
stories.summary: Ed Sheeran has secured permission to renovate six barns on his Suffolk estate, intending to create a private music archive while preserving the barns' 19th-century charm. This thoughtful restoration seeks to minimize major changes to the structures, ensuring that the project also promotes local wildlife and biodiversity, showcasing Sheeran's dedication to his music, heritage, and the surrounding environment.

stories.summary: Union health minister JP Nadda accused the Congress party of opposing the Special Intensive Revision of voter lists. He alleged that their actions are aimed at protecting outsiders who support their political ambitions. Nadda criticized the Congress for undermining the credibility of the Election Commission when faced with electoral losses. He noted that the current electoral process includes Booth Level Officers facilitating voter registration door-to-door.

stories.summary: With Democrats gaining Congressional control, Indian-Americans are grappling with uncertainty regarding immigration rules and job opportunities. Heightened fears about H-1B visa restrictions and deportation have taken center stage. In addition, increasing discrimination and the prevailing political climate are altering feelings of identity among the community. New survey data reveals a trend towards favoring Democratic candidates, indicating that the outcomes of the midterms might significantly influence the Indian-American experience.

However, his newfound status is marred by legal issues stemming from a wedding altercation where he punched another guest, causing severe injuries that required surgery. Although he claimed self-defense, a jury dismissed his argument, leaving his future uncertain as he awaits sentencing on December 11.

Georgia court revives tenants' claims after mistaken 2022 apartment raid and detention

The court has reinstated accusations of assault and false imprisonment against the property owner, stemming from the officer's actions. This landmark decision may pave the way for heightened accountability in property management concerning tenant security.

stories.title: They couldn't read or write, now these African grandmothers are solar engineers bringing electricity to 75,000 homes
stories.summary: Rural women in several African countries are being trained as solar engineers through the Solar Mamas programme. The initiative aims to provide communities with access to electricity while empowering women with technical skills. Women have learned to assemble and maintain solar lighting systems, creating local expertise. Reports indicate that the programme has brought significant improvements to daily life in villages.

stories.summary: TRAI has introduced the Network Anubhav Platform to provide users with insights about internet speeds and network quality. This platform compiles user test data from MySpeed and MyCall applications, enhancing transparency for consumers. Telecom service providers can utilize this information for network optimization based on user feedback and metrics. The geospatial maps will categorize results by service provider and technology, aiding consumers in their analysis.

Paris Jackson asks court to move $600 million into Michael Jackson's trust 17 years after his death
stories.summary: In a legal move, Paris Jackson has petitioned the court for a $600 million transfer to the family trust. While the estate has generated significant income since Michael Jackson's passing, his children have yet to see the trust funded. Its executors cite unresolved tax matters as a barrier. Paris believes that as she and her brothers near their thirties, distributions should begin.

stories.summary: Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma criticized Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's proposal for a public debate with Prime Minister Modi. Sarma emphasized that such discussions should occur in Parliament, not publicly. He challenged Gandhi to raise various critical issues like Bofors and the Bhopal Gas Tragedy during parliamentary sessions. Rahul Gandhi had expressed a desire for a debate to address national connections and financial matters.

Since rescuing the last of the species in 1991 and breeding them to over 1,000 individuals, conservationists have created a safe habitat that shields them from invasive threats. Despite this success, the long-term survival of these snails remains uncertain, necessitating continuous monitoring and further breeding efforts.

stories.title: When London Bridge was rebuilt in Arizona, workers numbered granite stones before dismantling it
stories.summary: London Bridge has a storied past marked by numerous reconstructions due to various calamities. In a striking turn of events, the City of London sold the iconic bridge to American entrepreneur Robert McCulloch for $2.46 million in 1968. The bridge was carefully reassembled in Lake Havasu City, featuring a hollow core designed to accommodate modern traffic.

Historic US midterms: Black, Indigenous, Latina & LGBTQ leaders win key races
stories.summary: The 2026 US midterm elections have led to historic firsts in gubernatorial and Senate races across the nation. Notable victories include the first Black woman governor in US history and the first Native American woman governor. The election of Texas' first Latina governor and Florida's first Black governor also signify progress in representation. Additionally, Minnesota has elected its first woman governor, further enhancing diversity in leadership roles.

He tracked down over 60 poachers and followed a blood trail for 1.5 km: Meet Zorba, the dog who protected Assam’s rhinos
stories.summary: Zorba, a Belgian Malinois esteemed for his exemplary contributions to wildlife conservation in Assam, was instrumental in tracking more than 60 poachers within Kaziranga National Park. His remarkable ability to retrieve vital evidence and follow scent trails showcased the invaluable role of trained dogs in environmental protection. Honored for his unwavering service, Zorba passed away in November 2022, leaving a lasting impact on both his handlers and the conservation community.

stories.title: Washington man loses father's ranch over financial abuse; court upholds $166,698 divorce judgment
stories.summary: Calvin Evans Jr. had anticipated taking over his father's ranch in Washington, a significant piece of property at the center of his divorce. In the proceedings, Deborah Bunney secured $174,000 for community contributions towards the ranch. However, after being found to have financially abused his father, Evans's inheritance was revoked.

stories.title: In 1944, a US Navy serviceman stationed in the Pacific mailed his wife a coconut
stories.summary: In an extraordinary act of devotion during 1944, U.S. Navy serviceman Raymond sent a carved coconut to his beloved wife, Marie. This unique letter, mailed all the way from Hawaii, bore their names intertwined in a heart, symbolizing their unwavering love. Their enduring marriage of 53 years stands testament to a bond that grew deeper with time.

North Korea fires missiles hours after rejecting US accusations over Binance hack
stories.summary: North Korea recently fired multiple missiles towards its eastern waters, indicating rising tensions with South Korea and the US. This action followed North Korea's denial of involvement in a significant cryptocurrency hack attributed to its hackers by the FBI. Kim Yo Jong criticized US accusations as part of a hostile policy and refused dialogue until it changes.

stories.title: US couple finds live Civil War-era artillery shell in basement of newly bought home
stories.summary: A young couple in Pennsylvania discovered a live Civil War-era artillery shell while clearing out the basement of their newly purchased home in South Connellsville. The object was among belongings left behind by the previous owners. The couple alerted police, who contacted the Allegheny County Police Bomb Squad. Specialists confirmed the shell was live and removed it for proper disposal.

stories.title: A butterfly disappeared from Ontario in 1988 and has not been recorded there since
stories.summary: In an exciting conservation effort, scientists are set to reintroduce the frosted elfin butterfly to Ontario, a species that vanished nearly forty years ago. Adult butterflies and their eggs are being moved from New York for breeding in captivity before their release. The initial reintroduction is planned for spring 2027 in Port Rowan, where habitats have been carefully restored.

stories.title: A vampire burial: A Polish woman was buried with a sickle to stop her rising from the grave
stories.summary: Unveiled by time, Zosia's grave in Pień offers a glimpse into 17th century Polish traditions regarding death and the supernatural. Archaeologists found an iron sickle and a toe-bound padlock alongside her remains, suggesting efforts to prevent her from rising as a vampire. This peculiar burial practice hints at Zosia's affluent background, compelling researchers to dive deeper into her life and the cultural fears that shaped her final resting place.

stories.title: US poll results: Democrat Amy Acton defeats Ramaswamy, flips Ohio governor's office
stories.summary: Dr. Amy Acton has been elected as Ohio's first female governor after defeating Vivek Ramaswamy. This historic victory marks the first Democratic win in the state's governorship in two decades. Acton campaigned on healthcare and affordability while highlighting her challenging childhood. Ramaswamy faced significant backlash for a controversial ad featuring Acton's estranged mother. Acton enters office without prior elected experience amid significant political shifts in Ohio.

stories.summary: Keisha Lance Bottoms has been elected governor of Georgia after defeating Rick Jackson in the recent election. Her victory signifies a historic moment as she becomes the first Black woman to hold this position. Bottoms focused her campaign on economic issues, pledging to expand Medicaid and raise the minimum wage. Jackson's significant campaign spending did not prevent his defeat despite his attacks on Bottoms' record.

This change comes amid concerns over the possible decrease in qualifying scores for NEET-PG 2025. The commission is focused on preserving the integrity of medical examinations and has also suggested equitable salary structures for medical residents.

As their metal fins became visible, emergency services swiftly evacuated the area, setting up a 200-metre exclusion zone for safety. Identified as German explosives, the bombs were eventually neutralized in a controlled detonation, underscoring the historic shadows that still linger in various regions of Britain.

stories.title: MrBeast Funds Free School Lunches: Kansas teacher’s campaign sparks gift; families get relief
stories.summary: At Tonganoxie Middle School, agriculture teacher Beth Schartz took significant steps to address student lunch debt after a concerning incident involving unpaid lunch balances impacted a child. In a remarkable turn of events, YouTube sensation MrBeast stepped in, generously funding free lunches for the entire academic year. This initiative not only provided nourishing meals but also included free back-to-school clothing, positively impacting families and promoting inclusiveness in the school community.

stories.title: Trump jokes he'll move to Israel and become PM if Americans get 'tired' of him
stories.summary: In a lighthearted moment during a Fox News interview, Donald Trump playfully proposed his candidacy for the position of Israel's prime minister, citing a staggering 99 percent approval rating among Israelis. He went on to declare that by 2026, the US would cease its annual aid of $4 billion to Israel, sparking considerable debate over the implications for military support and relations, coinciding with the midterm elections unfolding in America.

stories.title: BJP, allies slam Neha Bora for 'anti-Hindu' remarks
stories.summary: Neha Bora of AISA has come under fire for her remarks about the Brahmanical system and temple safety. Her comments have been interpreted as reinforcing claims of anti-Hindu sentiments within Rahul Gandhi's ecosystem. BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia condemned her statements, accusing her of insulting priests and promoting divisive rhetoric. LJP chief Chirag Paswan urged Congress to reconsider its association with her and similar figures.

stories.title: Katy Perry faces opposition from more than 360 neighbours over proposed 110-acre California youth camp
stories.summary: Katy Perry’s proposed Gratitude Canyon youth camp in Goleta, California, is facing opposition from more than 360 neighbours. Residents have raised concerns about wildfire risks, traffic, noise and evacuation access. The singer’s Firework Foundation is defending the project, saying it will provide underserved children with opportunities to explore arts, nature and outdoor activities.

stories.title: Pennsylvania woman treated for breast cancer had rare lymphoma; court allows family's lawsuit
stories.summary: A Pennsylvania woman received breast cancer treatment for 13 months before doctors discovered she had a rare and aggressive lymphoma. She died in January 2019, and her family sued the treating oncologist, alleging that the delayed diagnosis reduced her chances of survival. After a trial court dismissed the case, the Pennsylvania Supreme Court ruled that a jury should hear the malpractice claim.

stories.title: Judge needn't face strictures for typos in judgement: SC
stories.summary: In a significant move, the Supreme Court intervened to address remarks made by the Rajasthan high court about a trial judge. Union home minister Amit Shah has reached out to Congress, proposing a parliamentary discussion on the topic. Their strategy focuses on addressing the opposition's criticism related to the SIR and electoral setbacks. A BJP-commissioned survey reveals substantial public backing for the initiative, with the next campaign phase due to launch after Diwali celebrations.

Federal authorities remain dedicated to investigating threats to maintain the integrity of the electoral process.

stories.summary: In a remarkable initiative, the Charles Antetokounmpo Family Foundation and Enaleia have repurposed discarded fishing gear into vibrant basketball nets, enhancing public courts across Athens. This project not only replaces damaged nets but also tackles marine pollution by transforming waste into valuable resources for the community. Young athletes can engage with these recycled nets, fostering a sense of environmental awareness alongside their love for sports.

Previously owned by Leonora Pierotti Thomas, the house is rich in artistic character yet demands extensive restoration. Campaigns utilize machine-learning tools to personalize outreach, raising concerns about trust in media integrity and the electoral process. This ruling highlights the challenges in pursuing financial claims against county governments in Georgia.

stories.title: Texas farmers turn 640 acres of donated land into college scholarships for 300 students
stories.summary: A 640-acre farmland donation made to a Texas school district in 1984 has become a source of college scholarships for hundreds of students. Unveiled on November 1, this stupa strengthens the enduring friendship and cultural ties between India and Bhutan. This initiative highlights Bhutan's commitment to boosting its Buddhist identity and serves as a token of gratitude for India's continuous support in its developmental journey.

stories.title: One move, two gains: NHAI to desilt Bihar rivers and build roads with excavated material
stories.summary: Bihar's government has signed an agreement with the road transport ministry for river desilting to reduce flooding. The excavated silt and sand will be utilized in highway construction projects across the state. This initiative aims to improve water flow in rivers while providing construction materials at no cost. Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary emphasized the impact of flooding on the state's agriculture and infrastructure.

The court clarified that accusations of inflated billing require concrete evidence, particularly following Flux Drive Inc.'s unsuccessful trade-secrets lawsuit. This ruling reinforces the notion that simply employing AI does not warrant a reduction in legal fees, establishing a significant precedent for similar cases moving forward.

stories.summary: As election day for the US midterms arrives, the atmosphere is charged with anticipation. Three distinct scenarios could shape the future of Congress: a sweeping Democratic wave may bring notable victories, whereas a slim Democratic majority may present hurdles in legislation. On the flip side, Republicans retaining control over both chambers could steer Trump's political agenda. The results await, holding the potential to influence the nation significantly.

stories.title: 'Mischievous breach': SC halts BMC chief's salary over failure to clear encroachments
stories.summary: A Bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued a show-cause notice to the commissioner, asking why contempt action should not be taken against him for failing to implement the court's earlier orders. The court also rejected the commissioner's request for more time, imposed costs of Rs 5 lakh and directed that salary payments to him.

stories.summary: A study conducted at a seabird colony in Canada found that darker colours and patterned surfaces could reduce bird collisions caused by artificial lighting at night. Researchers discovered that vertically striped sheets recorded 2.8 times fewer bird collisions than plain sheets, while black sheets performed better than white ones. The findings could help make coastal buildings, ships and offshore facilities safer for seabirds.

stories.title: Trump unveils repaired Lincoln Memorial pool after costs exceed $14m, up from under $2m
stories.summary: The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool has recently undergone extensive repairs, as unveiled by Trump, marking a significant and costly restoration effort. Budget overruns have pushed expenses to over $14 million, primarily due to algae problems stemming from a failed blue coating. Officials assert that these costs are essential for the pool's lasting quality. Fortunately, after the essential maintenance work, the site is now welcoming visitors once again.

stories.title: Ann Widdecombe’s Dartmoor home where she was murdered goes on sale for £900,000, 4 months after death
stories.summary: Ann Widdecombe’s Dartmoor home, where the former Conservative MP was murdered in July 2026, has been put on the market for £900,000, just four months after her death. stories.summary: Two sisters in Washington, US, lost a property dispute involving fences on both sides of their home after a survey revealed discrepancies in the boundary lines. The Washington Court of Appeals upheld rulings favouring both neighbours, including an order to remove a fence encroaching on one neighbour's land. The court also upheld legal-fee awards and granted the neighbours additional fees for the appeal.

stories.title: Meet Eva Outram, UK woman who quit her $58,000 NHS job; now lives in a caravan and saves $3,200 a month
stories.summary: After her impactful experience on 'Alone', Eva Outram, formerly an NHS project manager, swapped her city life for a caravan with her partner, Tom Park, focusing on simplicity and financial freedom. By working on farms for accommodation, they manage to save about $3,200 every month. Outram envisions creating outdoor skill workshops to foster nature appreciation and has plans to eventually buy land to construct their own residence.

The Texas test: Latino voters could make or break Trump's midterms
EC allows voters deleted from draft electoral rolls to use Form 6 for re-inclusion
Quincy Jones tops Forbes’ 2026 highest-paid deceased celebrities list at $150 million
stories.summary: Quincy Jones departed from this world in November 2024, but his legacy thrived, bringing in substantial revenue well into 2026. Much of this financial success stemmed from a remarkable $150 million deal for his extensive music catalog. Additionally, his enduring relationship with Michael Jackson fueled renewed interest following a blockbuster biopic's release.

stories.title: 132-year-old Kirby home reduced to rubble
stories.summary: Houston's historic Kirby Mansion, a Tudor Revival gem, was abruptly leveled after city inspectors stopped renovation efforts over permit issues. Despite being well-maintained, the new owner proceeded with the demolition unauthorized, leading to outcry from preservationists. The community mourned the mansion with a vigil, pressing for policy reforms and alluding to a gas station development that might replace the beloved site.

stories.title: Dhirendra Shastri apologises for 'your Krishna, our Ram' remark; controversy explained
stories.summary: In a video message posted on social media from Kenya's Nairobi, Shastri on Monday said he had no intention of insulting any deity or suggesting that one was superior to the other. He apologised to anyone whose religious sentiments may have been hurt by his comments. The controversy began during a recent Ram Katha in Karera in Madhya Pradesh's Shivpuri district.

stories.title: US student forgotten in DEA cell for 5 days gets $4.1 million
Evening Newswrap: SC says protest sites cannot be occupied indefinitely; Sensex surges over 1,200 points, and more
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has reiterated that protest areas should be allocated for limited time frames for various groups. In economic news, the market witnessed a positive shift as the Sensex climbed over 1,200 points due to falling crude prices and increased foreign investments. Controversy erupted when the Samajwadi Party dissociated itself from remarks made by AISA leader Neha Bora concerning caste matters.

stories.title: '24 hours have passed, Modi ji': Rahul renews debate challenge to PM over 'foreign links' - watch
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi has extended a challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for an open debate on several allegations. He outlined topics including foreign influence, the Adani case, and financial matters that require discussion. Rahul gandhi further suggested that the debate take place in the presence of media and youth, proposing Mohan Bhagwat as a moderator.

stories.title: Essex couple transform their garden with miniature railway
stories.summary: Dave and Angela Walker, a couple from Clacton-on-Sea, dedicated eight years to building a miniature railway. Their project spans approximately 400 metres throughout their quarter-acre garden, showcasing various collected memorabilia. Despite opinions from others, they find joy in their shared achievement and partnership. The couple plans to open their railway for community fundraising events benefiting the local lifeboat station.

stories.title: Portugal’s Corvo Island goes dark to save thousands of young seabirds
Bihar CM Samrat Chaudhary says ‘crime might happen, but not apradh’; Tejashwi takes swipe
Why neither MAGA nor Democrats are particularly bothered about Indian-Americans
stories.summary: About 133 years ago, a man born Narendranath said he was from India and preached tolerance at the World’s Parliament of Religions in a speech that evokes awe even today. It’s sad that, so many years later, Americans of all stripes have become particularly intolerant towards his descendants.

stories.title: Europe on alert after bomb threats target at least four passenger flights
Taylor Swift donated 'Wildest Dreams' proceeds to African conservation group
'Islamic fundamentalists talking about secularism': Kiren Rijiju hits out at Rahul Gandhi over 'foreign help' remark
Utah rancher turns 1,100 acres into a solar-powered income stream
'Radical thinking': INDIA bloc allies snub Left leader Neha Bora's 'Brahmanvaad' remark
stories.summary: Neha Bora has been actively involved in protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. She took part in an October 10 demonstration organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and student groups in Delhi. Police detained several protesters, including Bora, as restrictions on public gatherings were imposed in parts of the capital.

stories.title: Bhutan's glacial lake outburst exposes growing disaster threat across the Himalayas
stories.summary: Bhutan experienced a significant glacial lake outburst that raised concerns regarding devastating glacial floods in the Himalayas. Authorities are monitoring a temporary lake created by debris from the initial flood event. The risks posed by melting glaciers are increasingly threatening both infrastructure and communities across the region. India, sharing river systems with Bhutan, has started its own review of disaster preparedness plans.

stories.title: UK High Court rules assets were gifted before death, orders £259,725 in legal costs
stories.summary: A High Court judge ruled that specific assets of the deceased were legitimate gifts received by Masudur Rahman before death, dating back to October 2020. This ruling ignited legal contention with four co-defendants. The court detailed the asset scope, allowing appeals on particular grounds. Rahman secured costs due to his successful claim, but his plea for an enhanced costs budget was ultimately denied by the judge.

stories.title: Tennessee couple lose land claim after decades of mowing and gardening, court rules for developer
stories.summary: A couple from Tennessee faced a setback as their claim over a strip of land beside their house was overturned by the court. They believed their usage spanning almost 30 years sufficed for establishing ownership through adverse possession. However, the appeals court determined that the couple's evidence fell short of legal standards, highlighting a vital legal principle: merely using land for an extended period does not guarantee ownership.

stories.title: Arnold Schwarzenegger’s charity night raises record $9.75 million for US students
stories.summary: Arnold Schwarzenegger's yearly charity gala has made a remarkable impact, raising $9.75 million for After-School All-Stars. This initiative plays a crucial role in offering educational and extracurricular activities to around 150,000 students across the country. The event boasted live entertainment, auctions, and generous contributions from various artists and companies. For over 30 years, Schwarzenegger has dedicated himself to fostering educational and mentorship programs vital for youth development.

stories.title: 'Incompatible with secular character': Centre tells Delhi HC mosque inside Krishi Bhawan must be demolished
Ex-Air chief AP Singh wrote to Rajnath, urged him to keep Race Course land under IAF control
'Huge impact on polls': IB opposes shifting convict in ex-Punjab CM Beant Singh's assassination to state jail
stories.summary: The Intelligence Bureau has raised concerns regarding Jagtar Singh Hawara's potential transfer from Tihar Jail to a prison in Punjab, citing possible ramifications for the impending assembly elections. Hawara, who is serving a sentence for the assassination of Beant Singh and is considered a high-risk individual, could see his transfer postponed according to his attorney.

stories.title: J&K: Omar Abdullah faces setback as Srinagar MP Aga Ruhullah quits NC, resigns from Parliament
'Gaddar': BJP accuses Rahul Gandhi of treason, calls him 'Bhasmasur'
stories.summary: BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia accused Rahul Gandhi of treason and promoting anarchy in India's democracy. He raised questions about Gandhi's foreign engagements and the Congress's MoU with the Communist Party of China. Allegations included inappropriate conduct towards a woman police officer during protests against the Chief Election Commissioner. Bhatia warned the opposition leaders about the potential backlash from the public regarding their calls for regime change.

stories.title: 'Inspired by Rahul Gandhi': BJP targets AISA's Neha Bora over 'Brahmanvaad' remarks
PM Modi inaugurates Pune Metro's 23-km Pink Line, says India's network now 1,200 km
India, Israel vote against Pakistan-backed UN arms control resolution: What it means
stories.summary: In a significant move, India and Israel opposed a UN resolution proposed by Pakistan and Belarus concerning regional arms control. Despite its adoption with strong backing, both nations voiced serious reservations. India's delegate argued that national security transcends geographic lines, highlighting the potential distraction from established UN disarmament agreements. Additionally, India expressed concerns regarding specific references to South Asian arms control measures present in the resolution.

stories.title: 'Can't occupy a site for all times': SC on Delhi protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
Azam Khan, facing 95 cases since 2017, moves SC against his arrest by ED
'Everything is available': SC flags open sale of firecrackers in Delhi despite restrictions
Rouse Avenue court seeks Delhi Police response on Bimol Akoijam's anticipatory bail plea
NHAI to use desilted river material for road projects in Bihar, says transport minister Gadkari
stories.summary: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has embarked on an innovative project to leverage materials from Bihar's rivers for highway development, aiming to alleviate flooding. This strategic move, a result of a memorandum of understanding between the Bihar government and the Ministry of Road Transport, is designed to tackle the dual flooding challenges posed by local rainfall and external water influx.

stories.title: Dilip Ghosh takes 'Sonia' jibe at Mamata for joining INDIA bloc rally against SIR
stories.summary: Dilip Ghosh has publicly lambasted Mamata Banerjee for her involvement in the INDIA bloc rally concerning changes to the electoral roll. He argues her party's diminishing political clout is prompting her to seek validation through an alliance with Congress. Ghosh highlighted her past victories, labeling her claims regarding electoral integrity as hypocritical, and pointed out the positive impact of removing fraudulent voters in fostering fair elections in West Bengal.

stories.title: 'Targeting civilian infrastructure must end': MEA after Indian national killed in attack on ship in Oman
'Rs 25cr spent on ads to claim no stubble burning, FIRs tell another story': BJP targets AAP govt in Punjab
stories.summary: Delhi Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa accused the Punjab government of permitting stubble burning while contradicting its claims. He alleged that Punjab's government had registered FIRs against farmers involved in stubble burning activities. Sirsa criticized the appointment of Reena Gupta as chairperson of the Punjab Pollution Control Board as an attempt to manipulate pollution data. He emphasized the adverse impact of Punjab's stubble burning on Delhi's air quality.

stories.title: California judge orders one former partner to pay the other $66,192 in legal fees after house dispute
stories.summary: Matthew Shroder and Mackenzie Fotsch are currently embroiled in legal disputes regarding a jointly owned property in Sausalito. After achieving a partial victory in a motion to strike, Shroder sought $90,010 in attorney fees and the court awarded him $66,192.50. This amount includes $40,887.50 for anti-SLAPP proceedings and $21,700 for the fee application, yet does not resolve their ongoing property conflict.

stories.title: Meet Hazmatt: Oklahoma’s 20-foot reclining robot made from discarded dumpsters, built for just over $14,000
stories.summary: Norman, Oklahoma has unveiled a captivating new public sculpture named Hazmatt, crafted from recycled dumpsters. This striking giant robot, funded by surplus construction funds totaling slightly over $14,000, is strategically located at the city’s Household Hazardous Waste Facility. Hazmatt serves to inspire the community, highlighting the importance of responsible waste management and showcasing the potential for creative reuse of discarded materials.

stories.title: Reddit Fights Teen Account Ban: Platforms contest Australia’s under-16 law; ruling may sway global curbs
stories.summary: In late 2025, Australia enacted a law prohibiting individuals under 16 from accessing social media. However, Reddit and a libertarian organization are contesting this legislation in the High Court. While the law seeks to safeguard youth, it faces backlash for its lacking effectiveness, as many teenagers under this age still manage to go online. The government has responded by imposing stricter penalties on non-compliant social media platforms.

stories.title: Judge Judy’s mentoring programme marks 20 years, reaching 1,500 young women
stories.summary: Her Honor Mentoring began with a modest gathering of girls two decades ago and has since flourished remarkably. This program matches high school seniors with dedicated mentors, guiding them through educational and career paths. Participants acquire vital skills, including financial literacy, that prepare them for both college and professional futures while fostering nurturing relationships that empower young women to chase their dreams.

stories.title: 'Doesn’t have courage to call all-party meet?’: Congress questions Shah over delay in discussion on delimitation Bill
Wisconsin father-son dealership feud ends with $321,330 civil-theft damages against son
stories.summary: A serious conflict arose between Carl Schneider and his son Chris regarding Hybrid Car Store Inc., their family-run dealership. Chris misappropriated corporate funds to pay off personal obligations, resulting in significant financial repercussions. The situation escalated with multiple lawsuits, resulting in a federal court ruling that held Chris accountable for civil theft.

stories.title: 1 killed, 13 rescued after unidentified aerial object strikes Indian vessel near Oman
stories.summary: An Indian seafarer from Gujarat was killed after an unidentified aerial object struck the Indian-flagged vessel MSV AL JUSUFI off the Oman coast on Monday. The remaining 13 crew members were rescued by the Omani Coast Guard. Union minister Sarbananda Sonowal said Indian authorities were coordinating with Oman to assist the survivors and arrange their repatriation.

stories.title: Man claims Crown land linked to Napoleon’s former dairy after 15 years
Record 2026 Campaign Spending: Billionaires, crypto fuel $11.9bn US midterms; TV ads dominate
stories.summary: The 2026 midterm elections in the U.S. are on track to raise a staggering $12 billion, marking the most expensive campaign in history. Wealthy individuals and corporations wield increasing influence over financing, with billionaire Elon Musk standing out as the top donor, having contributed nearly $500 million to Republican candidates.

stories.title: Can Trump defy history? The big battles shaping US midterms
SAD MP Harsimrat Badal writes to Om Birla over farmer's body removal, seeks action against SSP
stories.summary: Harsimrat Kaur Badal has reached out to the Lok Sabha Speaker to demand accountability from Mansa SSP Vaibhav Chaudhary. She accuses the police of inappropriately removing a farmer's body during a protest against alleged drug trade connections. Badal mentions intimidation tactics used by the police and claims her concerns were met with dismissal by the SSP.

stories.title: 'Lousy con artist': BJP attacks Rahul Gandhi after his 'foreign help' jibe at PM Modi
Maldives' former foreign minister Abdulla Shahid arrested in child abuse case
'Rs 14,000cr loss last month': Delhi traders seek protest-free Delhi till November 11
Netanyahu open to 'broad' government formation after election setback but rules out Arab parties
stories.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu has expressed a readiness to establish a broad coalition government under his guidance. His Likud party is attempting to stall the certification process of the recent election results, citing claims of foreign interference. Netanyahu has dismissed the option of collaborating with Arab parties, due to accusations of terrorism against them.

stories.title: EC can't monopolise voter awareness campaigns: SC; sets aside order denying permission to civil society
stories.summary: The Supreme Court said the Election Commission cannot monopolise voter awareness campaigns, setting aside the Rajasthan State Election Commission's order denying permission to a civil society group led by Aruna Roy. The bench directed the state poll body to reconsider its request within 48 hours for campaigning ahead of the final phase of Panchayati Raj elections on November 14.

stories.title: Supreme Court seeks Centre’s response on whereabouts of Barman from Bangladesh
stories.summary: Wife says he went to Siliguri for treatment, then to Deoghar and now untraceable

stories.title: 'Calibrated non-kinetic measures': How Indian Navy foiled Somali pirates, rescued 20
stories.summary: The Indian Navy successfully rescued all 20 crew members from the hijacked fishing vessel Azini off Somalia. The operation involved coordinated efforts with naval and air force assets over 48 hours. Marine Commandos were deployed to secure the vessel after locating it through persistent surveillance. The hijacking posed a significant maritime security concern, as the pirates could have used Azini for further attacks.

stories.title: Judge Clears Capitol Event: US court backs Satanic Temple’s free speech claim; Iowa plans appeal
stories.summary: In a significant ruling, a federal judge has mandated that Iowa officials allow the local chapter of the Satanic Temple to hold its holiday event. This decision comes after multiple rejections linked to building regulations. Despite state officials' reservations about the event, the judge found their concerns unconvincing. Activities scheduled include caroling and crafts for children. However, state officials are prepared to contest the ruling's validity.

stories.title: 26 killed as Russia strikes Ukraine school used for aid distribution
stories.summary: Russian forces struck a school being used as a humanitarian aid distribution centre in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, killing at least 26 people, with around 20 others missing. Rescue efforts were disrupted by fresh drone attacks. Meanwhile, cyberattacks triggered fake emergency alerts in Ukraine and Russia, as a limited ceasefire in the Kherson region expired.

stories.title: E-sign for SIR tribunal judges soon, can upload bulk orders on portal
stories.summary: The Election Commission has modernized its tribunal portal to assist West Bengal judges in bulk uploading orders, significantly enhancing appeal processing efficiency. Meanwhile, the home ministry has unveiled three new Foreigners Regional Registration Offices across India, designed to improve accessibility for international visitors. This strategy supports India's mission to establish itself as a premier destination for tourism and education.

stories.title: For 'outstanding vision', Bhutan dedicates one of 108 stupas to PM Modi
Marital discord no ground for termination of pregnancy: SC
Investment in renewable energy cushioned Iran war blow: PM Modi
First in 47 years: No operational fatality in CRPF in an entire year
Unhappy with Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth, six NCP biggies meet Amit Shah
Mammal Reintroductions At Sturt: six native species return; project expands beyond fences
stories.summary: Ecologists Rebecca West and Reece Pedler are leading an inspiring initiative called the Wild Deserts project in New South Wales, focused on reviving native mammal populations that have been absent for over a century. Their efforts have successfully seen the reintroduction of multiple species to Sturt National Park, where they are now thriving and breeding in the wild.

stories.title: Murtho Habitat Restoration: Former vineyard revived for regent parrots; family project spans generations
stories.summary: After departing from the wine industry, Tony and Cherie Townsend embarked on a remarkable project to repurpose their 40-acre vineyard into a sanctuary for regent parrots. Their family and local volunteers, spanning four generations, are actively involved in this conservation initiative. Backed by the Murraylands and Riverland Landscape Board, over 3,000 native seedlings have been planted, fostering vital habitats and illustrating the crucial role private land plays in enhancing biodiversity.

stories.title: 'Air fares up by 700%': Don't fly, says SC
SC on Diwali: Crackers on Nov 7-8 in 2 time slots, and keep it green
SC orders trial in Ram temple donation case; SIT says Rs 2.7 crore stolen
Day after quitting as Punjab MLAs, 3 AAP rebels come into BJP fold
Nebraska court vacates sale of couple's home over husband's commercial lease debt
stories.summary: A couple in Nebraska was on the brink of losing their family home due to a commercial lease debt solely tied to the husband. The creditor aimed to sell the property to reclaim funds. The Nebraska Supreme Court stepped in, clarifying that the lower court misapplied the judgment lien, which only affected the husband's interest.

stories.title: Record Subsurface Warming In Monterey Bay: MBARI logs 18.18°C at 60m; tropical species move north
stories.summary: Scientists have announced that temperatures at 200 feet off Monterey Bay have reached their highest levels in nearly forty years. This rise is attributed to the forthcoming 2026-27 El Niño, with sightings of tropical species migrating northward, suggesting significant ecological transformations. These shifts in ocean conditions pose a risk to deep-sea food availability, impacting various marine ecosystems.

stories.title: Bangka Slow Loris Rediscovered: Rescues reveal more than 90 venomous primates; habitat loss still threatens
stories.summary: A groundbreaking study reveals the comeback of the Bangka slow loris, once feared lost or critically endangered. Over 90 individuals have been documented on Bangka Island from 2015 to 2025, shedding light on their survival. Wildlife rescues have been instrumental not only in recording their existence but also in aiding rehabilitation efforts.

stories.title: Navy rescues 20 crew members of fishing vessel from armed pirates over 3,000km from Mumbai, Rajnath praises 48-hr op
Atlanta landlord's $50,000 fundraiser grows into $16.5 million, helping 5,500 families avoid eviction
stories.summary: Jason Dozier initiated a fundraising campaign in 2020, which led to the creation of the Housing Stability Fund. This programme has provided financial assistance to over 5,500 families facing housing insecurity in the Atlanta area. By streamlining processes and collaborating with landlords, the programme aims to prevent evictions and court backlogs. Follow-up surveys indicate that a majority of recipients remain in stable housing a year later.

stories.title: Louisiana woman wins nearly $450,000 after $32,500 river barrier fails and home shifts
stories.summary: After suffering extensive structural damage to her home from a failing wooden bulkhead, Elizabeth Molbert took legal action against the contractor involved and succeeded. The jury assigned 75% of the blame to the contractor and, in a twist, the appeals court ruled that Molbert had no fault in the matter, increasing her compensation to $448,431.34 and adjusting her mental anguish damages to align with her financial difficulties.

stories.title: Row erupts after Scottish govt sends IT contract to Bengaluru to administer welfare payment
Texas opens 3,000-acre state park along the Colorado River with $1 billion expansion fund
stories.summary: Post Oak Ridge has officially opened, marking Texas' latest state park. Spanning over 3,000 acres, it features two hiking trails along four miles of scenic routes. Plans for future camping facilities and river access are on track for completion by 2029. Input from the community has been vital in guiding the park's development, as part of a larger effort to expand public outdoor spaces across Texas.

stories.title: Howard Stern's wife Beth turns grief into rescue mission, helping over 2,000 cats find homes
stories.summary: After the heartbreaking passing of their bulldog, Howard and Beth Stern channeled their sorrow into meaningful change by founding Bianca's Furry Friends Feline Adoption Center, part of North Shore Animal League America. This center improves the conditions for cats waiting for adoption and boosts rescue capabilities. With over 2,000 cats fostered since 2013, Beth's dedicated efforts have played a crucial role in spotlighting the importance of adopting shelter animals nationwide.

stories.title: Farm Becomes Wildlife Retreat: Olivia Newton-John reshaped Dalwood estate; sale tied to cancer work
stories.summary: Olivia Newton-John owned a country estate in Australia that she transformed over nearly four decades. This property included natural features and a significant amount of wildlife habitat that she developed. After battling cancer, the estate was sold in 2019 for $4.6 million, reflecting changes in her priorities. Newton-John's connection to the area continued through her involvement with a wellness retreat she co-founded.

stories.title: Rahul can be PM only in mock Parliament: Amit Shah
Stephen Curry-backed golf teams make history with women's first NEC title and men's third win
stories.summary: Howard University's golf program reached new heights when both men's and women's teams won their conference championships. The women's team claimed its first-ever Northeast Conference title in April 2026. Just days later, the men's team secured its third consecutive NEC championship victory. The successes highlighted the growth of the program, supported by NBA star Stephen Curry's funding.

stories.title: Days after Farooq’s Pak praise, Mehbooba says Abdullahs created distrust between Kashmir & rest of India
Nebraska court rejects handwritten will signed by man but written largely by his longtime partner
stories.summary: In a significant ruling, Nebraska's Supreme Court declared a handwritten will invalid, stating that the primary handwriting was not that of the testator. The court reaffirmed the original 1984 will, which allocated assets to the deceased's sons. This decision underlined the necessity for a holographic will to be solely in the writer's hand to clarify testamentary intent, especially amid disputes from a long-term partner after Douglas G. Todd's death.

stories.title: Maryland court orders new trial over $3.2 million trust after sisters challenge inheritance
stories.summary: A Maryland appeals court has mandated a new trial concerning a $3.2 million trust fund held by three sisters. The court identified procedural errors that prevented two sisters from presenting crucial handwriting evidence regarding the trust. Their claims included accusations of undue influence exerted by their sister, the main beneficiary. The appeals court emphasized issues with the previous trial's allowed testimonies and evidence exclusions.

stories.title: North Carolina sculptor's tiny cabin grew into a 60-foot woodland castle
Paul McCartney-backed Liverpool arts institute celebrates 400+ graduates 30 years on
stories.summary: The LIPA held its 2026 graduation ceremony celebrating its 30th anniversary by awarding degrees to its very first graduates. With over 400 students from 28 different countries in attendance, this event marked a monumental occasion. Sir Paul McCartney was on hand to honor five notable figures for their artistry and impact on the cultural landscape, showcasing LIPA's commitment to nurturing creative talent across various fields, including music, theatre, and film.

stories.title: Fake nuclear threat alert sent to Ukrainians after emergency app hacked
IISc develops 3D-printed model to study how cancer drugs penetrate tumours
RLD leader projects Jayant Chaudhary as NDA's face for 2027 UP polls
Homebuyers body urges PM to recast RERA; separate promotion from protection
ICE officer surrenders after grand jury indicts him for running over immigrant with vehicle in Texas
Trump admin asks Supreme Court to set aside 20,000 California ballots over citizenship row a day before midterms
Power outage hits Washington DC's Foggy Bottom, over 1,100 Pepco customers affected
Indian Sikh couple's New Zealand asylum claim rejected after NZ$336,000 crore debt dispute with Punjab moneylender
Entire police force resigns in Georgia city; Mayor Craig Timmons admits tracking police chief's truck
stories.summary: A small Georgia city is facing a police staffing crisis after its entire full-time police force resigned. Mayor Craig Timmons admitted placing a GPS tracker on Police Chief Lamar Bunn's truck over concerns about his timesheets. Bunn has denied wrongdoing, while the mass resignations have left the city relying on the county sheriff's office for police coverage.

stories.title: Historic Mansion Sale Soars: Nantucket’s Hadwen-Wright House fetches $15.25 million; hidden cistern preserved
stories.summary: The Hadwen-Wright House in Nantucket fetched an impressive $15.25 million, after being originally listed at $15.5 million. This stunning mansion, a prime example of Greek Revival architecture, is steeped in history. Its extensive renovations not only maintained original features but also unveiled a unique brick-lined cistern now preserved for guests. This sale highlights the lasting appeal of Nantucket's historically significant residences.

stories.title: In 2013, divers started placing simple cinder-block pyramids on a Caribbean seabed
stories.summary: Initiated in 2013, the Grenada Artificial Reef Project employs concrete blocks to foster marine life habitats. Remarkable progress was observed shortly after, with algae and various invertebrates flourishing on the structures. However, while research shows these artificial reefs attract species typical of natural environments, further studies are essential to evaluate their role in aiding natural reef recovery and assessing their long-term effects on adjacent ecosystems.

stories.title: US judge dismisses charges against 2 ex-FBI officials over Hunter Biden laptop probe, calls prosecution 'weaponisation'
Iran's supreme leader gave government 'certain authorities' over peace talks with US: Pezeshkian
US midterms: Five flashpoints election officials are watching as America votes
'Look outside, Jack!' Who was the man called out by female pilot Nathalia in final moments of Learjet crash?
First in 47 years: CRPF completes 12 months without any operational casualties
stories.summary: CRPF Director General GP Singh congratulated personnel on the milestone, saying the last operational death in the force was recorded on October 30, 2025. The previous time the CRPF went such a long period without an operational fatality was before January 1979. The milestone comes against the backdrop of another serious challenge facing the force, the rising number of personnel dying by suicide.

stories.title: Meet the couple who couldn't afford a UK home bought an entire French hamlet for £26K, saved £100K
stories.summary: Yip Ward and Paul Mappley went from living in a caravan in England to owning an abandoned French hamlet. The couple bought the property for £26,000, which includes seven cottages, two barns and other buildings. By carrying out much of the restoration themselves, they estimate they have saved more than £100,000 while bringing the historic hamlet back to life.

stories.title: Trump's Justice dept steps into US midterm battles, breaks decades-old practice
'NCP united under Sunetra Pawar': Party rejects rift rumours as she skips Amit Shah meet
stories.summary: The speculation was fuelled by the absence of Maharashtra deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar and her sons, Parth and Jay, from Sunday's meeting with Shah. The development raised questions about whether the party's leadership was being sidelined in discussions over its future following the death of Ajit Pawar. NCP national chief spokesperson Umesh Patil rejected reports as "incorrect, baseless and misleading".

stories.title: NZ couple turn hillside land into a medieval brick castle with towers and a secret dungeon trapdoor
stories.summary: After three decades of craftsmanship, Denise and Greg Powell are parting ways with their extraordinary recycled-brick castle in Broad Bay. What began as a straightforward home evolved into a medieval masterpiece, complete with a secret trapdoor and various salvaged architectural details. As they downsize to a cozier residence nearby, this unique property has seen its value soar since their acquisition in the early 90s.

stories.title: New Hampshire closed 20 acres of Great Bay to shellfish harvesting for 5 years from November 1
stories.summary: The Fish and Game Department of New Hampshire has initiated a five-year period of closure at Great Bay to facilitate oyster restoration efforts. This move affects two key sites, one near Woodman Point and another near Nannie Island. Significant measures are being implemented to combat the alarming 90% decline in oyster reefs since 1970, involving collaboration between researchers and conservation groups to rejuvenate oyster populations and restore essential marine habitats.

stories.title: New York volunteers spent seven years preparing six 175-pound reef balls for Eastchester Bay
stories.summary: After years of meticulous planning, volunteers from City Island Oyster Reef successfully installed six reef balls in Eastchester Bay. These structures were intentionally seeded with oyster larvae to bolster local oyster populations. This initiative stems from thorough monitoring of both water quality and the ecosystem around City Island. Remarkably, marine species like fish and crabs have started to thrive in the area.

stories.title: Co-pilot of doomed Learjet flight that crashed in Florida identified as Nathalia Gadelha. She got her private pilot's license when she was 17
'Surge in popularity after reality show': Tej Pratap Yadav asks for enhanced security from Centre
stories.summary: In a post on X, Yadav said his recent appearance on a reality show had increased his popularity, with large numbers of people approaching him in public places to take photographs. He said the crowds posed a risk not only to him but also to the lone security personnel currently assigned to him.

stories.title: Russia exits European anti-torture treaty, ends independent prison inspections
Cyclone Murusu: 19 flights cancelled, NDRF on standby as coastal states brace for severe storm - top development
Indian-origin woman Srishti Tarana Sharma charged in US over pro-Palestine intimidation campaign at Michigan university
Cyclone Murasu to make landfall near at Andhra coast tonight; 120 kmph winds expected
stories.summary: Cyclone Murasu has intensified and is predicted to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast soon. It is expected to bring strong winds reaching up to 120 kmph and heavy rainfall. Several districts in Andhra Pradesh will experience severe weather conditions due to the cyclone. Precautionary measures have been implemented, including rescue operations and evacuation arrangements. Fishermen have been advised to avoid venturing into the sea during this period.

stories.title: 'Azam the, Azam hain': Will the Khan factor help or haunt Akhilesh in 2027 UP elections?
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav's recent visit to Azam Khan in jail underscores their deep political connection amidst ongoing legal troubles. Following Azam's fleeting bail, the Enforcement Directorate swiftly took him back into custody, adding complexity to the Samajwadi Party's election preparations. Balancing support for Azam while appealing to Muslim constituents presents a significant challenge for Akhilesh as he navigates potential electoral repercussions.

stories.title: 'Your social media posts amounted to instigation': Bombay HC pulls up actor Imran Khan - top quotes
stories.summary: A bench comprising Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna remarked that instead of deporting Khan immediately, authorities had shown leniency by issuing him a notice asking him to leave the country. Khan's lawyer, Venkatesh Dhond, responded by submitting an undertaking that the 43-year-old actor would not participate in any protest in the future. He also conveyed Khan's unconditional apology to the court.

stories.title: 'Rahul Gandhi has no vision, will be responsible for Congress's wipeout': BJP's Nitin Nabin at anti-SIR march
'3 crore Bangladeshi infiltrators don't exist on voters' list': Amit Shah counters Rahul's anti-SIR pitch
stories.summary: In a verbal blitzkrieg, a day after Rahul's mega Ramlila Maidan rally in the national capital, Shah said that behind the Congress's criticism of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) lies an "attempt to protect illegal Bangladeshi infiltrators", three crore of whom, he claimed, were struck off the electoral rolls during the revision.

stories.title: Evening newswrap: Imran Khan apologises to Bombay HC, SC allows green crackers & more
'You became PM because of foreign help': Rahul Gandhi challenges PM Modi for debate
61 detained in Ahmedabad as crackdown on illegal Bangladeshi immigrants intensifies
stories.summary: Ahmedabad's Crime Branch has taken action against 61 suspected illegal immigrants, mostly hailing from Bangladesh, in a city-wide effort to bolster safety ahead of Diwali. The police executed synchronized raids across different localities to pinpoint foreign nationals living without legal status. Deportation processes are currently being initiated, furthering previous measures aimed at curbing illegal immigration from Bangladesh.

stories.title: Centre notifies grievance redressal rules under VB-G RAM G Act, sets 15-day resolution deadline
stories.summary: The Centre has officially introduced grievance redressal protocols as per the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025. Complaints must receive resolution within 15 days, with preliminary inquiries to be conducted in seven working days. Individuals can lodge grievances through various methods, ensuring that all complaints will be recorded. Complainants will have the opportunity to present their cases, and issues that remain unresolved shall be escalated for further scrutiny and resolution.

Charity founder stole millions and spent $320,000 on lavish dining trips
Imran Khan tenders unconditional apology in HC over anti-SIR protest participation
FPCE writes to PM Modi, lists 5 key changes to RERA to strengthen homebuyer protection
SC allows green crackers in Delhi-NCR for Diwali, full ban from November 9
Sonia Gandhi meets Lalu Yadav in Delhi; Tejashwi shares photos, reminisces UPA-era tie
stories.summary: Tejashwi Yadav, Bihar leader of the opposition, said Sonia Gandhi had personally expressed a desire to meet his father after learning that he was in Delhi for a medical check-up. He also pointed out that the then Prime Minister Manmohan Singh's government had allocated more than Rs 1.45 lakh crore for Bihar's development.

stories.title: Texas man arrested after cemetery theft and FBI office bone incident
'Don't travel by air. Next case': SC judge on plea alleging 700% airfare hike
‘Rahul Gandhi fostering chaos’: BJP questions Congress over SIR row
Serena Williams helped build 2 schools in rural Kenya; years later, both remain open and part of national education system
stories.summary: Serena Williams established two secondary schools in rural Kenya to provide local children with education. The Matooni Serena Williams Secondary School opened in 2009, followed by the Wee Serena Williams Secondary School in 2010. Both schools are now integrated into Kenya's national education system and managed by community boards. HP's involvement brought important technology resources to enhance learning experiences for students.

stories.title: A Dutch engineer built a car controlled by a goldfish swimming inside a water tank; earning a Guinness World Records title
stories.summary: In an extraordinary showcase of technology and pet companionship, Blub, the goldfish belonging to Dutch engineer Thomas de Wolf, successfully maneuvered a motion-sensing vehicle for 12.28 meters on a Milan television show aired on January 23, 2025. By translating Blub's natural movements into steering commands, De Wolf envisions applications of this technology to assist people with physical disabilities, merging creativity with functionality.

stories.title: Meet the three former AAP leaders who switched sides to join BJP ahead of Punjab polls
Neymar's centre helps 3,000 children with education, sports and healthcare
US woman returns from abroad to find inherited house sold using forged documents
stories.summary: A Tennessee woman returned from abroad in 2021 to discover that her late brother's house had been sold using a fake identity and forged documents. After she sued the company involved in the sale, a lower court dismissed her case. On Thursday, an appeals court revived her fraud claim but upheld the dismissal of her negligence claim.

stories.title: 'Don't take court for granted': Delhi court summons actor Nora Fatehi again in Rs 200-crore extortion case
Shakira's foundation helps 224,000 children, builds schools and boosts higher education
‘Youth-oppressive NDA govt’: Tejashwi accuses Nitish of toppling Mahagathbandhan regime in 2024
Big setback for AAP ahead of Punjab elections; 3 rebel MLAs join BJP
Oprah Winfrey’s $60 million Maui wildfire relief fund helped thousands; now her donation brings new CT scanner to local hospital
stories.summary: Oprah Winfrey and Dwayne Johnson launched the People's Fund of Maui to support wildfire survivors and provided significant financial assistance. Winfrey made a separate donation for a new CT scanner at Maui Memorial Medical Center to enhance healthcare services. The scanner aims to improve diagnosis and treatment for all patients, benefiting the wider Maui community. This contribution is part of a broader effort to strengthen healthcare infrastructure on the island.

stories.title: Black Hole Blast Shapes Structure: Astronomers trace ‘Treble Clef’ origins; collision revives radio glow
stories.summary: Astronomers have uncovered that the peculiar Treble Clef formation stems from a black hole eruption and the merger of two galaxy clusters. Observations from a variety of telescopes across different wavelengths revealed that the explosive event launched particles, which were later re-energized through the cluster collision. This groundbreaking research enhances our understanding of how cosmic phenomena can fundamentally alter the structures within the universe.

stories.title: 2 Congress workers held for hurling beer bottles at BJP headquarters in Kerala
stories.summary: In a heated political climate in Thiruvananthapuram, two Congress party workers were apprehended for allegedly hurling beer bottles at the BJP headquarters in Kerala. The situation escalated tensions between the rival parties. Following protests and demands from BJP for arrests, the police utilized CCTV footage for a thorough investigation, leading to the identification of the suspects as local Congress members involved in the incident.

stories.title: Teen-Led Wildlife Effort: Georgia student turns Johns Creek into habitat model; certification endures
stories.summary: In a remarkable effort, Malcolm Barnard led a campaign to promote wildlife conservation in Johns Creek, Georgia, achieving the status of a certified habitat community. He focused on educating the community while engaging schools and organizations to adopt wildlife-friendly practices. By 2013, all public schools in the area were recognized by the National Wildlife Federation, fostering a vision of interconnected habitats rather than isolated green spaces.

stories.title: Punjab: AAP to seek cancellation of membership of 2 MLAs after they quit party
Travis Scott's Cactus Jack awards $10,000 fashion scholarships with design training
US man marries dying partner in hospital, court reverses ruling voiding marriage
stories.summary: A Kentucky man who married his partner of nearly 30 years in hospital just 15 days before her death has won an appeal after her daughter challenged the marriage. The daughter questioned her mother's ability to consent and how the marriage licence was obtained. On Friday, the Kentucky Court of Appeals overturned the ruling invalidating the marriage and ordered further examination of the case.

stories.title: '2.5 lakh shops shut, Rs 10,000 crore loss': Delhi traders blame INDIA bloc rally for business disruption
INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan saw creative expression take centre stage as slogans, posters and placards delivered the message
stories.summary: In a momentous gathering, the INDIA bloc's supporters came together at Ramlila Maidan to address pressing political issues. Leaders from multiple parties spoke passionately about the necessity for change, particularly calling for the ousting of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. This event highlighted the importance of unity against perceived electoral injustices, with speakers weaving in historical contexts to bolster their arguments regarding voting rights and electoral fairness.

stories.title: Netanyahu pushing Trump for nuclear strike on Iran? US commentator makes big claim
stories.summary: Tucker Carlson has claimed that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pressuring US President Donald Trump for military action. This action is reportedly a nuclear strike aimed at Pickaxe Mountain in Iran, where nuclear activities are believed to be ongoing. Carlson suggests that the pressure could lead to a decision within days, escalating regional tensions. Diplomatic efforts between the US and Iran continue, though military options remain under consideration.

stories.title: Brooklyn woman attacked, stabbed in neck while jogging on waterfront trail
stories.summary: A 28-year-old woman named Katie Suarez was critically injured during a stabbing incident while jogging. The attack occurred along the Shore Parkway Greenway at around 8 pm local time on October 30. Emergency medical personnel transported Suarez to NYU Langone Hospital-Brooklyn, where she was admitted in critical condition. Police are appealing for information from witnesses to help identify the attacker responsible for the incident.

stories.title: Kiren Rijiju jibes at Congress over INDIA bloc's Ramlila rally crowd photo, calls it 'AI-generated'
US explores route to bring Russian gas back to Europe through Ukraine: Report
stories.summary: The US is exploring a plan to resume Russian natural gas supplies to Europe through Ukraine as part of efforts to secure an energy ceasefire and advance peace talks. The proposal could offer Moscow a financial incentive while providing Kyiv with transit revenue, but faces strong European opposition amid concerns over renewed dependence on Russia.

stories.title: Chinese Airlines Face Losses: Jet fuel surge, weak fares hit Q3 margins; stocks sink this year
stories.summary: China's leading airlines are experiencing significant financial losses amid rising jet fuel prices and weak domestic fare competition. Air China and China Eastern are expected to report their seventh consecutive annual net loss since the pandemic began. China Southern, after a brief return to profitability, is also projected to return to losses. Analysts indicate that the fourth quarter may continue to be challenging due to high operational expenses.

stories.title: J&K: NC Srinagar MP Mehdi to quit party tomorrow to fight it back on 'ideological' turf
Fresh Iran strikes after US midterms? Inside Trump-Netanyahu's 'tough' call
stories.summary: Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held a tough phone call regarding Iran and military strategies. They discussed the possibility of military action after the upcoming US midterm elections. Trump expressed readiness for diplomacy, while Netanyahu urged immediate strikes against Iran. Diplomatic initiatives continue, with the US Vice President sending a letter to Iran's national security chief.

stories.title: Desi Bullet Train closer to reality as squeeze test nears completion
6 Indian trekkers 'ignore weather warnings', get stranded in Nepal
SC upholds HC order allowing I-T to reassess income of ex-CJI's sons
Could Einstein’s equations explain the universe’s expansion?
stories.summary: Researchers from UC Davis have proposed that dark energy may not be necessary to explain the universe's acceleration. They found weak points in the Lambda-cold dark matter model using Einstein's equations. By examining instabilities in Friedmann spacetimes, they suggest alternative explanations for cosmic expansion. Their work raises questions about the Copernican principle in the context of current models. This research could lead to significant shifts in our understanding of cosmology.

stories.title: Scientists have developed a new technology that could make electric car batteries smaller, lighter and longer-lasting, potentially letting drivers travel farther on a single charge without carrying a heavier battery
stories.summary: Scientists from the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology developed a new technology for anode-free batteries. This innovative approach focuses on enhancing lithium deposition to improve battery efficiency and longevity. By restructuring the copper surface for lithium storage, they have addressed issues with dendrite formation. Applying a thin layer of MXene further stabilizes the battery's performance.

stories.title: Introspect on need to improve judiciary responsiveness: CJI
Ranch Easement Preserves Habitat: Winn descendants shield 165 acres; Blanco River recharge gains
stories.summary: Four Winns Ranch in Texas, a treasured historical site, is preserved through dedicated efforts by the Winn family alongside conservation partners. Spanning 165 acres, this land is vital for protecting local wildlife habitats and water sources. Originally acquired by the noteworthy artist James Buchanan Buck Winn Jr., the ranch possesses rich cultural heritage while fostering agricultural and ecotourism activities, aiding the survival of rare birds and endangered aquatic species.

stories.title: Poverty removal not just slogan: PM Modi on World Bank data
12th century Nepalese Manjushri statue sold for about Rs 166 crore in 2026
stories.summary: A 12th-century Manjushri sculpture from Nepal recently sold for around ₹166 crore, illuminating the exceptional artistry of Newar creators from the Kathmandu Valley. This sculpture's intriguing journey through different collections illustrates its cultural significance and uniqueness. Furthermore, the influence of Newar craftsmanship on Buddhist art permeated throughout Tibet and Asia, showcasing Nepal's profound artistic legacy and its vital role in international art history.

stories.title: 1984 survivors, Sikh groups question timing of INDIA bloc rally on Nov 1, seek apology
Gyanesh has to go, PM & Shah next, says Rahul Gandhi at anti-CEC rally
12-year-old London boy raises £13,000 for wildlife, wins Attenborough's praise

A Neanderthal who died 75,000 years ago may have been killed by a wooden spear deliberately aimed at his heart, scientists say, offering rare evidence of targeted violence among our closest ancient relatives
stories.summary: A recent archaeological find in Shanidar Cave revealed a Neanderthal skeleton showing signs of lethal violence, potentially from a wooden spear, suggesting that early human emotional responses might mirror those of today. The evidence hints at both a targeted attack and social care, as the skeleton bore previous injuries. This discovery serves as a window into the dualities of early human life, showcasing their capacity for both violence and compassion.

stories.title: Fake claims, evasion of Rs 5.3 crore land, techie couple in I-T net
Golden Triangle's North East drug trade thrives on barter
£5 ivory chess piece found in family drawer sells for £735,000 after 55 years
stories.summary: An extraordinary Lewis chessman carving has fetched an impressive £735,000 at auction. Hidden away in a drawer for more than 55 years by the family of the dealer, this remarkable figure was revealed as a warder, part of the legendary Lewis Chessmen collection. Originally found in 1831, this collection comprises 93 intricately carved pieces from 1150 to 1200 AD, though the auction leaves four original pieces still unaccounted for.

stories.title: 82-year-old Florida man’s 70-year collection includes a letter from Elizabeth Taylor
In 1913, an Ohio couple sent their eight-month-old son to his grandmother through the postal service
stories.summary: In the year 1913, the US Postal Service unveiled Parcel Post, permitting the mailing of bigger packages. Ingenious parents even started shipping their small children to reduce travel expenses, gaining notoriety when six-year-old May Pierstorff was dispatched 73 miles away. This phenomenon sparked national debate, leading to the ban of child parceling, although similar incidents lingered until 1915, prompting stricter postal regulations to curb such extraordinary practices.

stories.title: Idaho Supreme Court revives condo owners' challenge to property changes approved by 88% vote
stories.summary: The Idaho Supreme Court has revived a legal dispute involving condominium owners challenging changes to property ownership. The contentious amendments were made by the Crystal Beach Condominium Association, affecting owners' shares and rental rules. A previous dismissal by a lower court has been partly overturned, confirming owners' rights to challenge changes impacting their property. Plaintiffs now have their claims for declaratory relief and title slander allowed to proceed.

stories.title: Texas court reopens insurance dispute after landslide destroys two homeowners' backyards
stories.summary: A legal dispute involving home insurance coverage in Travis County has been returned to court for further hearings. The Texas Third Court of Appeal overturned a previous ruling that held the insurer liable for damages. Homeowners claimed that earth movement caused significant damage to their properties, leading to a denial of their insurance claims. The appeals court requires the insurer to demonstrate the cause of the landslide.

stories.title: Florida has allocated $3 million to acquire a 642-acre property along the Suwannee River; officials say ending its current land use could save 159,000 gallons of water daily and reduce nutrient inputs
stories.summary: Florida has allocated $3 million for the acquisition of property along the Suwannee River to reduce water consumption. The Suwannee Sandhill Tract-Drew Property will help conserve approximately 158,800 gallons of water daily. This initiative is part of a larger $100 million investment aimed at various water conservation projects. The acquisition will facilitate the restoration of the land for wildlife habitats and public recreation.

stories.title: Dorothy Dandridge Home Listed: Former Hollywood Hills residence hits $5.499 million; price up nearly 90% from 2014 sale
stories.summary: A stunning Mediterranean-style home in Hollywood Hills, once owned by the iconic actress Dorothy Dandridge, is now on the market for nearly $5.5 million. Covering 4,368 square feet, the residence boasts four luxurious bedrooms and five opulent bathrooms. Dandridge's impactful legacy as a pioneering Black actress echoes through this property, complemented by breathtaking views of Los Angeles. The current owners have thoughtfully renovated it while respecting its historic charm.

stories.title: 'They'll become garbage': Trump says he'll become 'Mr. Veto' if Democrats win midterms
Poland’s top court turns into battleground as Tusk and pro-Trump president clash
Three held over pro-Khalistan graffiti at Delhi Metro stations after Diljit concert
Bhutan dedicates Buddhist stupa to PM Modi; Rijiju calls it ‘huge honour’ for India
stories.summary: In a heartfelt gesture symbolizing the deep-rooted friendship between Bhutan and India, King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck dedicated a stupa to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. This event took place in Gelephu Mindfulness City, where 108 stupas are being raised. Union minister Kiren Rijiju represented India, conveying PM Modi's gratitude. The stupa, numbered 76, represents the strong ties shared by the two nations.

stories.title: CM Mann says opposition parties have nothing to offer Punjab, eyes AAP's return to power in 2027
California doctor Violetta Mailyan gets 15 years for $45 million Medicare fraud and fake Botox claims
stories.summary: California doctor Violetta Mailyan has been sentenced to 15 years in federal prison for defrauding Medicare of more than $45 million through fake Botox injection claims. Prosecutors said she used the money to buy five properties, two Tesla vehicles, including a Cybertruck, and expensive collectibles. She must also pay $32.9 million in restitution.
