UK Labour minister under fire for claiming employers are not ‘working people’
Coal India records highest-ever monthly supplies at 70.3 MT in Oct, up 19%
Beavers set to return to Loch Ness after 500 years, with 15 family groups approved for release.
stories.summary: In an exciting development, wild beavers are about to return to Loch Ness after centuries of absence. The Scottish nature agency NatureScot has sanctioned their release as part of a transformative rewilding project. Over the next three years, conservationists will introduce family groups of beavers to the area’s waterways, focusing on enhancing biodiversity and wildlife habitats, while also implementing strategies to resolve any conflicts with local farmers and landowners.

stories.title: Delaware couple wins disputed backyard land after 20 years, despite neighbours' $30,000 demand
stories.summary: After two decades of contention, a Delaware court officially awarded Joseph W.C. Murray, Jr. and Danielle F. Murray ownership of a long-disputed parcel of land. The case arose when the Preradovic family challenged property lines after purchasing an adjacent lot. Failed negotiations led to litigation, ultimately resulting in the court granting the Murrays the rear yard while their claims to the front areas were rejected.

New airfare rules from next year: No govt intervention except in ‘extraordinary situations’ to prevent spikes
US: Multiple shootings on Halloween leaves 4 dead, 15 injured
‘Nobody can touch this Kumaraswamy’: Union minister dares cops, Karnataka govt over sting row
Florence Pugh's parents put £1.65 million Oxfordshire barn where the Oppenheimer star grew up on sale
stories.summary: Florence Pugh's parents, Clinton Pugh and Deborah Mackin, have listed their Grade II-listed Oxfordshire barn for £1.65 million. The Oppenheimer actress grew up in the 17th-century property, which her parents purchased for £950,000 in 2011. The couple are reportedly considering downsizing as their children have gradually moved out of the family home.

stories.title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine struck Russian defence facility in Rostov
He was homeless twice, now he is a billionaire
stories.summary: John Paul DeJoria overcame homelessness not once, but twice, before establishing thriving ventures in the hair-care and spirits sectors. A dedicated philanthropist, he signed the Giving Pledge to relinquish a minimum of half his fortune. Through the JP’s Peace, Love & Happiness Foundation, he champions diverse initiatives, especially food security. Notably, the Grow Appalachia program has empowered countless families to cultivate their own food.

stories.title: Ming royal descendant turned Buddhist monk painted 12 leaves of birds and flowers, sold for Rs 75 cr
stories.summary: Bada Shanren, originally named Zhu Da, was born into the Ming royal lineage in 1626. Following the Ming dynasty's collapse in 1644, he sought solace in a Buddhist monastery for many years. Later, he embraced secular life as a renowned painter, crafting works that emphasize bold simplicity. His masterpiece, 'Flowers and Birds,' comprised twelve ink-on-paper leaves and recently fetched HK$61.9 million at Christie's Hong Kong auction.

stories.title: Dhak beats on the Thames! British Bengalis take Durga Puja to London's iconic river
stories.summary: British Bengalis marked the fifth annual Durga Parade on the River Thames in London this Saturday. The event featured a decorated idol of Goddess Durga sailing past famous landmarks like Big Ben and the London Eye. Musical performances and dancing were part of the celebrations aboard the boat, showcasing local talent. Bihar Tourism Minister Kedar Prasad Gupta attended and invited Indians to visit Bihar.

stories.title: Former Mossad officer helped Flávio Bolsonaro flee Brazil: Report
International Digi Yatra trials to begin at 7 airports for Indian nationals this year for wider rollout in 2027: Government
US girl starts selling slime to pay for school trip, gets 8 million views in a month
stories.summary: A 14-year-old Indiana girl who started selling slime and squishy toys to fund a school trip to Washington, DC, has attracted over eight million online views. Lexi Long launched her business, Slime & Squish, on October 1 and reached her fundraising goal within nine days. Her business has since gained more than 30,000 social media followers and attracted customers at local events and shops.

stories.title: Tory leader Kemi Badenoch opposes formal British apology for slave trade, calls it a 'navel-gazing distraction'
Pakistan gas crisis: Families return to firewood as LPG prices soar ahead of winter
Pippa Middleton and James Matthews ordered to remove an unauthorised car park at £15.5 million estate
stories.summary: Pippa Middleton, Princess Catherine’s sister, and her husband James Matthews have been ordered to demolish an unauthorised car park at their £15.5 million Barton Court estate. West Berkshire Council ruled against the development after local residents objected to construction without consultation, citing concerns over its impact on the rural character of Kintbury.

stories.title: CBI extradites Mahadev App kingpin Sourabh Chandrakar from Oman
'Vote chori, yes papa': Mamata takes 'Johny Johny' jibe at CEC Gyanesh - video

A Chester Zoo collection of Dracula orchids has been declared nationally important, drawing attention to rare flowers with bizarre, vampire-like appearances that are increasingly threatened in the wild.
stories.summary: Chester Zoo recently received National Plant Collection status for its impressive collection of Dracula orchids. These unique flowers, which mimic various shapes, face threats from habitat loss and illegal collection. Pollination occurs through specific fungi-attracting smells rather than traditional scents. Chester Zoo's horticulturists are dedicated to preserving these rare species amidst growing environmental challenges. Currently, the orchids are not on public display but contribute to plant biodiversity conservation efforts.

stories.title: Florida is planning 4,800 acres of wetlands at the mouth of the Kissimmee River to remove phosphorus before it reaches Lake Okeechobee, decades after engineers began undoing the river's earlier straightening
stories.summary: Florida is planning a 4,800-acre wetland project to filter phosphorus pollution before it reaches Lake Okeechobee. This initiative involves directing stormwater through treatment areas filled with aquatic vegetation. Wetlands help mitigate impacts of excess nutrients and support local ecosystems. The project has been under development since 2019 and will provide flood protection and recreational opportunities. A public meeting is scheduled for November 2026 to discuss construction details.

stories.title: A cupboard buried when Mount Vesuvius destroyed Pompeii in AD 79 has yielded 38 bronze coins and at least 24 tiny childhood charms; archaeologists say the objects reveal glimpses of a family's lost everyday life
stories.summary: Italian archaeologists recently uncovered a sealed wooden cupboard in Pompeii, revealing artifacts from 2,000 years ago. Among the findings were 38 bronze coins, personal care items, and a unique childhood necklace. The discovery adds to our understanding of daily life in ancient Rome, highlighting ordinary people's lives. It is speculated that the residents could not retrieve their belongings during the volcanic eruption.

stories.title: No paneer, no honey, no milky chai? The real challenge of going vegan in India
Trump says Bolsonaro can remain in US indefinitely, calls Brazil election a 'disgrace'
stories.summary: Flavio Bolsonaro left Brazil after his electoral defeat, despite having led in several opinion polls. His departure came after a Brazilian Supreme Court justice ordered his passport revoked. He is also facing two federal money-laundering investigations, while police in Brazil had considered him a flight risk. The comments came as US secretary of state Marco Rubio held talks with Brazilian foreign minister Mauro Vieira.

stories.title: India trying to bring Russia, Ukraine & Europe to the table on 3 fronts: Jaishankar
stories.summary: India's External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar has discussed the protection of civilian shipping with Russia, Ukraine, and European nations. Efforts are being made to restore grain exports through the Black Sea, which have significantly declined. Additionally, the safety of energy infrastructure and fuel shipments is a major concern amid the ongoing conflict. Different interpretations of energy infrastructure complicate discussions on protection measures.

stories.title: Joint List offers to back anti-Netanyahu government: Report
'Super flop rally': BJP says Ramlila Maidan '40% empty', mocks INDIA bloc protest
US midterms: Trump ready with plan to outmaneuver Democrat-controlled Congress
stories.summary: Senior aides, including deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller and budget director Russell Vought, have been working with the White House Counsel's Office since April to identify measures Trump could pursue without congressional approval. These include policies on immigration, tariffs, housing costs and federal spending, according to a White House official and two people familiar with the plans.

stories.title: Veiled marble bust sells for record €1.925 million in Vienna
stories.summary: A marble sculpture of a veiled lady created by Antonio Corradini recently sold for €1.925 million. The auction took place in Vienna and set a new world record for the artist. The sculpture is 60 centimeters tall and showcases intricate craftsmanship that mimics the look of cloth. Bidders from the saleroom and via telephone competed for the artwork, but a telephone bidder ultimately won.

stories.title: Florida court overturns order against couple accused of disrupting weddings at a historic mansion
stories.summary: In a significant ruling, a Florida appeals court has reversed a previous order aimed at curbing a couple's disruptive activities that allegedly disrupted outdoor wedding ceremonies with loud machinery and gunfire. While the immediate limitations have been lifted, the legal battle persists with potential civil nuisance claims still on the table. The appeals court mandates that any new restrictions must strictly adhere to specific evidence criteria.

stories.title: Maya Jama donates £83,500 to charity after losing Celebrity Traitors, matching her potential prize money
stories.summary: Maya Jama, who participated in Celebrity Traitors, donated her potential prize of £83,500 to Action for Children. This charity supports children facing various hardships across the UK, including poverty and abuse. Following her exit in the show's finale, Jama shared her donation on social media platforms. Fellow contestants Sebastian Croft and Romesh Ranganathan each contributed their winnings to different charitable organizations.

stories.title: Rahul's Ramlila 'jalsa' to 'rub salt in wounds' of 1984 Sikh riot victims: Amit Shah
stories.summary: Union home minister Amit Shah said the "jalsa" would reopen painful memories for the victims and their families, accusing the Congress of showing little sensitivity towards the tragedy. Shah made the remarks in Chandigarh while addressing a gathering after inaugurating and laying the foundation stones for development projects worth Rs 258 crore.

stories.title: 'Stay quiet or I'll speak for an hour': Kharge's playful warning to supporters at Ramlila Maidan rally
'After Gyanesh, you are next': Rahul Gandhi says PM Modi, Amit Shah will face justice for 'vote chori'
'Gyanesh, when will you vanish?': Mamata mocks CEC; Akhilesh invokes Haldighati - who said what at INDIA bloc rally
stories.summary: During a rally at Ramlila Maidan on Sunday, senior leaders from the INDIA coalition raised alarms about electoral roll manipulation. They accused the BJP of endangering democracy through the Chief Election Commissioner. Opposition leaders like Rahul Gandhi and Mamata Banerjee demanded Gyanesh Kumar's removal and vowed to continue their campaign against him.

stories.title: Inside UK PM’s Diwali party at his residence; Gita chanting to vegetarian snacks, woman shares
stories.summary: Shanu had the unique opportunity to celebrate Diwali at 10 Downing Street, the iconic residence of the UK Prime Minister. The event was beautifully adorned with traditional decorations, offering a range of vegetarian delicacies. During the gathering, the UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and his wife participated in lighting a ceremonial diya, emphasizing the importance of community contributions and the strengthening of UK-India relations.

stories.title: US couple's fence extends nine feet into neighbour's land, court rules in their favour
stories.summary: A Delaware couple who maintained a fence and garden for more than 20 years won a property dispute after their new neighbours demanded $30,000 to let them keep the land. The neighbours claimed the fence crossed the legal boundary, but an October 30 court ruling recognised the couple's ownership of the entire disputed strip, including an unfenced garden planter, through adverse possession.

stories.title: Safari West's 400-acre wildlife preserve enters a new nonprofit era after decades of conservation
‘Will dig you out from ground, if needed’: Kharge warns CEC Gyanesh Kumar at INDIA bloc rally
New Zealand hospital employee diverted $1 million in patient payments through fraud
‘Did they really have to choose this day?’ BJP targets Congress over INDIA bloc rally on anniversary of 1984 riots
stories.summary: BJP organized a protest march in West Delhi's Hari Nagar demanding an apology from Congress for the 1984 anti-Sikh violence. Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri described the killings as a well-planned genocide rather than a riot. Several leaders participated in the march, expressing concerns over Congress's perceived failure to acknowledge the tragedy. The protest coincided with the opposition's rally addressing electoral irregularities on the same day.

stories.title: ‘Deeply shameful’: Tharoor slams UK over colonialism omission in slavery apology
stories.summary: Responding to British Prime Minister Andy Burnham's remarks in a post on X on Saturday, Shashi Tharoor said he had long maintained that putting a monetary figure on the damage caused by British rule was difficult. He also said Britain had never formally apologised for the destruction and exploitation carried out during its colonial rule.

stories.title: DGCA mandates twin pilot operations from Monday, chopper operators threaten to suspend Char Dam flights
'Why do you challenge democracy?' BJP chief Nitin Nabin accuses Rahul Gandhi of acting on behest of foreign powers
stories.summary: BJP leader Nitin Nabin accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of furthering foreign agendas at a rally in Haryana. Nabin criticized Congress for claiming democracy is at risk only when it loses elections in multiple states. He challenged allegations regarding voter deletion and past election irregularities linked to the party’s leadership. Nabin emphasized the need for governance based on the Constitution rather than dynastic politics.

stories.title: 'Every single shop forcibly shut': Rahul Gandhi targets BJP over Connaught Place closures during mega rally
'Cutting 130m voters unacceptable': Shashi Tharoor targets EC amid INDIA bloc's Ramlila Maidan rally
'Gyanesh Kumar can no longer remain in his position': TMC's Sagarika Ghose demands CEC's removal
stories.summary: Trinamool Congress MP Sagarika Ghose has intensified calls for chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to step down. Uniting the opposition for a common cause, leaders stress the urgency to restore trust in the electoral process. At a rally in Delhi, they highlighted the importance of safeguarding voting rights against authoritarian measures.

stories.title: US river straightened 110 years ago to drain land, now set for restoration to reduce floods
stories.summary: Authorities in Tennessee, US, have acquired 985 acres along the South Fork of the Forked Deer River to reduce flooding and restore natural habitats. The river was straightened in 1916 to drain surrounding land, but the changes contributed to flash floods and erosion. The restoration project aims to reconnect the river with its floodplain and eventually open the area to the public.

stories.title: A new fossil from China may reveal the first amphibian known to have lived entirely at sea; the armoured, 2.4-foot creature lived about 237 million years ago, challenging what scientists know about amphibian evolution
stories.summary: A recent discovery of the fossil Gerrothorax maritimus reveals that some ancient amphibians lived completely in marine environments. Dated to approximately 237 million years ago, this species had a flattened body covered in bony armour. The fossils were found in deep-sea sediments, indicating they lived far from landmasses. Geochemical tests confirmed the strontium isotopes matched those in seawater during the Late Triassic period.

stories.title: 'PM Modi, Amit Shah suffering loss': Sanjay Raut on business concerns of traders ahead of INDIA bloc rally
stories.summary: Sanjay Raut asserted that the rally by the INDIA bloc in Delhi would not disrupt business activities. He emphasized that this event signifies the people's demand for a change in government. Supporters of various political parties began gathering for the rally, which aims to address alleged voter roll tampering. The demonstration is expected to attract significant participation amid security measures by the police.

stories.title: 'India not a banana republic': BJP attacks Rahul Gandhi ahead of INDIA bloc rally
stories.summary: Union minister JP Nadda accused Congress and Rahul Gandhi of attempting to destabilize the government and create unrest. Nadda labeled the opposition's rally at Ramlila Maidan as a calculated conspiracy against democracy and the economy. He outlined a model of politics involving misinformation and provoking protests. The INDIA bloc, however, claims to mobilize for democratic rights concerning alleged electoral roll irregularities.

stories.title: 'No military solutions': EAM Jaishankar reveals PM Modi-Putin talks on Ukraine conflict in Delhi, Bishkek
stories.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar conveyed India's diplomatic commitment regarding the Ukraine conflict during discussions in Atlanta. His talks included priorities such as protecting civilian shipping and restoring crucial grain exports. Jaishankar also emphasized the need for energy security in light of ongoing disruptions. He met with counterparts from Russia, Poland, and South Korea to address bilateral and multilateral issues.

stories.title: Ohio couple splits before marriage, court awards woman $41,466 from house sale
stories.summary: An Ohio man who refused to share money from his house sale with his former partner has lost a court battle. The couple had signed an agreement in 2021 to divide the proceeds if the property was sold. After their breakup, the man argued that the woman had not spent enough on renovations. However, an appeals court upheld the agreement, awarding her $41,466.50.

'Remarkable valour': PM Modi pays tribute to Haryana's heritage on foundation day
stories.summary: Celebrating its 60th Foundation Day on November 1, Haryana showcased its rich heritage and remarkable achievements. Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted the state's vital role in agriculture, sports, and defense. Political leaders such as Amit Shah and Rahul Gandhi commended Haryana's vibrant culture. Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini spoke about the significant progress over the decades.

Texas Supreme Court Blocks Neighbours’ Broad Demand to Inspect Woman’s 14-Acre Homestead
stories.summary: In a significant ruling, the Texas Supreme Court has sided with Pamela Bosco, affirming her right to keep her 14-acre homestead intact. The court denied neighbors’ requests for property inspections due to insufficient evidence of alleged violations. This ruling underscores the importance of legal processes in property disputes and confirms that establishing wrongdoing necessitates proper evidence gathering.

stories.summary: As the INDIA bloc prepares for its rally, the Delhi unit of BJP has launched a poster campaign aimed at opposition leaders. This rally is centered on demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over perceived electoral discrepancies. Many protesters from different states have arrived to raise concerns about the electoral process, particularly regarding Electronic Voting Machines.

stories.title: Atlanta Quad Meeting: Jaishankar seeks action‑oriented agenda; bloc unveils AI, minerals push
stories.summary: During the Quad meeting, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar highlighted the significance of preserving freedom of choice and ensuring secure supply chains. The dialogue centered around addressing non-market practices impacting the Indo-Pacific, without naming specific nations. The ministers unveiled plans to enhance access to artificial intelligence and aid critical minerals recovery while condemning issues like human trafficking and online fraud, pledging to collaboratively combat transnational crimes.

Iran Sees US Letter As Victory: Rezaei hails softer tone as win; Khamenei warns of retaliation
stories.summary: Iran's influential security figure Mohsen Rezaei noted a shift in the US's approach toward Tehran, interpreting this as a triumph for the Iranian populace. In reaction, foreign minister Abbas Araghchi expressed optimism about potential negotiations, agreeing with the analysis of recent communications. Simultaneously, Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei cautioned against threats from the US or Israel, while President Trump maintained that Iran is keen to engage, hinting at an imminent meeting.

stories.title: Trump speaks to Netanyahu as US weighs fresh military strikes on Iran: Report
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump spoke with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu about military options against Iran while considering diplomatic negotiations. Secretary of State Marco Rubio indicated ongoing talks but stressed the importance of addressing security concerns. Israeli officials have doubted Iran's willingness to abandon its nuclear program or halt missile production. The situation remains tense as military preparations are reported by US and Israeli defense forces.

California real-estate executive sentenced for hiding debt while soliciting investments
stories.summary: In a significant ruling, Sanjeev Acharya, the former leader of SiliconSage Builders, will serve 18 months in prison after misleading over 20 investors about the company’s dire financial status from March to October 2020. He obtained over $2.2 million without revealing substantial debt. The court's verdict included a restitution order of over $2.25 million, highlighting the imperative for honesty in real estate investments.

Beat LeBron, Win $100,000: MrBeast faces James, Clark, Haaland; Biles and Liu bring Olympic star power
stories.summary: MrBeast has brought together an extraordinary lineup of sporting superstars for his latest YouTube challenge. The video features LeBron James, Caitlin Clark, Erling Haaland, Simone Biles and Alysa Liu competing against the internet sensation in challenges inspired by their respective sports. The crossover brings together basketball, football and Olympic excellence, giving MrBeast another opportunity to create a spectacle that reaches audiences far beyond his usual YouTube fanbase.

Appeals Court Rejects Nevada Ranchers’ Demand for Faster Wild Horse Removals
stories.summary: On October 29, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit upheld a decision favoring federal officials regarding wild horses. Ranchers Colvin & Son, LLC and Stone Cabin Ranch challenged the Bureau of Land Management's Gather Plans for lacking a specific timetable. The court ruled that the Wild Free Roaming Horses and Burros Act does not require a fixed timeframe for removals.

Canadian publisher with 25 million Facebook followers loses Meta claim over 2020 shutdown
stories.summary: A Canadian online publisher suffered significant losses when Meta permanently removed its Facebook pages in 2020. The publisher, which had millions of followers, argued that this removal violated its business rights. Despite submitting numerous s, many faced rejection for policy violations, which included misleading content. A court upheld Meta's decision, emphasizing its protection under Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act.

Conservationists' bid to bring lynx back to England after 1,300 years rejected by High Court judge
stories.summary: A conservation group aimed to reintroduce Eurasian lynx to Northumberland's Kielder Forest for ecosystem restoration. After submitting proposals for release, Natural England raised legal concerns based on existing wildlife laws. The conservation organization contested the regulator's refusal, arguing the laws should not conflict. However, the High Court ruled that the Dangerous Wild Animals Act still applied post-release.

This funding will kickstart a matching challenge designed to galvanize community support for the Built for Us initiative. Among its goals are major enhancements including the construction of the new Mississauga Hospital and Shah Family Hospital for Women and Children, furthering efforts to elevate regional healthcare facilities.

Launched on October 14, 2026, this initiative had clear content requirements and paid creators $1 for every 1,000 views their videos garnered. With an $8,000 budget that quickly diminished, this campaign showcased fresh possibilities for revenue generation within the realm of content creation, focusing on highlights from a single livestream.
